#1978. Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes

Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

But enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

Ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

Arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

Arsenal play Cesc Fàbregas’s Como on Wednesday, before taking on Manchester City in the Community Shield next weekend. Mikel Arteta’s side then start the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly promoted Coventry City.

Arsenal: Kepa (Meslier 46); White (Julienne 78), Mosquera (Ogunnaike 78), Gabriel (Salmon 60), Calafiori (Hincapié 60); Lewis-Skelly (Vieira 78), Havertz (O’Neill 78), Odegaard (Nwaneri 33); Dowman (Ibrahim 78), Gyokeres (Jesus 78), Tzolis (Martinielli 78). Substitutes: Setford, Nelson, Kabia.Booked: Gabriel.Goals: Nwaneri (54), Gyokeres (69 pen).Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson (Yamamoto 91), Inácio (Prates 59), Bensebaini (Reggiani 78), Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha (Guirassy 60), Mane; Karetsas (Chukwuemeka 46), Beier (Sabitzer 59), Silva (Albert 59). Substitutes: Drewes, Lerema, Kabar, Riedl.Goals: Inácio (7), Karetsas (29), Gadou (58).

Nwaneri steps up with the chance to win the shootout and does so with aplomb, sending Meyer the wrong way, and Arsenal win the shootout 5-4.

The former Chelsea man receives some boos as he steps up but calmly slots home to keep Dortmund’s hopes alive.

Meyer goes the right way but there is far too much power on this penalty from Martinelli. Meyer had no chance of saving that one.

We have the first penalty miss of this shootout as Meslier guesses the right way and saves what was a pretty poor penalty from Albert. Advantage Arsenal.

A few stutters in the run-up but Hincapie slots home into the bottom left corner, with Meyer going the wrong way.

He came on right at the end of the game to take a penalty and rewards the decision from his manager to do so as he lifts it over Meslier diving to his left.

Another penalty scored in the left corner. Meyer again guesses the right way but cannot prevent Vieira.

There is a bit of a stutter in the run-up as Reggiani stares down Meslier and sends the Arsenal keeper the wrong way, finding the same corner as Sabitzer and Jesus.

Meyer in the Dortmund goal guesses the right way but Jesus lifts it over him with a quality penalty.

Meslier takes an age to get ready but Sabitzer does not care, sending the Arsenal keeper the wrong way and emphatically finding the left corner.

Right, we are ready for penalties. Dortmund will take first, with Sabitzer to take their opening penalty up against Meslier.

Arsenal have the ball in the net in the final few seconds and think they have a very late equaliser but Martinelli’s effort is ruled out for an offside. Meyer will be a relieved man in the Dortmund goal as he allowed Martinelli’s shot to go through him.

The final whistle is then blown and Dortmund have beaten Arsenal 3-2 to take the Emirates Cup.

It is perhaps not a massive surprise but the game has lost some flow with all the changes both sides have made during this second half.

There is set to be a penalty shootout at the end of this one, no matter what the final result is.

Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas is in attendance, with his Como side taking on Arsenal here on Wednesday.

Jude Bellingham is supporting his younger brother Jobe today at the Emirates:

With just under 15 minutes to go at the Emirates, Arsenal are going to make a number of changes. Plenty of youngsters are entering the fray as are a few experienced players like Jesus and Martinelli.

The Swede sends Meyer the wrong way and slots into the bottom right corner. It is now 3-2 and this game is not over with 20 minutes to go.

Tzolis goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area and referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot. He was caught inside the box and there did not appear to be too many complaints from the visitors.

Nwaneri comes close to getting his second goal of the half. Tzolis rolls it across the face of the penalty area to Nwaneri, who hits it first time and forces Meyer into a good save to his right, pushing it onto the post.

In the aftermath of that Dortmund goal, there are a raft of changes for both sides. Arsenal have brought on Salmon and Hincapie for Calafiori and Gabriel.

Dortmund have brought on the experience of the likes of Sabitzer and Guirassy.

Arsenal had some problems from corners the other day against Betis and they concede minutes after getting a goal back. Arsenal fail to deal with a corner from the right and the ball ends up with Gadou at the back post. Gadou takes one touch before finding the net, despite the best efforts of numerous Arsenal defenders on the line.

Should Inacio have gone down? The young Italian is played in behind the Arsenal defence and has Calafiori all over his back. Inacio ends up losing possession on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area but had he gone down Calafiori could have been in trouble.

Mikel Arteta’s side reduce Dortmund’s lead to just the one goal. Tzolis cuts it back from the left side of the box and picks out Nwaneri eight yards out from goal in the centre of the box. Nwaneri makes no mistake, smashing home and Arsenal are back in this game.

That is good defending from Nwaneri. Just as Chukwuemeka was lining up a shot just outside the box, Nwaneri tracks back and steals it off Chukwuemeka.

White is found on the right side of the box but is denied by Meyer in the Dortmund goal. The subsequent corner comes to nothing.

Dortmund are not far off scoring their third a couple of minutes into this second half. The ball is rolled into the feet of Nmecha outside the box. The German midfielder, who scored a stunner for his country against Curacao at the World Cup, nearly picks out the top corner but it goes just over Meslier’s bar.

Dortmund have brought on former Chelsea and Aston Villa man Chukwuemeka on at the break. Arsenal have made an alteration at the break with Meslier replacing Kepa in goal.

During half-time at the Emirates, the official song of the 2026 Fifa World Cup Dai Dai by Shakira and Burna Boy is being belted out over the tannoy. The World Cup final was exactly three weeks ago today, with three of Arsenal’s players in Spain’s winning squad; David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi.

Konstantinos Karetsas has arrived. 🇬🇷🇬🇷🇬🇷 pic.twitter.com/nI4A7KPT4o

The first half in north London is brought to an end and it is the visitors Borussia Dortmund who lead 2-0 at the break courtesy of goals from Inacio and Karetsas.

Gabriel is into the book. He is in possession but his touch allows the ball to slightly get away from him. He then slides in to try and retain possession and catches Karetsas.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Nmecha eyes up a repeat of Dortmund’s first goal as he tries to find the run of Inacio into the Arsenal box but this time they cannot quite link up.

After Gyokeres was fouled, Arsenal have a free-kick inside the Dortmund half. Tzolis clips it in and picks out Havertz in space inside the Dortmund box but the German is a fair way out from goal and his header is easily saved by Meyer.

Arsenal want a penalty but the appeals are turned down. It all stems from good work defensively from Tzolis, who drives forward from the edge of his own box and then finds Gyokeres out to his left. Tzolis continues his run into the Dortmund half and is found. Tzolis then finds Gyokeres again, who goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area after a challenge from Gadou but the Swedish striker went down far too easily and that is never a penalty.

Dowman does brilliantly down Arsenal’s right to get past Beier but then goes down just before the byline. Referee Chris Kavanagh blows his whistle and Beier cannot believe it. Replays show that Dowman threw himself to the ground and it was a dive.

Tzolis takes the free-kick and delivers it to the far post, where Gabriel meets it but his powerful header goes over the bar. The Brazilian probably should have scored.

Mikel Arteta has made a change as Nwaneri has replaced Odegaard, who has only recently returned to training after the World Cup.

With it being a warm day in north London, we have a water break. Hopefully they do not catch on after the World Cup. Mikel Arteta is looking pretty animated talking to his side.

What a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

Odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

Arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

A dangerous cross from the left comes all the way to Svensson at the back post but he lacked conviction with his header and it goes wide. Perhaps he should be hitting the target.

Down at the other end Arsenal have a headed chance of their own. Havertz clips in a cross from the left and picks out Gyokeres. The Swede is a fair way out from goal and his header goes wide.

Should Havertz have done better with this opportunity? The German is played in down the right channel and has Gyokeres calling for the cross in space in the centre of the box. Havertz tries to find him but Meyer is out to smother it. Had Havertz found Gyokeres, it would likely have been a simple tap-in for the Swede.

Odegaard appears to be through one-on-one but then goes down just outside the Dortmund box. Mane pleads his innocence but referee Chris Kavanagh does not agree, giving a free-kick. If this was a competitive game, Mane would potentially have been sent off.

Gyokeres will take and opts for power over accuracy. It is safe to say his effort is terrible, blazing over the bar and missing the target by some margin.

Calafiori trips Bellingham as Dortmund attempted to counter. If this was a competitive fixture, Calafiori likely would have been booked for that foul.

Bellingham and Havertz are involved in quite the collision. Both players go for the header and Havertz just gets to it first. Havertz is awarded the foul and is ok.

The German side take the lead inside the opening seven minutes. Nmecha slides a lovely pass through the Arsenal defensive line to pick out the run of Inacio into the Arsenal penalty area. It is a clinical finish from Inacio, who slides his effort into the far corner,

Dortmund’s first proper foray forward causes Arsenal issues and Tzolis is forced to put it behind for Dortmund’s first corner of the game. The inswinger though to the front post is poor and Gyokeres easily heads away from danger.

Gyokeres wins Arsenal their first corner of the game out on the right. Odegaard’s delivery into the near post causes problems for Dortmund and forces Dortmund keeper Meyer to tip over his own bar for another Arsenal corner. Meyer this time punches Odegaard’s delivery away and Dortmund clear their lines.

Moments after Bruno Guimaraes’ unveiling, both sides now emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates.

Just before the two sides emerge the tunnel, there is a special guest who comes out first in the form of Bruno Guimaraes. Chants of “Bruno! Bruno!” ring around the Emirates as the Arsenal fans get their first glimpse of him in an Arsenal shirt, although the Brazilian is not involved today.

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Odegaard; Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis.Substitutes: Meslier, Setford, Hincapie, Jesus, Martinielli, Vieira, Nwaneri, Nelson, Ibrahim, Kabia, Ogunnaike, Julienne, O’Neill, Salmon.

Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson, Inacio, Bensebaini, Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha, Mane; Karetsas, Beier, Silva.Substitutes: Drewes, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Sabitzer, Lerema, Prates, Albert, Kabar, Yamamoto, Reggiani, Riedl.

Reports are that Jobe’s older brother Jude is at the Emirates today, not that Arsenal fans should think that Jude is swapping Real Madrid for the red half of north London.

Arsenal took the Premier League trophy with them to Dublin on Wednesday night and it is on show today at the Emirates. They kick off the defence of their crown on opening night against newly-promoted Coventry is just under two weeks.

Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀

When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

Yesterday Arsenal announced the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:

“I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

August 1- Girona 1 Arsenal 4August 5-  Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3Today- Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund (Emirates Cup)August 12- Arsenal vs ComoAugust 16- Arsenal vs Manchester City (Community Shield)

🚨 STARTING XI VS ARSENAL 🚨 pic.twitter.com/Wk6QPOGDnW

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️🧱 Gabriel at the back©️ Odegaard skippers the side😤 Gyokeres leads the line More pre-season minutes in the tank - let's do this, Gunners ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/FQwOjCDAje

Checking in for the Emirates Cup 🛬 pic.twitter.com/mQ1eAESKHY

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

#1973. Official: Shareholders’ Meeting approves AC Milan financial statements including €24m net loss

Not long before the unveiling of the new stadium project, the AC Milan Shareholders’ Meeting took place to approve the accounts for 2025-26.

The club’s official website confirmed that the Shareholders approved the financial statements for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026. The Group closed the 2025-26 fiscal year with revenue of €464.6m and a net loss of approximately €24m.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The solid and diversified business model built over recent years, supported by operational excellence and cost control, enabled AC Milan to absorb a significant portion of the financial impact of its absence from European competitions.

Commercial performance remained strong, with sponsorship revenue exceeding €100m and average attendance surpassing 72,000 fans per match, the highest in Serie A for the second consecutive season.

They also add that Milan are ‘entering a new phase of investment’, supported by RedBird’s long-term commitment and owner-operator approach, combining capital, operational expertise and execution capabilities to drive the Club’s growth and competitiveness.

Paolo Scaroni, Chairman of the Board of AC Milan: “These results demonstrate the resilience of our business model in a challenging season. Gerry Cardinale’s leadership, combined with RedBird’s long-term investment and operational expertise, has driven the Club’s progress and continues to shape its future, with sporting competitiveness remaining the key priority.

“The appointment of Massimo Calvelli as CEO reflects this direction. And the new stadium, whose design we will unveil today, demonstrates the value of this approach: a transformative investment for AC Milan, our fans, the city of Milan and Italian football.”

One of the key aspects RedBird are continuing to work on is the new stadium project, which as mentioned was revealed last night. Following the acquisition of the San Siro area in November 2025, it is the next step towards unlocking more revenue opportunities.

For the second consecutive year, Milan also published its Sustainability Report alongside its financial statements. Through Fondazione Milan, the Club harnesses the power of football as a catalyst for positive social change, promoting education, inclusion and wellbeing.

#1972. Chelsea could sell £70m Fofana and Malo Gusto in 2027

By Naim Beneddra | 01 Nov 2026 10:46

Chelsea are reportedly considering making two high-profile defenders available for transfer in 2027, with doubts growing over their ability to meet Xabi Alonso's long-term requirements.

The Blues could be prepared to part ways with Wesley Fofana, who joined from Leicester City for approximately £70m in 2022, while fellow French international Malo Gusto is also facing an uncertain future at Stamford Bridge.

According to Flashscore journalist Dean Jones, Chelsea's hierarchy are becoming increasingly concerned about the reliability of their defensive options and are assessing potential changes to the squad ahead of next year's transfer windows.

Both players came under scrutiny following Wednesday's EFL Cup elimination against Liverpool, when Fofana missed the decisive penalty in a 6-5 shootout defeat after a 1-1 draw.

However, the concerns reportedly extend beyond that result, with Chelsea evaluating whether the pair can provide the consistency required to compete at the highest level.

Fofana's position has become particularly uncertain despite the substantial investment Chelsea made to secure his signature four years ago.

The former Leicester defender arrived at Stamford Bridge as one of the most expensive centre-backs in Premier League history, but recurring injuries have prevented him from establishing himself as a consistently available first-team player.

His lengthy absences have disrupted his development and made it difficult for Chelsea to build a settled defensive partnership around him.

According to Jones, the Blues are now assessing whether Fofana can fulfil the role originally envisaged for him, with the 25-year-old at risk of losing his place in the club's plans during 2027.

The Frenchman's performance against Liverpool reportedly reinforced existing concerns, particularly after he missed the penalty that ended Chelsea's involvement in the competition.

Nevertheless, his recent involvement under Alonso offers a more complicated picture.

Having gone without an appearance for much of October, Fofana returned to the starting lineup at Anfield before retaining his place against Manchester United on Saturday.

Although he struggled during a first half in which United created several promising opportunities, the defender subsequently played an important role in Chelsea's 2-0 victory.

Lisandro Martinez was dismissed after catching Fofana with his arm inside the penalty area, allowing Cole Palmer to convert the resulting spot kick and double Chelsea's lead.

His involvement in that decisive incident underlined that he remains part of Alonso's immediate plans, even as questions persist over his longer-term future.

Fofana is contracted to Chelsea until June 2029, meaning any prospective departure would require an agreement between the club, the player and an interested suitor.

His injury record and substantial original transfer fee could also complicate Chelsea's attempts to secure a satisfactory deal.

Fofana is not the only French defender whose position has come under review.

Gusto, who joined Chelsea from Lyon in January 2023, is reportedly another player the club could consider moving on as part of a wider defensive overhaul.

The Blues have already begun exploring potential replacements at right-back, according to an earlier Flashscore report, with scouts assessing options across Europe.

The 23-year-old remains under contract until 2030, but his reduced involvement this season has raised questions about his place in Alonso's preferred system.

Marco Palestra has emerged as a competing option on the right, making Gusto's prospects of securing consistent playing time increasingly uncertain.

Chelsea reportedly valued the former Lyon defender at around €80m during the summer, although that figure is now being reassessed.

Interest has previously been attributed to Manchester City, Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich, Atletico Madrid, Liverpool and Tottenham Hotspur, but there is no indication that Chelsea have received a formal offer.

Gusto was introduced as a late substitute against Manchester United, highlighting his continued involvement despite speculation surrounding his future.

The possibility of losing both French defenders would represent a significant change in Chelsea's squad planning, particularly given their ages and the long-term contracts awarded to them.

However, no final decision has been announced, and Flashscore's reporting does not establish that either player will necessarily leave during the January window.

Chelsea's willingness to consider offers may ultimately depend on the availability of suitable replacements and whether interested clubs can meet their financial expectations.

#1970. Rangers boss Derek McInnes brands Falkirk win over Celtic 'not really a shock'

Rangers manager Derek McInnes has stated Falkirk's win over Celtic was "not really a shock".

"Falkirk are capable of that, and they did that a couple of times last season as well."

McInnes then backed his former club Hearts to be in the title hunt this season.

He said: "I do think Hearts will be title contenders again with the investment and size of squad they have got and the level of player they have got.

"I think Hearts will be up there again. It will be more of a surprise if they're not."

Niclas Füllkrug has reflected on his short time with AC Milan, admitting he would have liked to have made more of a mark.

Füllkrug is enjoying a stellar start to the season with Werder Bremen, with 11 goals in nine games across the Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal, the last of which came on Tuesday with a brace in the cup against his former team, Borussia Dortmund.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The second goal was one of the finest of his career and these staggering numbers put him ahead of some of the great strikers of recent years, including Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane who has 10 goals for Bayern Munich this season.

It has been a fruitful return to Bremen so far, and as a result the German striker is once again being talked about a possible return to the national team under Jurgen Klopp. He spoke to MilanNews journalist Alessandro Schiavone.

Eleven goals already, and we’re not even in November, after your return to Werder Bremen. Could you have scored more with Milan?

“Yes, of course. It’s a new season now, but I could have scored a few more goals and provided a few more assists at AC Milan, too.

“It was a bit of an unlucky period, and not the most effective in terms of goalscoring, but I still think I put in several good performances. It was a truly, truly wonderful time, and I still have great affection for AC Milan.”

Your winning goal against Lecce was a typical Füllkrug goal. What’s it like scoring at San Siro? Is it comparable to scoring at Signal Iduna Park in Dortmund?

“Yes, it’s quite similar to Dortmund. In Dortmund it’s a little different, there are still a few more people. But San Siro is amazing! It’s a historic stadium, special and truly, truly wonderful.”

“I still follow AC Milan, I watch the games, and I’m still in touch with some of the players and the lads. I wish them all the best. My best friend at AC Milan? Ardon Jashari.”

Milan could have kept you for just €5m, but was it the club that told you they didn’t want to keep you, or did you find out through the media?

“I can’t say anything about that… absolutely nothing (smiles).”

And what about the Champions League failure?

“I’d rather not say anything about that, too, because I don’t know. And then it would be too much…”

AC Milan are having an up-and-down season. Are you still following them?

“When I can, I watch the games. I still have some friends there I’m in touch with. I wish AC Milan all the best.”

#1964. Martin O'Neill sent health plea from worried Rangers hero as Celtic rivalry parked

Rangers icon Ally McCoist has revealed he would hate to see Celtic boss Martin O'Neill suffer and reckons the veteran manager has earned the right to walk away on his own terms.

The Ibrox hero, who has long admired O'Neill despite their rivalry, admits his biggest concern is the toll management can take on the 74-year-old's health. While McCoist hopes close friend Derek McInnes can guide Rangers to title glory this season, he stressed he would take no pleasure in seeing O'Neill pushed out of Parkhead or forced to continue beyond the point where the job remains enjoyable.

The former Rangers striker believes O'Neill's decades of service to the game, and his achievements at Celtic, mean he deserves the respect to decide for himself when the time is right to step aside.

Speaking to talkSPORT Bet Online Casino, the 64-year-old said: "I think Martin has absolutely earned the right and deserves the respect to stay for as long as he feels right. I really do.

"I would hate Martin to overstay his time at Celtic, first and foremost for his health.

Read more: Rangers boss Derek McInnes brands Falkirk win over Celtic 'not really a shock'

"That's the most important thing, because I've always gotten on really well with Martin. Obviously I want Rangers to win the league 100 per cent, but Martin has more than earned the right to see things out for as long as he wants at Celtic, and that should be the case."

McCoist also concedes Europe's demands could yet play a significant role in the title race.

"I don't think for a minute Martin will say they're prioritising, but their level of performance in Europe has been extremely disappointing. I know they created one or two chances against Benfica, but Benfica were three-nil up and done.

"The performances in Europe have been really disappointing from Martin's point of view.

"I don't have any doubt that it could work in Rangers' favour not having those Thursday European games. Celtic are not allowed, same as Rangers, to get into any game other than expecting to win, particularly at home, whether domestic or European, the fans won't allow it.

"So there is added pressure on Celtic, of course there is. But Martin will be delighted with their league form. I noticed a lovely quote from him this morning where he said it was a fantastic result at the weekend, but if they get beaten on Thursday there'll be another crisis!

#1963. Barcelona vs. Aston Villa: Head-to-head record and past meetings before Champions League battle

By Ben Knapton | 01 Nov 2026 11:24

Two of the fiercest attacking forces the Champions League has to offer collide at Camp Nou on Tuesday, when Barcelona and Aston Villa meet on matchday four of the 2026-27 league phase.

La Blaugrana have some continental wrongs to right after losing 4-2 to holders Paris Saint-Germain on matchday three, a result that ended their perfect start to the current tournament.

On the other hand, Aston Villa are seeking a fourth win from four matches in the UCL, having already bested Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking FK while scoring 12 goals along the way.

Here, Sports Mole takes an in-depth look at the head-to-head record and previous meetings between the two sides.

Barcelona and Aston Villa never met in the 21st century before the 2026-27 Champions League, which will also mark their first head-to-head in the top tier of European football.

However, the two former continental champions did lock horns four times in the 20th century, and Barcelona came out on top in two of those clashes, while losing one and playing out one draw.

That solitary stalemate came in the two teams' inaugural meeting in the 1977-78 UEFA Cup quarter-finals, as Villa pulled off an astonishing comeback from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 in the first leg at Villa Park.

Johan Cruyff put Barcelona ahead in the 20th minute before Rafael Zuviria's 80th-minute effort, but Ken McNaught's 87th-minute response and John Deehan's 89th-minute equaliser rescued an unlikely draw for the Lions.

Barca were not to be denied, though, as Rinus Michels's men triumphed 2-1 in the second leg at Camp Nou two weeks later, fighting back from 1-0 down to prevail before losing to PSV Eindhoven in the semi-finals.

Villa and Barcelona would reunite five years later in the 1982 UEFA Super Cup - contested over two legs in January 1983 - the Lions entering as European Cup holders and the Blaugrana as European Cup Winners' Cup champions.

The first leg - held at Camp Nou - ended 1-0 in favour of Barcelona, but Aston Villa turned the tide in chaotic circumstances in the second leg at Villa Park, winning 3-0 after extra time for a 3-1 aggregate triumph.

The second leg ended 10v9, as Villa received one red card and Barcelona two, but the Lions ultimately clinched their last European trophy for 44 years before Unai Emery masterminded their run to Europa League glory in 2025-26.

Jan 26, 1983: Aston Villa 3-0 Barcelona (Super Cup)

Jan 19, 1983: Barcelona 1-0 Aston Villa (Super Cup)

Mar 15, 1978: Barcelona 2-1 Aston Villa (UEFA Cup)

Mar 01, 1978: Aston Villa 2-2 Barcelona (UEFA Cup)

#1962. GdS: ‘Crazy desire’ – why Amorim hopes Cisse can become the derby hero

Alphadjo Cisse has had an electric start to the season so far with AC Milan, and Ruben Amorim could turn to him in the hopes of derby heroics.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) recall that during Wednesday’s defeat to Bologna at San Siro, the crowd chanted Cisse’s name louder than any other Milan player’s, even before a game that truly cemented his status as the player of the moment.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He will remain the team’s top scorer for the time being, unless Adrien Rabiot nets a hat-trick in the derby, or Goncalo Ramos or Diego Moreira pull off a four-goal haul. As it stands, Cisse leads the way with seven goals, followed by Adrien with four.

Cisse’s goals are fairly evenly split: four in the league and three in the Europa League. In Serie A, he reached this tally in 338 minutes of play, while in Salzburg, he needed just 207 minutes to record his first Rossoneri hat-trick.

His scoring rate is exceptionally high: one goal every 84.5 minutes in the league, a figure that improves to one every 69 minutes in international competition. And to those who might argue that many of these goals came from lucky, close-range touches, others are not scoring goals like that.

On his own, he has accounted for a third of the 21 total goals scored by Ruben Amorim’s side, and has more than double the three scored by Gonçalo Ramos, the club’s major summer signing.

Cisse was signed last winter and subsequently remained out on loan to Catanzaro. His season there ended in February due to an injury, yet Milan never left his side. If anything, credit goes to Amorim for placing his trust in him and integrating him from the very start, a gesture Cissé has repaid it.

He scored a goal on his debut against Torino, another against Juventus, and a brace against Bologna this past Wednesday. His three Europa League goals, meanwhile, all came on the same night in Salzburg.

Setting aside his international debut against Benfica – a match played by a makeshift side due to squad rotation – Alpha has not put a foot wrong in any game. Not even in the match against Lazio, a result that looks better in hindsight, given the Biancocelesti’s form.

Furthermore, it would be harsh to judge his performance as a centre-forward away at Bournemouth too negatively, as that display was clearly compromised by Maignan’s sending-off and the fact that the team fell behind by two goals, both from penalties.

Removing a player who is in a goal-scoring vein and fuelled by such enthusiasm could prove counter-productive, though the derby will bring more options, as both Rabiot and Moreira (who could slot into Cisse’s area of ​​the pitch) have been working toward their recovery since yesterday.

Two nights ago, Cisse operated as a number 10 – a link between the midfield and the penalty area – where he truly shone. While it’s true that Rabiot brings more experience to that central role, it’s equally possible that Adrien could drop back into the midfield alongside Modrić,.

Similarly, Cisse could start on the left, where he will face renewed competition from Moreira. Yet, Alpha possesses impressive stats, carried with the effortless grace of a young talent, one who now deserves the spotlight of the derby.

But, from what I’ve seen so far of Ramos – no, he simply does not have the technique to score in a league with top class defenses and I strongly suspect he is never going to score much in Serie A.. In the Portugal league, yes, Ramos scored a lot of goals. In Ligue 1 no. In Serie A, definitely no. Just like Gimenez, who was able to score in the defense optional Eredivisie, but couldn’t make the jump to Serie A.

And, now Amorim is running him into the ground – the last two matches he looked like a cripple unable to get free of the defender marking him.

#1961. Harry Kane makes admission after Ballon d'Or nightmare

By Naim Beneddra | 01 Nov 2026 11:42

Harry Kane has admitted that he could have played for another hour without scoring after enduring a frustrating first appearance since winning the 2026 Ballon d'Or.

The England captain missed a penalty and failed to register a single shot on target as Bayern Munich were held to a dramatic 2-2 draw by Borussia Dortmund at the Allianz Arena on Saturday evening.

It was an unexpected outcome to a remarkable week for the 33-year-old, who had been presented with football's most prestigious individual award in London on Monday, becoming the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001.

Kane received a special tribute from Bayern before kick-off, entering the pitch separately from his teammates and displaying the trophy alongside his family in front of 75,000 supporters.

However, the celebrations gave way to an unusually difficult evening in front of goal, prompting the former Tottenham Hotspur striker to deliver a candid assessment of his performance.

Already a club legend! ❤️? Harry Kane with a few words to the fans ?❤ https://t.co/K85U3spcz4

Speaking to reporters after the Klassiker, Kane acknowledged that he had fallen below his usual standards, although he was equally disappointed with Bayern's collective display.

"Today probably wasn't my best performance or the team's best performance, but that's just life," the England international said, as quoted by AFP.

"That's just part of being a striker, a footballer.

"I probably could have been out there for another hour today and the ball wouldn't have gone in the back of the net."

Kane's frustration was understandable given the opportunities he had to add another goal to his impressive tally.

With Bayern leading 1-0 early in the second half, he stepped up to take a penalty after Felix Nmecha was penalised for handball.

The striker struck his effort against the crossbar, squandering a chance to double the hosts' advantage.

According to Opta, it was only the second penalty Kane had failed to convert in 27 Bundesliga attempts, with his previous miss coming against Wolfsburg in May.

His difficulties continued when a misplaced pass was intercepted by Nico Schlotterbeck during the move that ended with Serhou Guirassy bringing Dortmund level.

Kane subsequently struck the woodwork again, although that effort would not have counted because of an offside decision.

Perhaps the most revealing statistic was his overall shooting record: six attempts, none of which hit the target.

Opta noted that only one player had registered more shots without testing the goalkeeper in a Bundesliga game this season.

Yet Kane still made an important contribution, heading Joshua Kimmich's cross back across goal for Dayot Upamecano to restore Bayern's lead.

That assist took his tally to 10 direct goal involvements in eight league appearances this season, comprising four goals and six assists.

The figures provide some perspective on an evening that was disappointing by the standards of the newly crowned Ballon d'Or winner, rather than evidence of a prolonged loss of form.

Kane, who scored 73 goals for club and country last season, was reluctant to dwell on the setback.

"You have to take it on the chin sometimes. It was an incredible week, but the focus for sure now is on the games ahead," he added.

Kane's determination to move forward comes at an important moment for Bayern, whose demanding fixture schedule has been complicated by fresh injury concerns.

Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise were all forced off during Saturday's draw, leaving the German champions facing uncertainty over several attacking options.

Those setbacks add to the absences of Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz, potentially increasing Bayern's dependence on their leading striker.

The club are also temporarily without head coach Vincent Kompany on the touchline as he continues his recovery from a health problem, with assistant Aaron Danks overseeing the team against Dortmund.

Bayern face another significant examination on Tuesday, November 3, when they travel to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

Kane has already indicated that he expects to be available for the encounter, while stressing that the squad will need to cope with a demanding run of fixtures.

"For Atletico, I'll be ready to go. It's an important game for us," he told Bulinews.

"We're going to a really tough place away from home so we're going to need everyone to step up."

Bayern remain unbeaten in the Bundesliga after eight matches, although Dortmund's late equaliser ensured that the title rivals stayed level on 18 points, with the Bavarians ahead on goal difference.

For Kane, the immediate challenge is to rediscover the finishing touch that helped him claim the Ballon d'Or.

His performance against Dortmund was a reminder that even Europe's most prolific forwards can experience difficult afternoons, but the England captain will have an early opportunity to respond in Madrid.

#1960. Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

Among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of new arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

Everton kick-off their new season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the new season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

Alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

More defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

That goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

Newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

Thierno Barry’s performance has been a positive for Everton, could he nail down the No 9 role this season? It has been a problem position for several seasons now. Barry is tripped and Everton have a free-kick.

Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

Then an amusing moment: great cheers from the crowd as David Moyes heads a Hornicek clearance back down the line. He didn’t fancy the cushioned first touch off his instep, then.

Everton have played some quick one and two-touch football around the box in this game, and another move ends with George shooting over the bar. Everton are making their first change: Patterson off, replaced by Rohl.

The game is still finding its shape again after all those Newcastle changes, but Murphy did force a sharp save from Travers with a low shot from a tight angle.

He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

The players on for Newcastle are: Woltemade, Murphy, Willock, Barnes, Ramsey, Johnson, Steur, Pivas, Miley and Charlton.

It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

Newcastle made a bright start, but as the half progressed there is no doubt that Everton have been the more dangerous attacking force and the scoreline reflects that. Here come the changes...

Everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

Thierno Barry almost finds the run of Hackney into the Newcastle penalty, and after a sluggish start, Everton have played some slick football in the attacking third.

A sign of some Newcastle frustration there was Wissa kicks Tyrique George across the shins. A bit naughty that, may even have been worthy of VAR attention in a Premier League game.

The Senegalese sends Hornicek the wrong way and finds the corner. No chance it was a penalty in the first place though, thankfully this is not a competitive game.

This is very soft, there was not much of a challenge by Joelinton on Dewsbury-Hall, but the Everton midfielder goes down in the box and is awarded the penalty.

It really should be 2-0 to Everton, a high-class moving down their left with Armstrong dinking a pass to Barry. He squared to Ndiaye who was free as a bird in the middle, but his shot was too close to Hornicek.

Joelinton runs down a blind alley before lumping a pass out for an Everton throw, and then the Newcastle man fouls Barry. The big Brazilian still finding his legs and getting up to speed.

A moment to forget for both Newcastle centre-backs. Thiaw was bumped and unbalance by Barry, before Botman steps out of defence and kicks fresh air against the Everton forward. Great recovery from Lewis Hall, but the ball breaks for Armstrong, who feeds Barry and he finishes across Hornicek.

Ndiaye has had a quiet start to the game for Everton, but his jinking qualities were on display there to beat a couple of Newcastle defenders. Everton lose the ball in midfield, and Tarkowski makes a superb last-ditch tackle to deny Osula.

Half-hearted appeals for a penalty from Wissa, but Hayden Hackney did not do much wrong. Looks like we will be spared a first-half hydration break, despite it being a sultry evening.

Osula skips through a couple of challenges at the edge of the area but fails to pick a pass in the box. Bazoumana Touré has looked lively for Newcastle on their left flank, and Bamba has done well for them in midfield.

Everton shake themselves into life as an attacking force. Cracking cross from Patterson into the box and Dewsbury-Hall’s run had gone untracked, but he was just stretching and could not generate enough power to beat Hornicek.

Good save from Travers to deny Elanga, but it was Mykolenko who made a hash of things in the box. The left back simply fell over the ball under no pressure. Newcastle the sharper of the two teams so far.

Joelinton feeds Bamba down the left wing for Newcastle who delivers a cross into the penalty area. Keane can only direct his defensive header back towards the penalty spot, but Wissa volleyed over with a first-time hit. Decent chance.

Thierno Barry makes it stick and proves a strong outlet for Everton. Botman brings him down at the expense of a free-kick just beyond the halfway line. Then Wissa drives into the penalty area for Newcastle after a one-two but he fouls Patterson.

Newcastle, playing in their lilac away kit, are the team trying to take the initiative with the ball, but Everton are quite happy staying compact and absorbing pressure. Elanga’s corner delivery is promising, but Osula does not connect cleanly at the back post.

Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

Wissa peels behind Everton’s defence inside the opening 90 seconds but he cannot lift the ball over Travers.

Bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

We know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

Big Dunc and Moyes catch up pre-match! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/Jh4APHOZvX

A word that keeps being used about Jaissle is “special”. Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Joelinton, Bamba; Elanga, Wissa, Toure; Osula

Newcastle subs: Gillespie, Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Johnson, M Miley, Finneran, Ramsey, Steur, Willock, J Murphy, Barnes, Neave, Woltemade

Your Mags at Murrayfield! ✊ pic.twitter.com/rDXpn0MqCg

Everton XI: Travers; Patterson, Tarkowski, Keane, Mykolenko; Hackney, Deswbury-Hall, Armstrong, Ndiaye; George, Barry

Here's how we start against Newcastle. UTT! 🔵📺 https://t.co/2VsWpyRq02 pic.twitter.com/vpnLPTRmLl

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#1959. Preston North End vs Sheffield United - prediction, team news, lineups

#1957. Moreira lifts lid on Kaka-inspired number choice, first derby and friendship with Rabiot

Diego Moreira is gearing up for his first derby as an AC Milan player, and he is very much relishing the occasion.

Moreira was the second big splash in the summer window for Milan, after the club-record signing of Goncalo Ramos from Paris Saint-Germain. The Belgian has already impressed with three goals to his name, including a brace that rescued a draw against Lazio in the capital.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Having sat out of the last two games against Udinese and Bologna, the good news is that Moreira has recovered from his muscle issue and will therefore be available to the head coach Ruben Amorim for tomorrow night’s derby.

He spoke to DAZN in the ‘Remember The Name’ programme in an interview that was broadcast on the eve of the game, with his words relayed by MilanVibes.

“My name is Diego because it was my mother’s favourite name. She adored Diego Maradona and really liked it. When people analyse it, they say that with this name I seem to be made to play football, so I really like it.

“My Instagram name? My godfather’s name is Armizy on social media, and I copied it. I spend a lot of time with him. When I was little, I used to play football everywhere and break everything.

“My dream was to become a professional footballer, and we’re almost there, come on (laughs). I left home at 15, a very difficult time for my mother, but now we’re happy because I’ve achieved my dream of becoming a footballer, and the sacrifices we made have led to this.

“My mom is very important to me, she’s unique, and everything we’ve been through now makes us happy. I talk to dad often, and when I finish games and they don’t go well, I only talk to him because I know we’ll talk about football and nothing else.

“He was the one who called me and told me about AC Milan’s interest, he was just waiting for me to say yes or no. When AC Milan calls you, you can’t say no. My tattoos speak of my family, even my grandparents.”

You have spoken before about Hazard, Kaka and Cristiano Ronaldo…

“Eden is a gem. A champion, an inspiration: when you grow up watching him, you try his moves and hope to be able to do them on the pitch one day. Cristiano is my idol, a champion, the greatest.

“As a kid, I wanted to be him, to have my hair cut like him, but I had too much. He made me believe in myself and pushed me to play football. I’m happy to have enjoyed his prime.

“Kaka? I wanted number 7. When they told me it was available, I was tempted to take it, but I like number 22. I hope to honour it and do well enough to deserve this number.”

“Milan-Inter is one of the biggest derbies in Europe. We’re fired up, I’d die for my team and to play these games, we’re fired up.”

You have struck up a friendship with Rabiot…

“From the first few days, Adrien has been one of the ones who welcomed me best, especially because he speaks French.

“We talk a lot, especially because we’re always the last ones in the dressing room, so we often eat together and talk about life, football, everything. I also really enjoy being on the pitch, so that helps us get along.”

“The fact that I have a strong personality has helped me settle in. I feel great in this group and they understand me. We have to win games to bring Milan back to where it deserves to be: we have quality, spirit, a great group and we have to do it.”

#1956. LASK Linz vs Slovan Bratislava - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 01 Nov 2026 12:10, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 12:11

After posting their first-ever Champions League win, LASK Linz will aim to double that tally when rock-bottom Slovan Bratislava visit Austria on Tuesday.

Before the sides meet at Raiffeisen Arena, LASK occupy the final qualifying slot, while Slovan are on course to finish pointless once again.

LASK's third European Cup campaign - and their first to reach either the group or league phase - started with back-to-back defeats at the hands of AEK Athens and Liverpool, but they finally got off the mark last time out.

After failing to take any points from their opening two matches, Dietmar Kuhbauer's side stunned Sporting in Lisbon, despite initially falling behind at Estadio Alvalade.

LASK soon hauled themselves level through Christoph Lang, before Sasa Kalajdzic and Krystof Danek scored midway through the second half to put them in full control.

With a masterful counter-attacking display, the Austrian champions ended up winning 3-2, so they have scored six times across their last two Champions League matches.

However, Kuhbauer will be acutely aware his side have conceded first in all three league phase fixtures so far, which is surely unsustainable if they are to reach the knockout rounds.

Including their dramatic playoff victory over Celtic, Die Schwarz-Weissen have not yet kept a clean sheet, while they have kept just one from 12 games across all competitions since the start of September.

That did not stop them beating WSG Tirol 2-1 in the Austrian Bundesliga on Saturday, though they currently sit third behind Red Bull Salzburg and resurgent giants Rapid Vienna.

To date, Slovan Bratislava have lost all four of their competitive games in Austria - conceding 14 goals along the way - and there are few reasons to hope such a streak can now end.

Slovan have lost all but one of 12 away fixtures in either the European Cup or Champions League - the sole exception was way back in 1970 - and they are already looking in some trouble this term.

After coming through qualifying, they recently became the only team to lose their first 10 games in UEFA's top competition, and the Slovakian side have yet to pick up a point.

Slovan opened up with a 6-1 hammering at the hands of reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain, then were beaten 3-0 by Stuttgart on matchday two, before going down 4-0 to Roma last time out.

It may be no surprise that the Sky Blues have faced the most shots (77) and the most shots on target (32) so far, while recording the joint-fewest shots (25) and fewest shots on target (five) at the other end.

Having finished 35th of 36 teams two years ago - without picking up any points - a similar fate could await if they fail to stop the rot soon, and even their traditional domestic dominance seems to be at risk.

Yaya Toure's men did beat Podbrezova 2-1 on Saturday, but they still lie second in Slovakia's Super Liga, trailing five points behind leaders Dunajska Streda.

Slovan Bratislava form (all competitions):

Aside from injured pair George Bello and Ramiz Harakate, LASK boss Kuhbauer should have a full squad available, after Nigeria international Moses Usor recently returned from a shoulder problem.

Rested on Saturday, Austria striker Kalajdzic has scored on both of his two starts in major European competition - for Eintracht Frankfurt in the 2023-24 Conference League and against Sporting last month.

Also benched at the weekend, captain Sascha Horvath is set to return in central midfield.

Meanwhile, Slovan have doubts about two forwards: Roman Cerepkai (back) and Andraz Sporar (illness).

Though the latter could be cleared to play, Gambian winger Suleiman Camara is ready to stand in, and Nino Marcelli offers another option.

The visitors' main man is Tigran Barseghyan, who scored their opening goal against Podbrezova and topped their charts for goal involvements, assists and chances created during the 2024-25 Champions League.

Likely to start on the bench, veteran defender Kevin Wimmer is a former LASK player, having made 31 appearances for the Linz club in 2011-12.

Jungwirth; Jorgensen, Mbuyamba, Andrade, Alemao, Dibango; Ljubicic, Horvath, Danek; Lang, Kalajdzic

Slovan Bratislava possible starting lineup:

Takac; Blackman, Bajric, Markovic, Cruz; Pokorny, Ibrahim, Gajdos; Barseghyan, Marcelli, Camara

These sides have been below their very best on the domestic scene, and they are both leaking lots of goals in Europe.

Sensing a big chance to claim precious Champions League points, they could put on an open contest, which the hosts will ultimately win.

The Ibrox ace made his international debut for his country last month and played in three friendlies against Ecuador, Uruguay and Venezuela and was an unused sub against Uzbekistan.

But that wasn't enough to see him included in South Korea's latest squad for their games against Qatar and Saudi Arabia later this month.

However, he has now been included in their under-21s squad for two friendlies against Mexico.

The squad doubles as South Korea's Olympic team for the football section of the Games in two years' time in Los Angeles.

South Korea Under 21s boss Kim Eun-joong said: "This is a good opportunity to gain practical experience against a strong team, Mexico.

"We will identify areas for improvement and take our competitiveness up a level."

Kim will travel to his homeland for the two games against the Mexicans at Cheonan on November 14 and a rematch against the same opponents three days later at the same venue.

#1954. Musah talks second chance at Milan, upcoming derby, Modric and other team-mates

The media coverage has ramped up into overdrive on the eve of the derby, with Yunus Musah the latest to speak ahead of the game.

Musah spent last season out on loan at Atalanta with Massimiliano Allegri not deeming him to be a part of his plans, but he returned in the summer as the Bergamo club did not use the option to buy. Many thought he would be packing his suitcases again, but that wasn’t the case.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Instead, the new head coach Ruben Amorim has placed a great deal of faith in the American, using him in a deeper midfield role which seems to be bringing out the best from him. He has previously spoken about feeling ‘grateful’ to have been given a fresh chance by Amorim.

Musah spoke in an interview with CBS Sports to preview Saturday night’s big game, one in which Milan really need three points in order to reduce the gap to the top of the standings. His words are via MilanNews.

“There’s still a long way to go, but after losing a season, I’ve learned that even in crucial moments, you have to keep going. Now I’m really keen to stay. I want to stay at this club and do really well here. The coach is helping me a lot, giving me opportunities that I need to seize.”

Considering what you went through last year, you’ve become the most used central midfielder this season: what instructions did the coach give you? What was the first thing he said to you when you spoke?

“Nothing complicated. The coaching staff works as a team, so the entire team knows exactly what each member is doing. They give us all the necessary instructions: how to receive the ball, how to read the various moments of the game, and how to interpret the play according to their instructions.

“This allows me to step onto the pitch without any hesitation. It’s a huge help, because when you step onto the pitch, you know exactly what you have to do.”

Can you better understand where you might not be recognised?

“For example, sometimes at the supermarket, when there aren’t many people, someone still stares at me, everyone wants to say hello or ask me something because everyone knows and watches AC Milan.

“Then, at a club where winning every single match is crucial, other teams approach AC Milan differently: for them, it’s the most important match of the season. Every match is difficult, everything has changed. Sometimes, to escape this celebrity aura, I go shopping at the supermarket at night.”

Knowing that Luka Modrić has been my favourite player for about 10-15 years, and given that you have the opportunity to train with him every day, what’s it like being around him?

“Yes, I try to enjoy the moment and the time I can spend with him. It won’t be many years, so I really appreciate every moment we spend together in midfield. In the past, when he played for Real Madrid, I managed to get a shirt.

“The world of football is really small, but now we find ourselves playing together, side by side in midfield. It’s unreal. It’s fantastic to share the dressing room with him, to be on the pitch with him.

“I’m learning so many things on the pitch just by watching him. Sometimes we speak Spanish, he speaks both English and Spanish well.”

“It’s a different game than the others. When you train for the derby, it’s more special. You don’t have to tell any of your teammates how important the game is or that they need to focus on it.

“Everyone is focused, working hard because it’s incredibly important for our fans, for us. It’s the game where, when you win, it’s like you’ve won a trophy. I’m very focused on this match.”

How difficult is it to focus on the games before the derby knowing that the match is so close?

“I think before the match, we all know the derby is close, but we’re focusing on the games we have to play first, then when the match comes, we’ll think about it. Clearly, it’s very important to win and take home the three points.”

Who did you grow up with as an AC Milan or Italian football idol? Who did you watch as a child?

“I really liked Ronaldinho, but I didn’t watch much football back then. I watched him more later, even through highlights. When I was little, I played football a lot more than I watched it. I enjoyed playing. Every day I’d go out with my brother and my friends and we’d spend hours playing.

“I love those days, out in the street playing. Anyway, Ronaldinho was a great player, and that’s why I chose the number 80 when I arrived at Milan.”

Who is most likely to become a coach after a playing career?

“Matteo Gabbia is truly tactically savvy.”

Who is most likely to become a social media influencer?

“I would have said Rafa but now I say Diego Moreira.”

Who is most likely to lose one of the three essential items: phone, wallet, or keys?

“Mario Gila always loses a lot of things, like on airplanes. Yes, definitely him. He needs those Apple gadgets, what are they called? AirTags! Yes, we need to give him some AirTags for Christmas.”

And who could survive the longest on a desert island?

“I’d say, I like it! I’m very resourceful, you know?

What’s the secret to surviving on a desert island? You seem very confident…

“I wouldn’t let the pressure get me down. I’d work hard, I’d try to find everything I needed to survive, I’d go fishing.”

The team most likely to win the Milan derby is?
