#1953. Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

After the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK

Both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

Luis Enrique has now won 13 trophies with PSG. Serial winner 🏆 pic.twitter.com/RAsyI1Ui2s

💬 "We are ALWAYS hungry you know... we want more, we want more" Désiré Doué reflects on PSG's UEFA Super Cup Final win.📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nwreU1Skz7

Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

Possession: PSG 61%- Aston Villa 39%Shots: 12-15Shots on target: 6-4Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 29-34

Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

Not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo

Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

Into the final minute of added time we go.

Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

One final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

The ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

Alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

Aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

Aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a big chance for Hemmings.

Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

The VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

Doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

Cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

Mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

Other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

Just inside the PSG penalty area, McGinn cuts onto his left to get his shot away and his deflected effort is saved by Safonov diving to his right.

One of Aston Villa’s coaches has been booked for some protestations after Torres is penalised for a foul on Doue. Torres is also booked for that challenge.

Two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

Incredible to think he is only 17 years and 212 days old. He’s been all over PSG centre-back Willian Pacho and thoroughly deserves his goal.

The teenager could even have had a hat-trick. What a second-half this could be.

Madjo has managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s Georgian magician Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, which is quite some achievement.

Possession: PSG 67%-33% Aston VillaShots: 6-10Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 11-17

After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Madjo has his third massive chance of this first half and this shot comes off the post. Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

Aston Villa have had a few great chances in this first half and there is another. A free-kick into the PSG penalty area causes issues for the French side and Kamara’s header towards goal is saved by Safonov.

Madjo has his second huge chance of this first half. Once more it is McGinn who provides the cross. The Scot does really well on the right side of the box to fake the cross with his left and instead delivers with his right. He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

Aston Villa have just settled things down. Either side of Kvaratskhelia’s goal, they were on the ropes but have calmed things down.

Hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

Referees are now hot on players taking too long over throw-ins, with Mendes falling foul of that. That is one of the fairly new rules that will be good for the game.

A huge chance for 17-year-old Madjo to equalise. McGinn picks out the young striker with a sublime cross from the right. Madjo is just eight yards out and has a free header but it goes just wide of the far post. Aston Villa should be level.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

After Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. The Portuguese defender then has four different teammates that he could pick out in the penalty area but his cross misses all four.

PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia shows great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

A few minutes after I said that Aston Villa had done a decent job of keeping PSG at bay, Luis Enrique’s side take the lead. Bizot had just made a great reflex save to deny Doue but he is unable to stop Kvaratskhelia’s effort. The Georgian cuts inside onto his right just inside the Aston Villa penalty area and gets his shot away quickly after quick feet. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

As you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

Moments later, Kamara decides to shoot from range and his low, driving effort goes wide of Safonov’s right post. With Onana injured long-term and Tielemans now at Manchester United, Kamara’s importance to Aston Villa is even higher.

In last year’s Super Cup, PSG were stunned in the first hour against Tottenham as went 2-0 down before coming back to win on penalties. PSG have played fewer friendlies than Aston Villa up until this point so there may be a little more rustiness in Luis Enrique’s side than Unai Emery’s.

This is going to be a very tall order for Aston Villa, who look very different tonight to how they ended last season, up against a team of PSG’s calibre. Not only have Villa sold some key players like Rogers and Tielemans but the likes of Konsa and Watkins are yet to return after the World Cup.

McGinn is afforded too much space and time to cut onto his left foot out on the right and whip a dangerous cross towards the far post. Pacho is on hand to head away with a great defensive header.

Moments later, good work from Maatsen out on the left earns Aston Villa a corner. Unai Emery’s side have made a decent start to this game. Buendia’s delivery into the near post is headed away by Marquinhos.

We are under way in Salzburg, where it has been a very hot day but the temperature has cooled a touch with the sun having set in Austria.

Some huge banners are on display on the pitch, displaying not only the emblems of the two clubs but also images of the trophy lifts that have earned these sides a place in tonight’s game. Both sides emerge from the tunnel, past the trophies they won with the two captains carrying them out, and we are moments away from kick-off in Salzburg. Here is a reminder of how the sides line up tonight:

PSG: Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Nuno Mendes, Joao Neves, Vitinha, Zaire-Emery, Akliouche, Doue, Kvaratskhelia.Substitutes: Chevalier, Beraldo, Zabarnyi, Ruiz, Dembele, Digne, Hernandez, Mayulu, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.

Aston Villa: Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Joao Gomes, Kamara, Hemmings, Buendia, McGinn, Madjo.Substitutes: Wright, Asemota, Mings, Barkley, Abraham, Bogarde, Nedeljkovic, Alysson, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.

💬 " I am confident they're going to play today with the level we need" Unai Emery on the inclusion of João Gomes and Brian Madjo into Aston Villa's lineup. 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FCjBmGDcNo

Lucas Digne has only just swapped Aston Villa for PSG in recent days but he already comes up against his old teammates. He is on the bench for PSG tonight and could offer some good insight into Unai Emery’s side.

PSG forwards Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and both are on the bench for PSG tonight. As PSG close in on moves for Ferran Torres and Mika Godts, could Liverpool’s moves for Barcola and Mbaye accelerate in the next few days? Barcola has only recently returned to training after the World Cup and is joined on the bench by compatriot Ousmane Dembele. Maghnes Akliouche, who has joined PSG from Monaco this summer, starts tonight.

Brian Madjo is just 17-years-old but he starts up top for Aston Villa tonight against the Champions League winners, with Ollie Watkins yet to return after the World Cup.

“There is a lot of change but when you look at other clubs in England, there is a lot of change. What we have still is our main core, same manager, same methods and same desire to achieve more. A lot thought we reached our ceiling a few seasons ago and we proved them wrong. As long as we have that hunger to achieve more, Aston Villa fans can expect as much as possible.”

New Villa signing Alejandro Garnacho has been ruled out tonight as part of the concussion protocols.

Garnacho was signed from Chelsea last month and took a whack to his face in the recent game against BG Pathum in Thailand.

Tonight’s game will be refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but got turned away at the border.

Team news is in 🔒 #PSGAVL pic.twitter.com/yeKkyIKiHQ

What will we learn from the “new Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

Unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

The Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

“I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

“I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

“No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”

PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

#1952. Arda Guler's stunning stats create Mourinho dilemma

By Naim Beneddra | 01 Nov 2026 12:21

Jose Mourinho faces an increasingly complicated selection dilemma at Real Madrid, with Arda Guler emerging as one of La Liga's most creative players despite regularly being substituted by the Portuguese manager.

The 21-year-old Turkey international has registered 33 key passes and created 10 big chances in the Spanish top flight this season, figures that place him among the competition's leading attacking playmakers.

Yet Guler has completed none of his eight league starts, raising an intriguing question about his place in Mourinho's plans as competition for attacking positions intensifies.

According to Brazilian outlet Trivela, the former Fenerbahce youngster has become one of Madrid's most influential performers, with his contribution to the team's attacking play extending well beyond his goals and assists.

His performances have taken on additional significance during Vinicius Junior's four-match suspension, while summer signing Yan Diomande has also taken advantage of his opportunities.

With the Brazilian's return approaching and Rodrygo expected to recover from injury in January, Mourinho could soon face some difficult decisions over how to accommodate his attacking options.

?⚪️ Arda Güler has created the MOST chances for Real Madrid this season. https://t.co/lzStdJbUnj

Guler has contributed three goals and four assists across all competitions this season, but those numbers tell only part of the story.

In La Liga, the Turkish midfielder has scored twice and provided two assists, despite creating 33 shooting opportunities for his teammates.

That puts him level with Barcelona's Lamine Yamal for key passes in the competition, according to figures compiled by Sofascore and highlighted by Trivela.

Even more impressively, Guler has created 10 big chances, the second-highest total in La Liga, while his expected assists figure stands at 3.39.

The discrepancy between his two actual assists and his underlying creative numbers suggests that his contribution has not always been rewarded by his teammates' finishing.

His performances also demonstrate why Mourinho has increasingly used him in different areas of the pitch.

Although frequently deployed on the right, Guler regularly moves into central positions to receive possession, link midfield with attack and deliver passes into dangerous areas.

He has also become an important part of Madrid's set-piece routines, with three of his four assists in all competitions coming from corners or free kicks.

However, his influence in open play has been just as important.

During October's victory over Rayo Vallecano, he produced a precise through ball for Kylian Mbappe to complete the scoring.

Guler also played a significant role in Madrid's 2-1 El Clasico victory over Barcelona, initiating the move that led to Mbappe's decisive goal.

His pass released Eduardo Camavinga, who carried the attack forward before supplying the French striker.

The youngster could have added further assists in that match, having created promising opportunities for both Mbappe and Diomande.

Those contributions have helped Guler develop into a central figure in Madrid's attacking structure, even though Mourinho has continued to manage his minutes carefully.

The Turkish international has started eight of his 10 La Liga appearances this season, without completing any of those starts.

Against Barcelona, he remained on the pitch until the closing stages, marking a departure from several earlier matches in which he had been withdrawn considerably sooner.

There is no suggestion that the substitutions reflect a disagreement between Guler and Mourinho, but the pattern is striking given the midfielder's creative output.

Guler's growing importance comes at a time when Madrid's attacking hierarchy is becoming increasingly crowded.

Mbappe has already scored 14 goals this season, establishing himself as the side's principal attacking reference point.

Jude Bellingham has also remained a regular under Mourinho, although his role has evolved towards carrying the ball through midfield and contributing to Madrid's build-up play.

Meanwhile, Diomande has made an increasingly compelling case for regular selection.

The summer arrival has recorded six goal involvements in his last five appearances, making the most of the opportunity created by Vinicius's suspension.

That combination of form and tactical flexibility presents Mourinho with an intriguing problem.

Guler's creativity has become particularly valuable, but the manager must also consider how to reintegrate Vinicius, who is eligible to return after the November international break.

The Brazilian is serving a four-match suspension following his dismissal against Villarreal and has therefore been unavailable during Madrid's recent winning run.

Rodrygo's anticipated return in January would add another experienced attacking option, although his recovery from a knee injury remains an important consideration.

For Mourinho, the challenge is not simply deciding which players deserve to start. It is finding a combination that preserves Madrid's ability to create chances while maintaining the balance that has contributed to their improved results.

Guler's versatility could work in his favour, particularly given his ability to operate between midfield and the right flank.

However, his repeated substitutions suggest that Mourinho has not yet settled on how best to use the Turkish international over the course of a full match.

Madrid face Racing Santander on Sunday before travelling to AEK Athens in the Champions League and Valencia in La Liga next week.

Those fixtures offer further opportunities to assess Guler's importance before Vinicius becomes available again.

With 33 key passes already to his name, the Turkey international has developed a compelling statistical argument for retaining his place, regardless of which attacking stars return to contention.

#1951. 'I thought I was watching The Karate Kid' - top ref rages at Rangers VAR escape

Mark Clattenburg has called out Ryan Lee and John Beaton after insisting Rangers' James Penrice should have been sent off during the Scottish League Cup semi-final win over Aberdeen.

The former FIFA referee was left stunned after Penrice escaped punishment for a first-half challenge on Aremu Afeez before going on to set up Ryan Naderi's late winner as Rangers booked their place in the final at Hampden.

Penrice, operating in midfield alongside Nicolas Raskin, escaped punishment after missing the ball and catching Aberdeen's Afeez with a high, studs-up challenge near the halfway line.

Referee Lee opted against showing a card, while VAR official Beaton chose not to intervene.

Read more: Martin O'Neill sent health plea from worried Rangers hero as Celtic rivalry parked

The decision has come under intense scrutiny, with Clattenburg unable to believe Penrice remained on the pitch.

Speaking on the So Near, Yet So VAR podcast, he said: “I thought I wasn’t even watching football. I was watching my favourite, The Karate Kid.

“Listen, it’s more justifiable and easier to understand when the ball isn’t really that high. If you look at it again, the ball isn’t really there, and I think the player knows what he’s doing.”

Clattenburg went on to explain why he believes the challenge was impossible to defend.

He said: “I think he’s just decided he wants to catch his opponent high with his studs.

“And when you’re playing the ball, when you’re trying to play, you don’t go in like that. You would go in with your body. You would go in with your knee.

“You don’t go in with your studs and then make a clear movement with the studs towards an opponent’s ribs, hip, wherever we want to call it.

“I was surprised it wasn’t red. I’ve seen it in real time.

“For me, when it’s not a footballing action, then you can never support a player’s actions, and I think when a referee gives a red, then nobody can have any argument.”

Former SPFL referee Bobby Madden agreed with Clattenburg's assessment, with both officials adamant Rangers should have been reduced to 10 men.

The controversy was heightened when Penrice went on to have a decisive impact on the result, providing the assist for Naderi's 83rd-minute winner that secured Rangers' place in the final.

Aberdeen will feel particularly aggrieved given the match-winning contribution came from a player many believe should already have been dismissed.

Clattenburg and Madden are not alone in that opinion. Former SFA referee Des Roache has also argued that Penrice should have been sent off for the challenge on Afeez.

#1950. GdS: Milan vs. Inter to be a ‘full’ sell-out for the first time since 2019 – the reason

The derby between AC Milan and Inter on Saturday night will be a full sell-out for the first time in over half a decade.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, it is as if there has been a surge in pride just hours after the unveiling of the new stadium that will replace it in five years. San Siro opens its arms even wider for tomorrow’s derby, as it has for over 100 years.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The highest possible capacity can be sold: for the occasion, the safety curtains located in the two stands will be removed, namely, the Terzo Anello Blu (South) and Terzo Anello Verde (North). This means that San Siro will be a sellout in the truest sense of the word.

The last time it happened was for the derby on 17 March 2019, with 77,479 spectators. A total of 2,350 additional seats are available: this is the amount that was removed from the stadium’s capacity in the summer of 2019, which became effective starting with the 2019-20 football season.

The decision was made by the Provincial Supervisory Commission and implemented by the City of Milan and the MI Stadio, following observations by the technical commission, which also included the Polytechnic University, of the vibrations felt particularly in those areas (sectors 349-351-352 of the Green third and 307-309-310 of the Blue third).

This measure, however, was not related to a true safety issue, but was considered ‘managerial’ by the technicians at Palazzo Marino: the aim was to prevent fear from spreading among fans when they felt the vibrations.

It’s worth noting that the absence of restrictions will apply to both the league and the Coppa Italia: in the Europa League for AC Milan and the Champions League for Inter, the screens will be regularly placed in the centre of the away stands.

Anyone entering San Siro, however, has been accustomed for years to seeing those three blue and green rectangles located in the stands at the centre of the third tier. Now they will no longer be there: San Siro is destined to say goodbye, but for now it’s only revving up.

#1949. Martin O'Neill tells Celtic new players to 'cope' as Falkirk post-mortem begins

Martin O’Neill admits Celtic’s new players need to show they can handle the pressure of playing for the club following the 2-0 defeat to Falkirk.

Goals from Ethan Ross and Scott Tanser proved the difference as the home side racked up a fourth successive victory to move up to fourth in the table.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Celtic, in contrast, have now won just three of their last 10 matches as they passed up the chance to move seven points clear of Rangers at the top.

Camilo Duran endured an off-day as he failed to score despite creating numerous chances, while Callum Osmand, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Mika Baur and Haissem Hassan also struggled. And O’Neill acknowledged it will take a strong mindset for the squad to come through this turbulent period.

He said: “You have to cope with the pressure to be a player here. And sometimes, as the great Tommy Burns once said, it might be easier to play against Celtic than for them at this stage.

“But hopefully we've enough players in the dressing room who've been big winners here, who can hopefully pull them through that. We have conceded some poor goals and haven’t kept a clean sheet for some time which is the essence of a championship team. But we’re still top and we need to address it. And that’s the way out of it.

“It’s Celtic Football Club. We’re not used to losing a lot of games. But we were in a much worse position this time last year so we have to buckle down and win a game in Europe [against Besiktas]. Thursday is a big game and then the following Sunday is massive [against Kilmarnock] before we go into the international break.”

Celtic had 24 shots throughout the 90 minutes with nine on target but couldn’t find a way past Scott Bain who made a number of impressive stops against his former club.

“I’m naturally disappointed to have lost the game,” added O’Neill. “We had a lot of chances. Their goalie was magnificent but naturally we’ve lost so I’m very disappointed.

“At half-time I thought we were still in the game. I thought we’d played decent stuff. If you concede a magnificent goal you take it in your stride. When you concede a bad goal then it’s tough to come back. And then the goalie makes some saves and it’s frustrating. Despite mistakes at the back, we had enough chances to get back.”

This was Falkirk’s first win over Celtic since March 2007 and John McGlynn praised his players for a big performance.

He said: “Huge credit to my players. It was a remarkable shift. I don’t want to take anything away from the outfield players but Scott Bain had the game of his life. That’s our fourth win on the bounce, and three clean sheets in a row so I’m ecstatic.

“Beating Rangers or Celtic was one of the boxes left to tick. Thankfully we’ve done that. We’ve climbed the table and we look forward to Tynecastle next week.”

#1948. Celtic Europa League rivals make shock decision to sack history-making boss

Celtic's Europa League opponents Torreense have sacked the manager who made history with the Portuguese minnows after they slumped to the bottom half of the country's second tier.

The Hoops face one of the smallest teams ever to play in the league phase of European competition later this month when they play Torreense.

The game will be played in Leiria, 50 miles away from their home of Torres Vedras, because their 2,000-capacity stadium is not suitable.

They made history last season when they defeated Sporting Lisbon in the Portuguese Cup Final under boss Luis Tralhao.

But they have sacked him and replaced him with former Estrela da Amadora manager Joao Nuno instead.

Torreense are languishing in 12th place in the Portuguese second division after a disastrous season so far domestically.

However, they made history when they won in Norway against Lillestrom in their opening game and were only defeated by Sunderland after an injury time goal.

They play Armenian outfit Ararat-Armenia this week - the only team behind Celtic in the table, on goal difference - before welcoming the Parkhead side at the end of the month.

The Imps have collected four points from their last six league matches, with the victory over Burnley and a 2-2 draw at Millwall their only positive results in that sequence.

#1945. Amorim discusses Cardinale’s ‘Top Gun’ remark, Scudetto aim, Ramos’ struggles and injuries

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim has responded to Gerry Cardinale’s words about him being his ‘Top Gun’ and the Scudetto being an aim.

For Milan, there is once again the need to bounce back after a negative result. On Wednesday night at San Siro they led at half-time against Bologna, before conceding three times in the second half to eventually lose 4-2.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Not only did that knock the Rossoneri out of the top four but it put them seven points behind Inter and Lazio who are the league-leaders at the moment. So, it means that a victory is needed in the derby to keep pace at the top, but there is at least some good injury news: Diego Moreira, Mario Gila and Adrien Rabiot are all back.

Amorim spoke to the reporters who gathered at Milanello for his pre-match press conference on the eve of the game. MilanNews relayed his words.

“I truly appreciate Cardinale’s support. We already knew – and everyone here has the clarity to understand – that we can’t build a solid foundation if we have to deal with these kinds of issues in the middle of the season.

“It will take time, it’s inevitable, but at the same time, we want to win every single game: when we fail to do so, we’ll continue to feel it, making it our own with great pain. It will be like this for a while. We need time to grow and improve the team, and we know that good things take time to find the perfect balance and hit the mark.

“I think it’s a good analogy and it makes perfect sense, but that doesn’t take away the pain of defeat. That’s still there, it still stings, but we need to be extremely clear with our fans, making them understand that it will take time.”

What differences do you feel between this derby and the ones in Manchester and Lisbon?

“I think it’s a special match because it’s being played in the same city, and yesterday we saw the plans for the new stadium. It’s a unique rivalry, but there’s also a deep bond: two great teams in the same city sharing a stadium.

“I don’t think you can find a context like this anywhere else; it’s truly special. But matches like this… well, if we look at Portuguese culture, the feeling is the same: the sense of responsibility for victory, the enthusiasm of the fans, are very similar. The football culture here is closer to that of Portugal.

“In England, it’s slightly different: there’s a great battle, but the spirit remains a bit more sporting. Here, you can feel that Latin element that we also experience in Portugal, so I really think it will be a special match.”

“They’re ready to join the team. We’ll have to evaluate tomorrow morning whether they’ll be able to start or what the game plan will be. Of course, I already have an idea, but we’ll see tomorrow.”

Has the team regained the energy it didn’t see on Wednesday?

“Everyone knows it’s a special match, a special moment, and when you get to play it, the context doesn’t matter, it doesn’t matter if you’re tired. You have to go out there and give it your all, and we’ll be there.

“I said it: I felt it from the first minute of the match against Bologna, watching the game from the bench. We can’t lose a game like that. We can’t afford to concede two goals in two minutes. We can do much better, and there are so many small details that I’ve already discussed with the team.

“But since we returned from international duty three weeks ago, there hasn’t been any real time to train. And I’m not saying other teams are in a different position, I’m speaking for ourselves: I feel like there are so many small things we’re missing simply because we don’t have the time to address them in training.

“So it’s not just a question of energy, although I’ve noticed that, because with energy you can also mask a lot of shortcomings, but there are so many aspects we need time to work on if we want to become a better team.”

Cardinale says that the Scudetto is possible this year and that there will be some signings in January…

“You always have to talk about the Scudetto as the main objective when you’re at Milan, but we’ve already dropped points and we need to fix things. We just have to focus on improving the team step by step.

“What we did wrong in the last match needs to be corrected for the next one. Because if we start thinking too far ahead, about the standings and long-term goals, we risk forgetting what’s really important to us. We want to win consistently, year after year.

“We don’t want to win a season just because we had a bit of luck or because we took shortcuts in the foundations of the project, only to find ourselves back where we started the following year. That’s why we have to fix things day by day, addressing both needs in parallel.

“But when you’re Milan, the moral obligation is to declare that the objective is to win. And at the same time, we have to be aware that next week we have a match that could allow us to close the gap at the top.

“Taking all this into account, we just have to focus on winning the next match, and everything else will calm down. But the objective of the club is always and in any case winning Serie A and that remains our final goal. How long will it take? I don’t know.”

“I have zero envy for Chivu because I’m already in the right place, that is, at Milan and not at Inter. That’s the way I am, that’s the way I am.

“I haven’t learned the lesson from my previous experience: I chose more or less the same situation, a club in the midst of rebuilding, which is trying to launch young players like Cisse to build something from scratch.

“It’s a challenge that excites me, I like it, and that’s why I chose this project: I’m really happy with my choice. At the same time, however, I’m not naive: I know very well that you have to win games to buy yourself the time necessary to build something lasting.

“Everyone chooses their own path, and this is mine. Whether it will work or not, no one can know anything now, but I’m really happy because this reflects exactly who I am and the type of work I want to do.

“I understand the questions you ask me: there are days when, in the morning, I think that perhaps I could have had more experience, more calm, a larger squad, fewer injuries. But at the end of the day, I was the one who chose this job, so I’m very happy with it and I’ll go all the way, straight down my path.

“You already know: if I embrace an idea, I certainly don’t change my mind. I can change the tactical system, sure, but I won’t change my conviction, and I’ll do everything I can to win and be successful here.”

What do you think of Inter? Did you speak to Chivu yesterday?

“He’s very nice. We were complaining a bit about the timing of the presentation because we’d played the night before: he won, so he was happier than me, but we had a match to prepare for, and that was our priority.

“But I think we were all really enthusiastic about the new stadium, I think everyone can say that. Inter, for me, is that team we were talking about: a team that can play with their eyes closed, that rotates, like in the last match in midfield, and continues to express themselves in exactly the same way.

“Certain individual characteristics change, but they already know what to do on the pitch even without needing to practice too much. They have an extraordinary ability to read the moments of the game.

“You can clearly sense that, even if they find themselves behind late on, they have the maturity to understand that they can win any match: it’s an awareness you gain when you win so many matches and so many titles.

“They have a lot of talent in their squad, but we’re there to fight against that too and we’ll be ready for the match.”

Goncalo Ramos scored a brace against you in a derby between Benfica and Sporting CP with you on the bench. Could he also be the man for the Milan derby?

“I think it could be. I think all the problems and difficulties Goncalo Ramos is experiencing are primarily a team issue. I think we need to push forward… We control games well, but we play too far from the opponent’s goal.

“We need to raise our centre of gravity and the team on the pitch, spending more time in that area of ​​the pitch to allow Ramos to play his game. He’s playing far from the goal because the team can’t push the opponent in the final thirty metres. I think we need time to correct this aspect as well.

“We want to do better and we will improve in this area. But in any match, a player like Goncalo Ramos, who has already shown he can break the deadlock at any moment and score in any situation, can be the man of the match in the next one.”

Why did you reduce the squad so much at the start of the season? Do you regret it?

“When it happens, you think about it, but these are things you can’t control. There are factors that are beyond your control. Think about Saelemaekers, who had that physical problem practically at the end of a training match during the international break.

“Then Chukwueze comes along with another problem, and as a result Moreira ends up being overworked because he’s forced to play more minutes since Chukwueze and Saelemaekers aren’t there. Imagine having three players for a single position and all three get injured: at that point you overload that department.

“And then you take that player and make your rotations, and you find yourself fielding Tomori… well, I’m not saying as a winger, but adapted to emergency situations, maybe having him do an extra 400-meter sprint.

“Then obviously I take the risk because I want to win against Bologna, I know perfectly well that we can’t afford to lose other players and that certain characteristics were needed for that specific match. So I pushed for Tomori and we found ourselves with this problem.

“I think that sometimes Some things simply can’t be controlled; you have to imagine them. In my head, at the beginning, I had three options for that role, and all three had physical problems: when that happens, you can’t manage the impossible.

“Unless you have a squad of forty players, but then you have to deal with financial management, with each player’s playing time, or you have to accept taking some risks, taking a gamble. Today, if I could go back, maybe I’d want a few more players.

“But if we look at the situation rationally – and we have to be rational – the numbers at the start of the week told us we were fine with the rotations; but then in the last week, with three games in a few days, we found ourselves with six or seven starters or key players out of action.

“It’s a situation you can’t control. So, to answer the question: yes, maybe we’re short on resources right now, but there’s always a rational logic behind every decision made at the start of the season.”

Ramos gets fouled a lot. Should he become a bit more aggressive too?

“I like the way we’re going here in Italy, we’re on the right path. More speed, fewer fouls: I think it’s an evolution that’s improving the quality of the game. Sometimes you might think that maybe that could be a foul, but I like it that way.

“And then, I’m not going to talk about the referees: just take the images of the Udinese match and compare them with those of other games. I won’t say a single word more and you’ll understand exactly what I mean. But I won’t comment on the referees, I want to be crystal clear.

“I like this kind of approach, I like that in Serie A we see results like 5-1, 4-4, 3-3: I think it’s really a great advertisement for our country and for our movement. However, if you look at what happened with Udinese and compare it to other matches, well…

“Maybe it’s becoming difficult for Ramos to have more touches of the ball, maybe it’s difficult for Ramos to move freely inside the penalty area. Take the images, do the comparison, and then make your own evaluations and decisions.”

A bit of defensive fragility has also been evident in recent matches…

“In Bournemouth, we conceded two goals from penalties and one from a free kick, having been down a man for the entire match.

“Against Bologna, however, we conceded the fourth goal in seven minutes: we were completely out of position, and instead we had to maintain our identity until the last second, because we were buying time to reopen and turn the game around.

“Conceding a 3-2 is not the same as conceding a 4-2, and we still had plenty of time to recover. My feeling is that after the 3-2, we became anxious, starting to lose our composure and overturn our positions on the pitch.

“The central defenders going up with the ball, Pavlovic running forward with the ball, all these little flaws are details that we absolutely must correct in training, talking about them openly.

“It takes that collective maturity to understand that yes, the momentum of the game has changed, but we had 40 minutes left to fix it because we would have created chances anyway. Different situations, different dynamics. on which we must inevitably grow as a team: this is a clear fact.”

“Injuries and muscle problems have nothing to do with the medical staff, the gym staff, or Milan Lab. The responsibility lies with me, the coach, and the way he trains the team.

“What I can say is that there are several situations to consider: overloading certain areas forces us to take risks, and then we need to thoroughly analyse the medical history of individual players.

“Take, for example, those who say that a player like Cisse doesn’t play, scores a goal, and then misses the next match: we need to look at his history, the pubalgia problems, the serious injuries he’s suffered in the last year, and it’s my duty to manage him accordingly.

“We need to consider how many consecutive matches these players have played in the past, how many meters of sprint they complete, whether it’s the same type of effort or whether the game has changed.

“It’s the combination of all these factors that causes injuries. And then there’s bad luck: when you suffer a foot problem, it’s pure and simple bad luck. I’ll tell you: the episode that happened to Saelemaekers was just bad luck.

“When you find yourself With one less option at a certain position, you can’t rotate the players as you’d like, and then things happen. But I want to say this very clearly: the medical staff is extraordinary, they’re doing an exceptional job and they work hard every single day.

“Workload management is my job, it’s my responsibility. I know the medical history of every player on the roster, I know the daily workload, and I try to manage it as best I can. Sometimes, however, I’m forced to take risks, or there are guys who aren’t used to playing so many games in a row.

“Take a player like Jashari: he’s played three games, two of them 90 minutes, without any problems. Others, however, play a half and a half and are already feeling the fatigue.

“We try to monitor and manage all of this with the utmost attention, but I repeat: I’m very happy with our medical staff and they’re doing an incredible job.”

Why these ups and downs in performance and results?

“It’s a combination of factors that combine. Of course, we need to develop the maturity needed to control matches and manage the various moments of a match, and we’ll get there with time.

“Then there’s the busy schedule and the simultaneous injury crisis: a situation that doesn’t make our game any easier, because to perform at our best, we need certain technical and physical characteristics. I think it’s truly a combination of all of these.

“We need to pay attention to every single detail; we need to train more, spend more time talking and working on these aspects. But right now, we don’t even have time to fully recover, let alone do targeted training sessions.

“That’s why we’re having so many difficulties in some matches: to find that consistency of performance, we need to address and correct all these issues during the week, but we don’t have the time. Despite everything, I assure you that we will become a great team.”

Will the substitutions be one of the keys to the match? How is the team’s spirit?

“Regarding the second question, I sensed the right mentality in the players. Yesterday we were bitter, we were angry: more than bitter, we were truly furious. I myself was very angry yesterday, and it’s difficult to start over the next day.

“Today, however, I saw them completely focused on the match against Inter, concentrating on technical and tactical training, because that’s all that matters now. They were extremely attentive and have a clear understanding of the game plan and what needs to be done.

“In terms of attitude and mentality, this team is on the right path. If we analyze our performances, various types of difficulties emerge. There are games where we start terribly and finish on a high, like against Lazio, and others where we play excellent 66 minutes, like against Atalanta, only to then drop in intensity.

“Sometimes it’s more a question of psychological momentum than chronological playing time. The key is to find consistency throughout the entire 90 minutes. We don’t yet have the same experience and maturity as Inter: it’s It’s an obvious fact, and we must acknowledge it pragmatically.

“When Inter find themselves in trouble towards the end, they tend to fill the penalty area, pushing many players forward and using crosses to overload the opposition’s defenses. Our playing style is different; we’re not that type of team.

“So both tactical and technical aspects come into play. We simply need to focus on being consistent throughout the match, because so far we’ve shown different sides depending on the game: sometimes we start strong and then fade, other times we start poorly like against Lazio and improve in the second half.

“We need to become a better team, more mature and capable of reading and interpreting the various moments of the game.”

#1944. Hibs create Hampden history and set up final showdown against Rangers after thrilling Edinburgh derby

Hibs created history by defeating bitter rivals for the first time at Hampden to set up a Premier Sports Cup final clash with Rangers.

Goals from Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath earned Hibs a precious victory - their first under new head coach Marink Reedijk - to upset the form book and take down Hearts.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sitting bottom of the Premiership, Hibs came into the match as major underdogs against Wouter Vrancken's side - with history against them, having losing all four of their previous Edinburgh derbies at Hampden, including a 5-1 Scottish Cup final reversal 14 years ago.

However, they recovered from the concession of an early goal and held firm amid a Hearts fightback to set up a final clash against Rangers on Sunday, December 13.

Hearts started fast and opened the scoring on four minutes. It was a simple goal. Calvin Miller swung in a corner from the right and Braga ran in unmarked to head home from close range.

Given their recent poor form, Hibs could easily have sank without a trace. They responded. Captain Felix Passlack was sent through on goal but Hearts keeper Beau Reus made himself big enough to block.

At the other end, Tomas Magnusson glanced a header just wide of the post - but had to come off afterwards after suffering what looked like concussion in the challenge with Jason Kerr.

Hibs were getting plenty of joy down their left-hand side and on 15 minutes, Owen Elding blazed over the bar after being found in space in the centre of the goal.

Their leveller arrived four minutes later. Boyle darted across from his left flank to meet Elding's clip over the Hearts defence and while Reus got something on the Australian's effort, the ball trickled in via the post and survived a VAR check for offside.

Hibs grew in confidence and pressed Hearts. The Jambos suffered another injury blow on 37 minutes when Miller went down clutching the back of his leg and he was unable to continue.

Hibs went ahead at the break thanks to McGrath's effort on 42 minutes, stabbing home after Joe Newell's drilled effort had been blocked by Hearts defenders.

After a breathless first half, Hearts pushed for a response straight after the restart. Laurent Mendy flashed an effort over the bar on 53 minutes, then a moment later Sallinger did well to turn away a stinging drive from Braga.

Hibs had their chances too. Reus got down low to save from Boyle, while the Belgian was in the right place to deny Marko Ivezic's header just after the hour mark.

Sallinger made a really smart intervention to turn over a fierce Sabri Guendouz strike on 68 minutes as Hearts now pressed hard for an equaliser, with Reedijk's men having to defend a number of crosses into their penalty box.

Nevertheless, Hibs were still dangerous on the break and Reus did really well to plunge at the feet of substitute Thibault Klidje on 75 minutes after he was sent through on goal. The Togolese then curled over on 82 minutes in another counter attack.

Hearts were throwing men forward in a now desperate hunt for the next goal and Braga should have dome better than header wide after another good delivery from Altena on 87 minutes. Then Reus made another huge save, again stopping Klidje.

Hibs weathered the extra three minutes of stoppage time to claim a famous win, with Sunshine on Leith blaring out at the end as the Hibs players celebrated with their ecstatic fans.

#1943. Man City transfer news: Enzo Maresca boost as 22-year-old 'open' to 2027 move

By Darren Plant | 01 Nov 2026 12:56

Manchester City have reportedly received a boost amid alleged interest in Villarreal defender Alex Freeman.

Enzo Maresca and his squad are still reeling from suffering a 1-0 defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion on Saturday.

The Premier League leaders have now posted consecutive losses in the top flight, and could drop down to second place in the standings depending on the result between Liverpool and Arsenal.

Although Man City are awaiting to discover the outcome of their appeal against the Premier League's 114 charges against them, they continue to monitor the transfer market.

That is particularly the case at right-back, with Man City not having a traditional player for that position who features on a weekly basis.

According to Football Insider, Freeman is open to making the switch to the Etihad Stadium in 2027.

The 26-cap United States international has starred for Villarreal this season, and has made a total of 23 appearances since joining the Yellow Submarine in January.

Although he has a contract in place until 2032, it is suggested that the ex-Orlando City SC man would be interested in moving to the Premier League.

Whether Villarreal would entertain any offers for the 22-year-old at this point remains unclear.

That said, with Freeman having cost in the region of £5m, there is a clear opportunity to make a substantial profit.

While Matheus Nunes has made six starts in the Premier League and Champions League this season, Maresca has not settled on the Portuguese.

Abdukodir Khusanov and Rico Lewis are also options at right-back, yet they are also not viewed as long-term first-choice options.

Freeman still has much to prove given his limited high-level experience, yet being 6ft 2ins and versatile tick certain boxes with Maresca.

Man City will seemingly monitor his progression ahead of the winter transfer window.

#1942. Jamie McGrath hopeful Hibernian heroics in cup clash can lift league fortunes

Jamie McGrath hopes Hibernian’s cup heroics can help revive their wobbling William Hill Premiership campaign.

Hibs went into the Premier Sports Cup semi-final clash against Hearts at Hampden on Sunday bottom of the league, having lost four out of four against their city rivals at the national stadium and with Marink Reedijk looking for his first win as boss at the fifth attempt.

It looked like another day of disappointment was on the cards for the Leith side when Jambos attacker Claudio Braga headed in from a Calvin Miller corner with only four minutes on the clock.

However, Hibs fought back and striker Martin Boyle deservedly levelled in the 19th minute and McGrath struck three minutes before the interval with his first goal of the season to ultimately set up a meeting with Rangers in the final at the national stadium on December 13.

Hibs are one point behind second-bottom Kilmarnock ahead of the trip to Aberdeen on Saturday and McGrath, 30, said: “It was a good feeling obviously to give back to the travelling fans.

“We haven’t given them too much to shout about so far this season, so I think they would have bitten your hand off for a win in Hampden against Hearts.

“But yeah, it’s obviously a great feeling, into a cup final now, so something to look forward to.

“Hopefully now this is the start of us getting a turn on things and building on that.

“We have to get our league form back on track because that hasn’t been good enough.

“I think over the last few weeks we’ve shown what we can do in spells.

“It’s just about getting a full 90-minute performance because even on Sunday we were probably on top for a large period of game.

“I know you can’t control the full 90 minutes, but we’re still adapting to what the manager wants and I think when you see on Sunday when it clicks, it can be really, really good, but it’s about keep working hard now.

“We have to build on these small details, Every day is something new for us to be learning and we’re heavily on the video clips and we’re all buying into it. So, yeah, we’re slowly but surely getting there.”

McGrath’s crucial counter after midfielder Joe Newell’s powerful low drive had been blocked off the line and the Republic of Ireland international quickly tucked the ball in at the near post.

He said: “The ball just fell and the next thing I know it was in the back of the net so I didn’t even know how to celebrate or whatever.

“It’s obviously my first of the season, so it’s been a bit of a frustrating period for myself with a few injuries and niggles and stuff like that.

“But hopefully now we can all kind of stay as fit as we can, the squad’s kind of coming back to full fitness over the next few weeks, so hopefully it’s all clicking at the right time.”

#1941. Jack Milne delivers honest insight into Aberdeen struggles, personal battles and dressing room unity

Jack Milne has conceded this season has brought some of the toughest challenges of his career but insists Aberdeen must stick together through the difficult moments as they look to turn their fortunes around.

A narrow 1-0 defeat by Rangers in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final at Hampden left centre-back Milne contemplating another setback in a campaign mired by inconsistent performances and results, which have placed increasing scrutiny on manager Stephen Robinson.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Milne, however, believes there is a strong sense of unity within the dressing room and insists the players remain convinced they are building something positive together despite their domestic struggles.

Asked about his own experiences so far this season, Milne admitted: “I'd be lying if I said it's not been difficult. Probably one of the hardest battles of my career. I've had a lot going on and some disappointing performances. But that's football, it's got ups and downs and we’ve got to keep our heads down and get through it.”

The defender was keen to stress that his team-mates are determined not to allow the external criticism surrounding the club to undermine their collective efforts.

“We try not to pay too much attention to the outside,” he declared. “It's us as a group, as players and staff. We feel we're building something. I think every player in there feels like we're building something. It felt, even before the game [on Saturday], there was a special, special feeling brewing.

“All of us believe we're going to get a result that could turn our season around. We just need to keep working hard, stay together through the tough times and the good. Hopefully, we come out the other side of it.”

There was certainly evidence of that fighting spirit against Rangers, with Aberdeen pushing their Glasgow rivals all the way before eventually conceding seven minutes from time.

Milne felt the performance represented a significant improvement in terms of commitment and determination, despite the disappointment of missing out on a shot at Hampden glory.

“We gave it everything. I gave 100 per cent. We were down to the bare bones and I don't think there's one person in that changing room who didn't give everything today. Yeah, I'm disappointed.

“But I think there are definitely positives to take from it. The grit and determination was definitely there. We fought for every ball, every duel. On another day, we probably get a result.”

#1940. Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes showed he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward quickly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

You would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6

It was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

The misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

Manchester United Lammens (Mee 61); Dalot (Mazraoui 60), Yoro, Heaven (Armer 46), Amass (Shaw 60); Santos (Collyer 46), T Fletcher (Tielemans 61); Diallo (J Fletcher 60), Zirkzee (Cunha 60), Dorgu (Thompson 46); Mbuemo (Fernandes 60).Subs not used Heath, Honor, Lacey, Gabriel.

Leeds United Trafford (Cairns 46); Bijol (Rodon 46), Muharemovic (Cresswell 46), Bornauw; Bogle (Gnonto 46), Longstaff (Stach 46), Tanaka (Ampadu 46), Chadwick (Justin 46); James (Okafor 46), Aaronson (Wilson 46); Nmecha (Calvert-Lewin 46).Subs not used Mahady, Lienou, Mills, Piroe.

Decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

Bottom left. Manchester United win the Boyle Sports Cup.

Smacks it even higher into the top right.

And I think Amapdu’s signal means Leeds will go first.

The ref decides to call time as the stewards cannot catch the juvenile intruders.

Not sure what we can say about stadium safety here but the game has ended prematurely after five kids came on, all of whom got to Bruno Fernandes to take selfies. It was very funny but, equally, plenty on the Manchester United bench were far from happy. Penalties to follow.

Some sealion ball juggling from Mazraoui involving foot, thigh and head, gets him past Justin on the right  but Gnonto heads away his cross.

Two young Man Utd fans run on to the pitch to try to take selfies with Man utd players. They are joined by three more and now another.

Bruno Fernandes lets fly from 20 yards, cushioning a pass from Tielemans before hammering his shot into the crossbar with little backlift.

Gnonto breaks down the right, plays it infield to Wilson who runs at the heart of the Man Utd defence but smacks his shot into a defender.

Cresswell blocks Mazroui’s shot with his right elbow which was pinned to his side and the ball falls to Bruno Fernandes but Cresswell is there again to block the shot, this time with his legs. From the corner, Bruno Fernandes balloons a long shot over the bar.

Enormous frustration for the masses who have wanted a Bruno goal. He’s just “scored” - right on the moment when our friend the stadium announcer bellowed the match was a sell out but never provided the actual figure – but a linesman’s flag has stopped him in his tracks. You fancy he will have one more involvement before the game creeps towards a penalty shootout.

Bruno Fernandes shoots past Cairns with a left-foot shot from 16 yards, smacking it inside the left post but the flag had long been raised.

The ball pinballs out to Justin by the D from the corner and he hammers a shot that Mee saves with great agility by the right post.

Excellent pass from Okafor from the left ought to have put Calvert-Lewin through but Armer does brilliantly to hold him up. Gnonto makes a run down the side but Calvert-Lewin checks back to shoot into Armer and the ball deflects behind for a corner.

There will be a shootout if the match is drawn after 90 minutes. The Boyle Sports Cup cannot be shared, it seems.

Mazraoui drives down the right and feeds it inside to Fletcher whose deflected cross falls kindly for Thompson but the young striker cannot control it and Leeds recover.

Amapdu hurls a long throw into the box on the diagonal from the right. Rodon flicks it on and Calvert-Lewin dives to try to nod it past Mee but he can only stick his effort wide. It was just a bit too far in front of him to reach with control and power.

Clever pass from Gnonto sends Wilson into the box on the underlap to cross low, seeking Calvert-Lewin. Mee is out to stop it reaching him. Oakfor sets off on a  bustling run down the left for 35 yards but then fluffs the cross.
