Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in New Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have new signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

#1939. Cardinale explains what he has learned as AC Milan owner and what he still wants to achieve

Gerry Cardinale has shed some light on the ‘learning curve’ of being AC Milan’s owner, as well as some of the plans he has for the future.

It has been a bit of a different past few months for Cardinale compared to his first few years with Milan. The owner has chosen to become more hands-on in his involvement, overseeing decisions such as the managerial clear-out at the end of last season and the hiring of Ruben Amorim.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For the American, the vision remains to get Milan back to the top of Italian football. This morning he stressed in another interview that Amorim will be given time and will be backed with more signings, such is his belief that the Portuguese is the right man for the new era.

Cardinale was interviewed by ClassCNBC, a channel that broadcasts financial and economic news from around the world 24 hours a day. He spoke about various topics connected to Milan, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

What does the new stadium represent for you and the project?

“It’s a long journey: we’ve owned the club for four years and have been implementing this plan since day one, aware that to bring Milan back to where it deserves to be – at the top of Serie A and among Europe’s elite – every single aspect must be transformed: the live event, the fan experience, the infrastructure for the players.

“It’s an entire ecosystem that must be renewed and modernized to keep pace with the times. We have enormous respect for the history and culture that San Siro embodies, but our goal is to bring AC Milan back to the top.

“If we want the stadium to be a tribute to the tradition and legacy of one of the most important brands in world sport, the infrastructure and the new facility must evolve in tandem: this has been the heart of the project from day one.”

How do you protect the assets of a club like AC Milan while also projecting them into the future?

“That’s a great question; we think about it all the time. Ultimately, there’s the infrastructure, and then there’s how you bring it to life: the hardware and the software. The answer lies entirely in the software. And the software is the people, the fans, that unique energy.

“An energy that, even for an American like me, accustomed to top-level US sports, when you experience it at San Siro with the people, is unparalleled in the world. I think any American would agree.

“We can bring our strategic model, but it only works if we have a profound respect for this heritage. We engage with the community to understand what’s truly fundamental: there’s a legendary history here, and we’ll do everything we can to live up to an iconic name like San Siro.”

You talk about a ‘sports and entertainment’ platform. Where do you draw the line between the worlds of sports and entertainment?

“Sports and entertainment are increasingly intertwined. The reason? The cost of TV rights and club valuations have risen to the point that entertainment is becoming indispensable to supporting the sporting side of things.

“But the real reason we’re doing all this is to bridge the economic gap with the Premier League. The secret of European football is that the Premier League has gained a lead over the rest of the continent, and we in Europe are all in the same boat.

“It’s a general problem in sports, also present in the United States: the gap between large and small markets, between rich and less wealthy clubs, continues to widen due to media rights.

“Entertainment, if managed properly and without ever losing sight of the centrality of the pitch, is the fundamental lever for generating the resources needed to finance a competitive team.”

Will modern infrastructure be enough to bridge the gap with the Premier League, or is it primarily a cultural issue?

“It’s the sum of all things. We start from a very simple premise: Italian football absolutely needs to change, and this change must act as a driving force for the entire ecosystem.

“There’s a huge amount of work to do, and as AC Milan we have the responsibility to be the pace car, the point of reference for change and innovation. Terms that often scare many people, but which, if channeled and managed well, represent a huge benefit.

“It’s the same concept as what we’re doing in Hollywood right now: often those in power consolidate the status quo and don’t want change or innovation; they don’t wake up in the morning with a sense of urgency.

“But if you don’t do that, Netflix overwhelms Hollywood, and the Premier League takes over the continental leagues. Our work and our investment approach consist precisely in entering these ecosystems to innovate them.

“Doing so with a club like AC Milan is a great privilege and an extraordinary opportunity, because we have a profound respect for what has been, with the aim of bring it back to its past levels.”

What is the club’s financial health, considering the €50 million equity injection? Will further capital injections be needed in the future?

“What I can say is that we remain in control of our financial health. The decision to close in the red this summer was my own, made the day after we were eliminated from the Champions League, when I took direct operational control of the club.

“Looking at how things had been going over the last four years, I realied that the time had come for real change. And I wasn’t willing to implement structural changes in a matter of weeks, between the end of the season and the transfer window, as almost all clubs do.

“I didn’t want to delegate such a revolution to an external structure in such a short timeframe: these are too important organisational decisions, so I decided to intervene personally. At the same time, I chose to restructure and re-establish the sporting area.

“We have retained and developed several key players, brought in new ones, and lowered the average age of the squad. The reality is that, just as with TV rights, there has been a strong inflation in player salaries: it’s up to us to decide whether we want to compete to win, and we must accept these dynamics.

“For this year, we chose to go into the red, but we will return to the red very quickly once we have consolidated the organizational structure, managing incoming and outgoing transfer operations as best as possible, and maintaining commercial momentum.

“Recently, I have focused heavily on the sporting and football aspects, but we also bring a wealth of expertise to the business side. When we acquired the club in 2022, revenue was around €280m; we’ve increased it to over €400m, and we can still do a lot more, not least because the new stadium will provide a further, crucial boost in this direction.”

“They keep asking me questions like, ‘Are you having fun? Are you happy?’ My answer is a mixed one: I’m happy when we win, I enjoy it when we win, and right now we’re not winning enough.

“That said, this has been by far the most difficult challenge I’ve ever faced in my life, and I love challenges of this magnitude. The implications of a success here are monumental, and the ripple effect it would have for the local community, the country, the league, and the entire football landscape would be truly profound.

“The stadium, to give a concrete example, sends a message to the world and to international football of primary importance, particularly for Serie A and for Italy, precisely at a time when the movement isn’t performing up to its glorious tradition.

“For us, being able to position ourselves as a global leader with an infrastructure of this kind and with what it represents for the future is a fundamental objective.”

Do you intend to move forward by personally managing every aspect of the club, or do you think the club and the sports structure need a strong management figure, a technical director?

“That’s a great question. I wanted to clarify two key points. First, I will never hand over the keys to anyone again. From now on, I will always be operational and present in person. This is too important, and I can make too great a contribution, for that not to be the case.

“Second, however, is that I intend to do what I do best: one of my main tasks is organizational design, and our goal is to build a world-class football organization.

“Given what we represent and AC Milan’s history, we must be able to attract the best professionals on the market, and that’s exactly what we will do. So, we will continue to do both.”

Do you already have a specific name or profile in mind?

“It’s a question I get asked all the time. But it’s not just about naming names, and it’s curious how in football discussions, people always look for scoops on individual figures. I say that what really matters is the planning, the organizational architecture, what we’re building.

“As for names, I can only say that yes, I have some profiles in mind, but they will only become operational within and in accordance with the corporate model we’re designing, and that’s what I’m totally focused on.”

Do you also have player names in mind? Is he becoming increasingly expert in the art of selecting and acquiring players?

“Well, yes. If you’d told me a year ago that I’d be spending my time watching videos, interacting with scouts and our technical staff, I’d have been quite surprised, but it’s something that’s gotten under my skin now.

“The learning curve has been incredibly steep, but then again, if you look at what I’ve done with RedBird and throughout my career, it’s always been about building organizations made up of top-notch people.

“It means knowing how to negotiate, knowing how to manage financial considerations, making sure people are all pulling in the same direction to achieve the set goal. That’s exactly what football thrives on, and that’s what determines its success.

“It’s no different from what we do in the corporate world. It’s about doing things the right way, building a solid organization: and it’s not enough to win, it’s not enough to have a big name at the moment, you have to do it consistently.

“It means creating a structure that can constantly evolve, because the world doesn’t just sit back and wait for you. The Premier League will continue to grow stronger, and our job is to is keeping up.”

Looking back, how do you evaluate these four years at Milan? What were the things you did well, and what were the mistakes you wouldn’t repeat?

“Hindsight is wonderful, as we all know. If I could start over again, I’d like to have the same awareness I’ve gained over the past four years. When we bought the club four years ago, it had just won the Scudetto, and I thought the sporting and footballing aspects were already in place and working perfectly; so I focused on other priorities, like the new stadium and commercial development.

“The reality is that you have to take care of both things simultaneously, and you can’t take it for granted that the pitch is in order. So, if I could go back, as steep as the learning curve was, I would have dedicated the same amount of time to the sporting aspect from day one as I am now.

“But the advantage of having taken this path is that today I perfectly understand what needs to be done. The time I spent this summer personally managing the club gave me the opportunity to understand exactly which roles to include in the new technical area structure.

“I would take care of the commercial side with my eyes closed; the world of football, however, has its own art and science component, and now I’ve finally climbed that ladder. learning curve. Putting these two elements together, the sum of the parts will be significantly greater than the whole.”

#1938. Queens Park Rangers vs Burnley - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 01 Nov 2026 13:00

Queens Park Rangers will be looking to bounce back when they welcome Burnley to Loftus Road on Tuesday evening.

The hosts currently sit ninth in the Championship table, while the visitors are 22nd.

QPR will be eager to respond after a 4-1 defeat at Southampton on Saturday, which followed an emphatic 5-0 home victory over Swansea City a week earlier.

Richard Kone scored four goals across those two matches, having struck a hat-trick against the Swans, and the R's have now found the back of the net 10 times in their last four league outings.

However, they have also conceded eight goals in that same time and head coach Julien Stephan will be keen to shore up his backline.

QPR are in the running for promotion this season and sit just two points off the playoffs, meaning they could move into the top eight if results go their way on Tuesday.

Burnley, meanwhile, remain in the bottom three after a goalless draw with Portsmouth in Fabio Celestini's first match in charge.

The Clarets were frustrated by Portsmouth's defence, taking a total of 18 shots as they looked to pick up a first home win of the season.

Celestini praised his side's "spirit" after the game, calling the performance a "first step but not enough".

That clean sheet was an improvement after Burnley were thumped 4-1 by Lincoln in what proved to be Nicky Hayen's final game in charge, but they must start to make dramatic changes.

Burnley have managed just one victory all season, but could move out of the relegation zone if they win and Watford lose on Tuesday.

QPR will be hoping Kone can continue his good form up front alongside Paul Smyth.

Kwame Poku and Harvey Vale are expected to start out wide, while Glen Kamara and Jonathan Varane should continue their midfield partnership.

Burnley will be keen for veteran striker Jamie Vardy to find some form, having managed just one goal in six games so far, and he is expected to lead the line.

Largie Ramazani and Marcus Edwards could continue out wide, with Andreas Hountondji, Reo Hatate and Josh Laurent set to start in midfield.

Queens Park Rangers possible starting lineup:

Charles; Adamson, Edwards, Dunne, Kemper; Poku, Varane, Kamara, Vale; Smyth, Kone

Coudert; Walker, Ekdal, Julio, Pires; Hatate, Hountondji; Edwards, Laurent, Ramazani; Vardy

QPR are an unpredictable team at the moment, while Burnley have entered a new era under Celestini. However, QPR should have enough attacking quality to beat a Burnley side that has only picked up one win all season.

#1937. James Penrice expecting '10 times’ the joy if Rangers lift Premier Sports Cup

James Penrice enjoyed Rangers’ Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Aberdeen but believes the winning feeling will multiply by 10 if they win the final.

The Light Blues registered a 1-0 victory at Barclays Hampden on Saturday thanks to a late but deserved goal from striker Ryan Naderi, who pounced on a strike towards goal from Penrice to direct the ball into the net from six yards.

Gers players took the acclaim of their fans at the end after confirming Derek McInnes’ first final as boss, with Rangers facing Hibernian at the national stadium on December 13 after the Hibees beat city rivals Hearts 2-1 on Sunday.

Penrice, on loan from Super League Greece side AEK Athens, said: “I think it’s special seeing boys that haven’t seen the kind of scenes before, haven’t seen Rangers at Hampden.

“I think it can only help. And I think it will be 10 times that if you were to come back here and win it in six weeks.

“So the motivation for the boys is to relive that again, 10 times that.

“And I think that’s what we’ll be trying to put into the group and it can only help us.”

Penrice admits his decision to join the Ibrox side in the summer was vindicated – albeit there had been no hesitation.

The former Partick Thistle, Livingston and Hearts left-back said: “It was never in doubt. Never.

“It was the only place I wanted to go in the summer. And I pushed a hell of a lot.

“This is why I want to come here and play for a massive club and play in games like a final. It only backs up my decision.”

It was not a classic display from Rangers, especially in a low-quality first half but Penrice stressed the importance of digging deep to get results.

He said: “I think that’s what it is. We’d love to be knocking the ball about and score six or seven goals, but sometimes that doesn’t happen.

“Teams come and they sit lower and they make it hard for us.

“At Rangers, that’s going to happen. You need to score goals. I think it’s just that final bit. The final pass, the final shot. I think composure in front of goal. But I can’t complain.

“The boys ran themselves into the ground and I think big Ryan gets his striker’s goal and it’s a massive positive.”

Although he had been pushed into midfield at times in previous games, Penrice started alongside Nico Raskin in the Gers engine room in a tactical move by McInnes which raised some eyebrows.

However, Penrice took it in his stride, saying: “It was obviously not what I’ve been used to in a two. But when the gaffer says play there, there’s no question, I’ll play wherever.

“Whatever I can do to help the team is what I’ll do.

“Obviously, it’s not a position I’ve played in before in the past for Livingstone and Partick.

“But if he asks me to play in there, I’m going to say yes. I could play anywhere.”

#1936. Hibs bullish over Rangers final as Hearts boss enters uncharted territory

Hibs head coach Marink Reedijk has backed his team to produce another Premier Sports Cup final upset when they face Rangers next month after making history against Hearts.

Written off by many ahead of Sunday’s semi-final against their Edinburgh rivals, Hibs recovered from the concession of a fourth-minute opening goal to win 2-1 and defeat Hearts for the very first time at Hampden Park.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Goals from Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath in an action-packed first half wiped out Claudio Braga’s early header and while Hearts pressed hard for a leveller in the second half, Hibs held firm to set up a December 13 final clash against Rangers.

Hibs will be underdogs once more when they return to the national stadium but Reedijk, who got his first Hibs win at the fifth time of asking, believes his players have shown what they are made of by winning a derby of such magnitude.

Asked what makes him confident Hibs can lift the trophy, Reedijk said: “The performance of today and the performance we showed the week before. And if we have more progression, we progress even better and better and better.

“We can make every opponent's lives a little bit difficult or very difficult. And no matter which team it is, it's always another match to play. Finals are, again, special matches, but also finals are not only based on these special moments.

“It's also about teams with a plan and teams with an idea. And I think if we build on what we are doing now, keep on going and it will have ups and downs. I know I have a really good belief that we also can do something in the final.”

Reedijk was full of praise for his veteran midfielder Joe Newell, who started for the third time in a week and won the man of the match award.

“For Joe, I can only take my hat how he copes with the fact that we play three matches in the week. And now it's not only about that he can cope with three matches in the week, but also the performances he put on the pitch. And today was important with the two goals.

“And I'm very happy for him as well because he came from a long injury history and without playing. And how he puts himself full, that's really good to see.”

Reedijk revelled in watching his players listen to a rendition of Sunshine on Leith from Hibs supporters afterwards and said he was moved by the scenes.

“I'm not always showing my emotions, but it's really touching,” admitted Reedijk. “So maybe it looks like I'm an ice king, so to say.

“Normally in Holland we say ice queen, but therefore an ice king because I'm not a woman. But for me, it is really important that this happens and it comes close to my heart because this is what football is about. Guys who inspire people on the pitch with something people off the pitch and in the stands love to see.

For Hearts manager Wouter Vrancken, it was a painful afternoon - exacerbated by the loss of two more players through injury.

Hearts went into the match without eight first-team regulars and had to replace Tomas Magnusson (suspected concussion) and Calvin Miller (knee) before the first half was out. Vrancken revealed he has never had to deal with an injury crisis of such magnitude.

“Nothing like this. Not even close,” said the Belgian. “I didn't see Tomas because Tomas is to the hospital. Calvin was in a brace but it's always difficult to say directly after the game. So we have to wait for a scan on Monday or the day after.

“The doctor and medical staff, they did their concussion test on the pitch, at that moment. Tomas passed the concussion test and then he came to me to come in.

“Then he was going left and right, he couldn't stand on his legs anymore. When I saw it, there's no doubt in your head that you're going to let him on the pitch at that moment, because you cannot take the risk. Then he saw it himself also at the moment. He said, 'no, I can't do it. And then we had to change him, and now he's to the hospital, so I don't know.”

Hearts now head to Switzerland to face FC Thun in the Conference League and will need to pick themselves up after such a painful result. They have yet to win in the main phase and need a positive result to maintain hopes of progressing to knock-out stages.

"Really sore and disappointed of course, especially when you see the game going on, how the game was going on,” continued Vrancken. “We didn't have to go this way because we had control of the game when we started. I think it started with the moment that Tomas was injured, that's clear, and afterwards Calvin.

“And those two changes, I'm not pointing out the guys who came in, for sure not, but these changes get us out of the rhythm and because of the connections. Maybe not top in the duels because we were really strong in these duels. These first moments and second balls, picked up those second balls, finding the right spaces.

“Then you lose these profiles, and then it's searching again, and then hesitations. Sometimes we gave them too much space and then you lose actually the game in those 20 minutes, I'd say. Because then when you get to half-time, you can adjust some things and get the hesitations out of the game and be clear on those things.

“Also in possession, especially with the profiles on the pitch, we had to go more from possession and then it was much better. Then we dominated the game again and it's just a pity that they didn't get rewarded. They had a lot of knocks already, mentally and emotionally, also today. You just hope that they get rewarded for fighting hard and it's a pity, especially in such a game, of course."

#1935. Official: Christian Pulisic signs contract renewal with AC Milan until 2031

AC Milan have announced the contract renewal of Christian Pulisic, tying the American star to the club until 2031.

On Tuesday this week, the news broke that Pulisic’s contract renewal was imminent after ‘an agreement in principle’ had been reached between the parties. Sure enough, the No.11 arrived at Casa Milan yesterday to sign his new deal with the club.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As we highlighted in our latest newsletter, as Pulisic still benefits from the Growth Decree, the reported pay rise from €4m to €5m will not cost them a fortune. As opposed to €9.25m gross without the Decree, they will pay €6.55m.

On their website this afternoon, Milan announced the long-awaited news and confirmed that the new contract will run until 2031.

“AC Milan is pleased to announce that Christian Pulisic has extended his contract with the Club through June 30th, 2031.

“Since joining the Rossoneri in July 2023, Christian has established himself as a key member of the team, standing out for his technical ability, character, consistency and unwavering work ethic. His 44 goals in 141 appearances for the Rossoneri highlight both his importance to the team and his role in the Club’s future plans.

“Pulisic’s contract extension reflects a shared commitment to building on the progress made together in recent years, with the ambition to keep improving, achieve new milestones and write more memorable chapters in the Club’s history,” the statement reads.

With 44 goals and 28 assists in 144 games to his name, the 28-year-old has been a key player in the last few seasons and Milan believe that he’s about to enter his prime years. Securing the renewal was thus an important step forward for the club’s entire project.

#1934. Feyenoord vs Inter Milan - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 01 Nov 2026 13:50, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 13:55

Level on three points apiece from three games, Feyenoord and Inter Milan must go for victory when they meet in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

Approaching the midpoint of this season's league phase, the two former European champions are at risk of elimination before they clash at De Kuip.

Facing a fight to reach the Champions League's knockout stage, Inter hardly warmed up for their trip to Rotterdam in ideal style.

Instead, the Nerazzurri were well beaten by AC Milan in Saturday's Derby della Madonnina, making it eight straight second-city derbies without a win.

Inter recently came from behind for the fifth time in eight league games when they dramatically beat Fiorentina, but they failed to complete such a comeback against their fierce city rivals.

With illness sweeping through Cristian Chivu's squad, those left standing were left powerless to resist as the Rossoneri surged into an early two-goal lead and eventually won 3-1.

Now trailing behind surprise Serie A leaders Lazio - and Milan are within four points - Chivu's side must swiftly switch focus to their continental campaign.

After departing at the first knockout round last season - losing both playoff legs to Bodo/Glimt - Inter had started this term with a 2-1 reverse to old boss Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid.

Then, after suffering a shock 4-3 defeat to Club Brugge at San Siro, they finally got off the mark with a tense 1-0 win over Shakhtar Donetsk, despite being reduced to 10 men.

Beaten seven times in their last nine Champions League fixtures, the 2023 and 2025 runners-up are under pressure to improve; Chivu's personal record at the elite level still features more losses than wins.

At least history will be on their side when they travel to De Kuip: since losing their first game against Dutch opponents - to Ajax in the 1972 European Cup final - Inter have won 10 out of 14 without tasting defeat.

Enjoying their third Champions League campaign in the space of four seasons, Feyenoord reached the knockout phase in 2024-25, initially knocking out Milan before falling to Inter in the round of 16.

The only other meeting saw Feyenoord go through, as they won 3-2 on aggregate in the 2001-02 UEFA Cup semi-finals, before going on to lift the trophy.

Like Inter, they come into this clash with just three points on the board: Giovanni van Bronckhorst's side started with a 5-1 loss in Barcelona, then followed up with a 3-2 home victory over Como, but they lost 1-0 away to Real Betis last time out.

The Dutch club have now lost 10 of their last 13 major European matches, while Van Bronckhorst has won just two out of 15 in his Champions League management career.

That dismal record features no clean sheets and 13 defeats, but both wins have been at home to Italian teams: 2-1 against Napoli during his first spell in charge, and against Como on matchday two.

Domestic results have been more positive, though. Distant runners-up to PSV last term, Feyenoord retained top spot in the Eredivisie on Saturday despite settling for a 1-1 draw with Fortuna Sittard.

Still unbeaten at De Kuip across all competitions, they can now welcome one of Europe's traditional giants to their intimidating home ground.

As well as captain Lautaro Martinez, Inter's injury list currently includes Luis Henrique and Benjamin Pavard, plus English pair John Stones and Curtis Jones.

While Alessandro Bastoni scored in the Milan derby, he must now serve a UEFA ban for his red card against Shakhtar.

Ever versatile, Carlos Augusto could fill in. Including his late winner last time out, the Brazilian has been directly involved in five goals from his last eight Champions League starts.

When these sides met in March 2025, Marcus Thuram and Hakan Calhanoglu were both on the scoresheet; with Martinez absent, either Pio Esposito or Ange Bonny should partner Thuram up front - providing they recover from illness.

Feyenoord have made the fewest changes to their starting XI in this season's Champions League - just one so far - and Van Bronckorst is unlikely to divert from that path on Tuesday night.

Long-term absentees Bart Nieuwkoop, Jordan Bos and Thomas Beelen remain sidelined, and Jeremiah St. Juste is a doubt, but Gijs Smal, Reiss Nelson and Shaqueel van Persie could all return, having recently resumed full training.

One of three Feyenoord forwards with at least seven goal involvements this season - alongside Nacho Ferri and captain Luciano Valente - wing wizard Anis Hadj Moussa has attempted the most shots following a carry in the Champions League so far (10).

Ernst; Read, Watanabe, Marmol, Lopez; Zechiel, Vanhoutte, Targhalline; Hadj Moussa, Ferri, Valente

J. Martinez; Bisseck, Akanji, Augusto; Diouf, Barella, Calhanoglu, Zielinski, Dimarco; Thuram, Esposito

Given their strong home record and Inter's defensive woes, Feyenoord will take at least one point from their fourth Champions League fixture.

The hosts are not watertight themselves, though, and their visitors still possess plenty of firepower, which should make for a very entertaining contest.

#1933. Celtic Fans Collective demand Dermot Desmond attend AGM in person and face scrutiny

Celtic Fans Collective have called on Dermot Desmond to attend the upcoming Celtic AGM in person.

The supporter group issued a lengthy statement demanding that the Parkhead shareholder show up to the event in person to face scrutiny over boardroom decisions.

The group claims Desmond wields "considerable influence over the direction and decision-making" at the club and must "answer questions about his role".

A Celtic Fans Collective statement read: "For twenty years, Dermot Desmond has not attended Celtic's Annual General Meeting, despite wielding considerable influence over the direction and decision-making of our club.

"Although only a minority shareholder, Desmond appears to exercise influence far beyond his shareholding. With that influence comes a responsibility to be accountable.

"We call on Dermot Desmond to publicly commit to attending the 2026 AGM in person and answer questions about his role in the running of Celtic Football Club.

"Sending his son, another representative or a prepared statement in his place is no substitute for attending personally.

"The decision by Peter Lawwell to prematurely conclude last year's AGM left a clear impression among supporters that the Board had taken an opportunity to avoid scrutiny. Responsibility for how that meeting was conducted and ultimately concluded rests entirely with the Board.

"This year, however, the focus must be firmly on scrutiny rather than protest. There is a clear understanding across the support that the AGM must provide the opportunity for important questions to be put directly to those running the Club, without allowing scrutiny to be evaded once again.

"Celtic supporters have repeatedly sought meaningful dialogue and a more constructive relationship with the Club.

"At a time when fans want to see decisive leadership, a public commitment from Dermot Desmond to attend the AGM in good faith would be an important demonstration of his willingness to engage directly with supporters and shareholders."

Celtic Trust added: "As a Non-Executive Director of the Club, it is the duty of Dermot Desmond to attend the 2026 Celtic PLC AGM.

"He has been absent from these meetings for 20 years - refusing to face and answer questions from shareholders.

"He should commit to ending that absence this year."

#1932. Hibs shed Hearts Hampden baggage as club gets vitamin pill it so desperately needed

Oh how Hibs needed this moment. Struggling under new head coach Marink Reedijk and serially oppressed by Hearts at Hampden this century, they spectacularly turned the tables with this 2-1 Edinburgh derby victory to set up a Premier Sports final date with Rangers next month.

Hibs arrived at the national stadium with a lorryload of baggage against this opponent here and plenty of doubters. Hearts were odds-on to deliver a fifth victory over their neighbours at Hampden and despite taking a fourth-minute lead through Claudio Braga, they unravelled in the first half and could not find a way back in the second period.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

This was a historic moment for Hibs - and potentially a watershed one for a club that has had little to shout about this season. They sacked David Gray in September and brought in 35-year-old Dutchman Marink Reedijk, whose four matches prior to facing Hearts read three defeats and one draw. They went into this match bottom of the Premiership.

Hibs did not play like a team flirting with relegation. They showed admirable courage to recover from an early set-back and seized upon a Hearts team that never took control of proceedings and suffered from two first-half injuries to Tomas Magnusson and Calvin Miller.

Reedijk got his team selection and tactics spot-on in a first-ever win over Hearts at Hampden. His midfield engine of the excellent Joe Newell, Miguel Chaiwa and Josh Mulligan played with purpose and energy. They pressed Hearts at the right moments and the deployment of Martin Boyle in the unfamiliar left-wing role to capitalise on the weakest sector of the Jambos' team was a feather in Reedijk's cap.

Hibs had to dig in. Hearts flooded forward in the second half in search of a leveller after Hibs took a 2-1 lead to the sheds. They bombarded the Hibs penalty box but the two centre-halves in Jason Kerr and Marko Ivezic held firm. When goalkeeper Raphael Sallinger was called upon, he was solid. Heroes in green and white everywhere.

None more so than Boyle, who battled illness all week ahead of the match and was restored to the starting XI. His equaliser on 19 minutes was his sixth career goal against Hearts and Hibs looked a better team for his presence.

Reedijk contended pre-match that Hibs had improved game-on-game since he took over. Wednesday's 1-1 draw at St Mirren was ugly but this win was beautiful for Hibs, so beautiful for the 19,000-plus fans who made the journey to Hampden.

Hibs did not sell out their allocation. Sunshine and Leith was belted out after the final whistle, players and fans reunited after weeks of disharmony, where ultras group Block 7 have been banned and pelters thrown at the club's hierarchy.

A penny for the thoughts of sporting director Malky Mackay, who has been savaged by some sections of Hibs fanbase for recruitment over the summer. He and the board have a final to look forward to.

This should also act as the biggest vitamin pill for Reedijk, who has changed the way Hibs play. They commit more men forward, press higher and take risks. It had not paid off prior to visiting Hampden but a win of such magnitude should surely supercharge those in the Hibs dressing room.

It was another sobering afternoon in Glasgow for Hearts, whose last two visits were a 7-1 trouncing by Celtic and that cataclysmic title loss to the same team back in May. Hopes were high that Wouter Vrancken's side could be the one to end the club's long wait for the League Cup - they have not won it since 1962 - but they find new ways to inflict pain on the fanbase when it comes to this competition.

Too many Hearts players just didn't hit their stride. Braga's header on four minutes, a simple finish after a lush delivery from Miller, was the perfect start, but for the rest of the first half they toiled with Hibs' aggressiveness and energy.

Hearts' heavy schedule caught up with them. Eight first-team players missed this game due to injury and competing on three fronts, Magnusson and Miller were the latest to be added to the list. Magnusson suffered a head knock in a challenge with Jason Kerr and could not continue, while the influential Miller pulled up clutching his hamstring and last 37 minutes. The playmaker in particular was a huge miss.

Even still, there was enough in Hearts' armoury to make a fist of things. But whether it was heavy legs or the sheer desire of the Hibs players, whose work off the ball was impeccable, the rest of the opening 45 minutes belonged to Hibs. Boyle scurried on to Owen Elding's clipped ball over the Hearst defence to net via keeper Beau Reus and the post on 19 minutes and then three minutes before the interval, McGrath slotted home after Newell's fierce drive was blocked.

Vrancken has won plaudits for the way Hearts have attacked this season, but defensive fragility remains a hallmark of this team. Hibs were able to capitalise on space in behind their rivals and remained a threat after the break, although it was at the other end where they really excelled.

Hearts chucked bodies forward and all manner of crosses were flung into the box. Josh McPake was their chief outlet but bar one ball that was fizzed dangerously across the face of the Hibs goal, there wasn't enough quality. Sallinger made two smart saves from Braga and Laurent Mendy. They stood tall when many would have backed them to fold.

The full-time scenes will live long in the memory of Hibs supporters. Sunshine on Leith blared loudly over the tannoy as, arm in arm, the players took the acclaim of their adoring faithful.

After missing out agonisingly on the Conference League, after losing the first derby of the season at Easter Road, after parting company with a club legend, after sliding down the table, this was the historic result Hibs craved. They will now hope it is the catalyst for more success.

Manchester United are reportedly giving consideration to making an approach for Al-Ahli forward Ivan Toney in the winter transfer window.

Acquiring someone like Toney feels like the ideal move from United's perspective, particularly when they have not kept a Premier League clean sheet this season.

#1930. Game management, more physicality and a much-needed win: Talking points from Crawley Town's win at Oldham

Crawley battled against an Oldham side that played with nine men for the best part of an hour as referee David Rock reached for his back pocket twice in the first half.

The Reds capitalised early into the second half before seeing out the game to take all three points of fellow League Two strugglers for the first time since the second game of the season and close the gap to those in front - here are four talking points from the 0-1 win.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

There have been a lot of questions about a lack of experience in this Crawley side this season and that resulting in a mismanagement of important moments in games, which has seen the Reds drop many points so far this season.

To some extent yesterday’s game put some of those doubts to bed despite it being against a nine man Oldham side. For a side that have won just one game all season the fact that Crawley were able to see out the game is much greater of an achievement in context of the season rather than just solely looking at this game.

It can be much harder than most people expect to face a team that is reduced to nine men because naturally they are going to sit in a low block, soak up pressure and aim to counter and score from set pieces.

The Reds weren’t able to put the game to bed but came away with the three points albeit a narrow 0-1 win and at times it felt as though Crawley were the ones that had nine men and were holding on.

In the context of the season this could be a massive three points for Crawley and certainly a platform to build whether you consider the performance or not. It was vitally important that they closed the gap to those in front of them sooner rather than later.

Their victory at Oldham makes it just their second win in the league all season and with the majority of results going Crawley’s way they have been able to close the gap to three points and also have one even two games in hand on some teams.

One notable element that was evident Crawley were particularly lacking in was a more bodily presence. The Reds came up against a very physical side in Oldham with Blackwell emphasising that in his post-match interview saying that he only had Priestley Farquharson that matched the presence of the likes of Mike Fondop, Donervon Daniels and Manny Monthe.

Especially with Oldham down to nine they were always going to sit deep, therefore Crawley would have a lot more opportunity to put the ball into the box however with their strength and height more often than not they made first contact and were able to clear any danger.

#1929. I watched Celtic lose to Falkirk and noted telling Chris Sutton comments and a magic wand in decline

Celtic lost for the second time in the league this season as they were beaten 2-0 away to a Falkirk side who celebrated victory in this fixture for the first time since 2007.

The champions were unable to stretch their lead at the top of the Premiership, with nearest challengers Rangers on Premier Sports Cup duty.

Here are a few talking points from the match:

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sitting four points clear at the top just weeks after a 7-1 thrashing of a title rival wouldn’t usually be the sort of scenario worthy of cracked crests and furrowed brows. But there is something evidently deeply wrong with Celtic at this moment and it’s not entirely clear how to fix it.

Coming from behind to defeat Hibs and draw with Dundee United had helped to paper over the cracks but there would be no victory on this occasion to mask another under-par performance. Celtic gifted Falkirk an early goal and then were easily cut open for the second, while missing a raft of chances at the other end.

The statistics make for grim reading. They have now won just three of their last 10 games in all competitions, losing six of them. European football has become a burden rather than a pleasure, ever since the Champions League capitulation to LASK. The Europa League visit of Besiktas to Celtic Park on Thursday now becomes an occasion to be feared and not excitedly anticipated.

Martin O’Neill saved their bacon last season – twice – but seems to have lost his magic touch. Team selections alter every week, while half-time substitutions – often to fix tactical failings - are now commonplace. When even someone like Chris Sutton, so often an O’Neill ally, says on television that Celtic are “in regression” as a club then it just underlines the fact that all is not well.

A parting of the ways between manager and club now seems inevitable but it remains to be seen which party chooses to cut the cord first and when.

No team has scored more than Celtic’s 27 goals in the Premiership this season but that tally could and should be a lot higher. They were especially wasteful against Falkirk, offloading 24 shots, landing nine on target but failing to score with any of them.

Falkirk goalkeeper Scott Bain played the game of his life but, even still, there was a wastefulness about Celtic. Camilo Duran started through the middle but couldn’t finish any of the opportunities that came his way. Callum Osmand was removed at half-time after failing to make any significant contribution down the left, Haissem Hassan spent most of the game looking for fouls and throwing tantrums while Kasper Hogh made a negligible impact off the bench.

At 64, John McGlynn is just a year older than Jose Mourinho, recently appointed as Real Madrid manager, and Everton boss David Moyes. And yet there never seems to be much clamour around the Falkirk manager whenever vacancies crop up despite his incredible record in the last few years in steering the Bairns from League One to the giddy heights of fourth in the Premiership.

Appointing younger managers seems to be all the rage these days – Craig McLeish, Marink Reedijk and Alfred Johansson are all still in their 30s – but it feels like McGlynn deserves greater recognition of what he’s achieved, regardless of age.

This weekend, AC Milan will have to do without Fikayo Tomori, with the English defender suffering an injury against Bologna.

Although they have not helped themselves – with limited depth available to Ruben Amorim – Milan are in a defensive crisis reminiscent of the 2024/25 season. Indeed, the injuries at the back are constant and even back-ups are now struggling.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Tomori wasn’t considered a part of the team until the start of the season, being reintroduced in case of injury to any first-teamers. Now, though, he has fallen to the same crisis that has affected his teammates.

As MilanNews reports, Tomori will now be absent for a period after suffering a medial flexor muscle injury in his right thigh. Unfortunately, it seems it could be a while until he’s back for the Rossoneri, with a check-up scheduled in two weeks’ time.

#1927. Steve Herbert: Let's hope this sorry season is about to come good

It’s taken two months but Crawley Town have finally felt that winning feeling again in the league.

A huge three points were earned at Boundary Park last weekend when a Danilo Orsi goal in the fifty second minute sent the three points back to West Sussex. It was a hard earned victory, and a tough watch, but the boys got the job done. Helped by the fact the Latics were reduced to nine men by halftime after two of their players had received marching orders. A lot of fans then presumed the Reds would go on and win quite comfortably, but that’s not how football works.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Think back to the beginning of August and our home game with Crewe, when we ourselves were reduced to nine men after Gordon and Ebiowei were sent off. It took the opposition a while to break us down, and when they did the goal was a huge slice of luck.

It was a similar story at Oldham but this time it was on the opposite foot. What was impressive was the managerial decision by interim boss Kevin Blackwell to substitute Kai Jennings in the first half after he’d picked up a yellow card. The referee was probably desperate to reduce the arrears. So by taking the player off it stopped the referee from making that happen and with it we kept eleven versus nine and the win was sealed. Clearly the locals weren’t happy and at full time an Oldham fan launched a crutch at the referee! Yes you have read that right, how the supporter made it home is anyone’s guess.

The success puts us to within three points of safety with a huge six pointer coming up at Rotherham on Saturday week. But prior to that our attention turns to the FA Cup and a trip to Dorset to face non league opponents in Wimborne Town. The tie has been moved to a Sunday and live tv, obviously because it reads FA Cup shock all over it. Wimborne Town FC have even built a new terrace on one side of the ground ahead of the game. After trips to Maidenhead United and Borehamwood in recent seasons, this is yet another cracking game to look forward to, and in all honesty we should be doing everything we can to make sure we make it to the second round. That’s where we can all start dreaming of progressing to face the big boys of the Premier League in round three.

What it also gives everyone is a nice distraction from a disastrous start to our League Two campaign.

Although after the win at Oldham let’s hope this sorry season is about to come good. See you all in Dorset on Sunday Reds fans.

#1926. Liverpool vs. Arsenal lineups confirmed as major Trey Nyoni, Christos Tzolis, Dominik Szoboszlai calls made

By Ben Knapton | 01 Nov 2026 15:18, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 15:27

Liverpool and Arsenal have confirmed their starting lineups for Sunday's Premier League main event at Anfield.

Reds boss Andoni Iraola has made seven changes to the team that beat Chelsea in the EFL Cup in midweek, but one of the four starters from that clash - Trey Nyoni - keeps his place for a momentous full Premier League debut.

The 19-year-old has been given the nod over Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, the latter of whom is only fit enough for the bench after recovering from a hamstring setback.

Nyoni and Alexis Mac Allister will operate behind the expected front four of Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak, with Victor Munoz also among the substitutes following a knee problem.

Iraola has also made an expected three changes in defence, where Joe Gomez, Kostas Tsimikas and Giorgi Mamardashvili drop out for Ronald Araujo, Milos Kerkez and Alisson Becker.

Team news is IN! ✊? #LIVARS https://t.co/f9Zy0zK7sx

Meanwhile, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has made nine changes from Tuesday's EFL Cup loss to Fleetwood Town, with Kai Havertz and Jurrien Timber the only players to retain their spots.

Havertz is given the nod as the number nine over Viktor Gyokeres and is part of an attack also featuring Christos Tzolis, who makes his first Arsenal appearance since September 19 following a hamstring injury, and Noni Madueke, who is fine after an ankle issue.

Declan Rice is unsurprisingly fit to start in midfield despite a hamstring scare and joins up with Bruno Guimaraes, while Riccardo Calafiori has also shaken off a knock to replace Piero Hincapie at left-back.

On the opposite side, Timber - preferred to Ben White - makes just his second Premier League start of the season, while Ezri Konsa, Gabriel Magalhaes and David Raya all return too.

Arsenal start the day three places and six points above Liverpool in the Premier League table, and the Gunners will leapfrog Manchester City into top spot with a draw or a victory at Anfield.

Meanwhile, the fifth-placed Reds are one point adrift of fourth-placed Chelsea, but Iraola's men need to win to overtake the Blues - and move to within three points of Arsenal and Man City - due to their inferior goal difference to Xabi Alonso's side.

#1925. Why Rangers must turn late semi-final heroics into platform for success as Hampden return vindicates transfer

Rangers have spent much of the season searching for consistency, but their latest visit to Hampden provided further evidence that Derek McInnes’ squad are beginning to understand what is required when the pressure is at its highest.

Following the statement victory over Celtic in the Premier Sports Cup quarter-final, there was an expectation that Rangers would carry that momentum into their last-four meeting with Aberdeen. They duly delivered, although the nature of their narrow 1-0 triumph in Mount Florida was perhaps more indicative of the qualities required to win trophies than any display of attacking flair.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It was not an evening for extravagance. Instead, Rangers had to show patience, determination and the mental strength to keep searching for a breakthrough. That moment eventually arrived in the 83rd minute through Ryan Naderi and the man who provided the assist, James Penrice, believes such attributes are becoming increasingly evident within the squad and are helping to foster a winning mentality.

“When you're on the pitch and you play for Rangers, you should go until the end of the game,” he said. “You've seen that a couple of times. The resilience to keep going to the end, keep pushing. They made it very hard for us, but I think we got our reward. Ryan gets his strikers goal and it's a massive positive.”

Having already swept Celtic aside, Rangers knew the importance of backing up that emphatic 3-0 victory. Defeat in the semi-final against a struggling Dons side would have undermined much of the positivity generated by their quarter-final success, making the assignment another significant test of their character and credentials.

Penrice acknowledged that reaching Hampden was particularly important for those members of the squad experiencing such an occasion for the first time. He believes the occasion will provide added motivation ahead of their return to the national stadium in six weeks’ time, when they will be expected to justify their favourites' billing against Hibs.

“That was big. For a lot of the boys, it's their first time being at Hampden,” stated the 27-year-old. “It's massive that they experience that and it will help them want it more. It's special seeing boys that haven't seen those kind of scenes before, haven't seen Rangers at Hampden. It can only help us, and I think it will be ten times that if you were to come back here and win it. So that's the motivation for the boys is to relive that again.”

That appetite for success could prove a major factor in the weeks ahead. Rangers now have another outing at Hampden to anticipate in mid-December, but former Hearts man Penrice is under no illusion that reaching the final guarantees anyone a place in the starting XI. Quite the opposite, in fact.

With several players edging closer to a return from injury, competition for places is expected to intensify, ensuring nobody can afford to become complacent. It is a scenario Penrice welcomes.

“When you come back here in six weeks, everyone should be pushing. Pushing to try and get in the starting 11, pushing to get on the bench,” he explained. “You need two or three players in each position fighting for a jersey. And good enough to fight for a jersey. All wanting to win, all wanting to play and I think that's the main thing.”

Penrice has also shown a willingness to embrace a different challenge, having been deployed in midfield on a couple of occasions despite being more accustomed to operating in defence. His readiness to adapt to an unfamiliar role underlines his determination to contribute wherever required.

“It was obviously not what I've been used to in a two. But when the gaffer says play there, there's no question I'll play wherever,” he declared. “Whatever I can do to help the team is what I'll do. Obviously, it's not a position I've played in before in the past for Livingston and Partick. But if he asks me to play in there, I'm going to say yes. I could play anywhere.”

That mentality will be essential. While being favourites to lift the trophy inevitably brings expectation, it also carries responsibility, and having negotiated the semi-final hurdle, they must now prove they can deliver when silverware is at stake.

Reaching a cup final so early in his Ibrox career offered Penrice further confirmation that his decision to move to Ibrox from AEK Athens in the summer was the right one.

“It was never in doubt. Never,” he exclaimed. “It was the only place I wanted to go in the summer. And I pushed hell of a lot. This is why I wanted to come here and play for a massive club and play in games like a final. It only backs up my decision.”

#1924. Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn

An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

The visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU

Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq

Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK

Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

“I think it is a really harsh one. He [the referee] has to be sure at such a critical time of the game. And I do not think he can be sure. I think he has almost had a guess that he is in the box. It is such a big call.”

“We see the ref’s position. The fact the ref makes the decision to give the penalty in my opinion, it is a bigger decision to give it then to not. We have got the luxury of the replays and we are still not sure. His whole body is outside the box.”

“It looks outside the box to me [the penalty incident]. The still picture suggests to me it was outside the box. We can get better and we will have to. We have to be more dominant with the ball at times and be better in attack. We have done a lot of work on that in pre-season. Having been in this league a long time, the power of the dressing room is crucial and any motivation tool you can you use is important. I think we will be fine. You have to enjoy football and love it. I think the boys enjoyed it tonight.”

“Obviously frustrated. The boys did everything to get the three points but it is gutting in the end. I thought I was outside the box when the ball came in and the decision went against us. They are saying it is in the box and it is frustrating. We dug deep and thought we had it. I cannot fault everyone as we all put in a shift, it was just the final details with the penalty decision. We deserved the three points. If we play like that every week, we will go far in the table.”

“Before the game we were predicting Wolves would be right up there [this season] and we thought it would be a comfortable win. But that was not the case.  Blackburn gave a really good account of themselves and had lots of openings. [Cesar] Peixoto will be breathing a massive sigh of relief with that handball.”

“Wolves got away with one if I am being really honest. In terms of their second-half performance, they did not do anywhere near enough. I thought Blackburn were excellent throughout and deservedly took the lead. It is a huge decision [to give the penalty], but in the end Raul Jimenez steps up to get his side the point. [Cesar Peixoto] will be delighted to get something in the end.”

Blackburn nearly score a late winner as Garrett’s shot is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a later Blackburn corner.

He sends Toth the wrong way and calmly slots home to bring Wolves level in added time. That penalty decision will certainly create some debate. The Championship is always full of drama and we get some on opening night.

Drama on the opening night of the campaign.

Relief for Wolves, heartbreak for Blackburn.

Late drama at Molineux! The cross is sent in from the left and the ball strikes the arm Alebiosu on the edge of the box. Was it inside or outside the penalty area? It is definitely handball but was it outside the box? It was very, very close but there is no VAR in the Championship so the penalty will stand.

Four added minutes. Are we on the verge of seeing the first shock of the new Championship season on opening night?

Wolves are desperately running out of time and Blackburn still look comfortable.

Home fans are beginning to filter out slowly.

Mosquera is still struggling but he has come back on whilst limping around. I cannot imagine there will be too much in terms of added time, either three or four minutes would be my guess, no more.

Mosquera has gone down again and he may not be able to continue as he receives treatment on the sidelines. Wolves may be ending this game down to 10 men.

Wolves struggling to create anything of note even with Jimenez’s introduction.

Centre-back Mosquera has gone up front but appears to be struggling with an injury. He’s jogged back to his natural position now.

Desperate long balls being sent forward but Blackburn look comfortable for now. The home fans are quite audibly unhappy with this second-half showing.

Wolves do not currently look like scoring an equaliser.

Mosquera is struggling with a knock but Wolves made all five changes. If he is unable to continue, Wolves will have to finish off with ten men.

The frustration inside Molineux is growing and the home fans want to see some more urgency from their side as they trail with under 10 minutes left.

Blackburn are now going to make their final two alterations of the night as Ribeiro and Garrett come on.

Wolves are going to make their final two substitutions as Lima and Chirewa replace Moller Wolfe and Andre.
