Wolves are pushing to find an equaliser but are struggling to carve out many genuine opportunities.

Ohashi is penalised for a foul on F Lopez not far outside the Blackburn penalty area and that was pretty harsh on Ohashi. Jimenez is lining this one up as is F Lopez.

The former takes but his effort hits the wall.

Wolves’ frustration right now is summed up by a dreadful cross from F Lopez from the right side of the box that goes behind for a goal kick. The TV cameras then turn to some of the Wolves fans, who look rather forlorn in the stands.

Double changes for both sides. For Wolves, Doyle and Tchatchoua come on. For Blackburn, Fevrier and Ohasi enter the fray.

You’d have thought a goal had gone in such is the reaction from the home crowd to Jimenez’s introduction. I have to say, I’m surprised Mane has made way but Jimenez will play through the middle with Armstrong moved out to the left.

Blackburn made a change earlier in the half with Wolverhampton-born Sam Morsy on for his Rovers debut. One manager going for it as the other attempts to shore things up.

Wolves’ last shot on target was all the way back in the 18th minute, when Munetsi put them in front. That is in fact their only shot on target tonight, compared to Blackburn’s four.

Should Wolves have been given a penalty? Jimenez goes down after Atcheson did stick out his leg but was there enough in it to give a penalty?

Jimenez is indeed now going to come on and Molineux rises to welcome him onto the pitch. The Jimenez scarfs go up around the ground and his song is sung. Mane goes off.

Raúl Jiménez receives an incredible reception from the Wolves fans as he makes his league return for the club 👏🇲🇽 pic.twitter.com/mPE7pvTJZt

No messing about from new Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto with his side behind and discontent brewing in the stands, Raul Jimenez is going to be introduced. His name has been sung throughout the game with a hero’s welcome imminent.

Can he inspire a comeback? Wolves and Peixoto will certainly hope so.

Munetsi, the scorer of Wolves’ goal, has a shot deflected from the edge of the box and it goes behind for a corner. Gudjohnsen, the scorer of Blackburn’s second, heads away at the front post.

You can sense the frustration growing from the home fans inside Molineux, with a few groans creeping in.

Blackburn are the first to turn to their bench as one experienced midfielder replaces another with Morsy coming on for Forshaw.

Wow! What a start to the second half. Blackburn have turned it around, Tony Mowbray clearly inspired his troops at half time.

Molineux is silenced now with Blackburn fans making all the noise. Some home supporters were still taking their seats as Gudjohnsen turned the ball home.

Can Wolves turn the game back in their favour? It’s all a bit slow now from the hosts followed by the first signs of disgruntlement from the home supporters.

And to top it off, Mane is booked for simulation.

The first Wolves player into the book tonight is Mane and it is for simulation. Watching the replays, that feels like a fair call as Mane threw himself to the ground and it probably was a dive.

Molineux is stunned as the underdogs take the lead inside the opening five minutes of the second half. Tony Mowbray’s side have started well since the break and are rewarded. Afolayan is found making a run into the penalty area on the right side of the box and his cross is slotted home by Gudjohnsen. His father Eidur would have been happy with a striker’s finish like that.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK

Morishita drives forward through the Wolves half and towards the penalty area. He lays it off to Afolayan, whose effort is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a Blackburn corner, which is headed and then cleared away by Wolves.

We are back under way at Molineux. No changes for either side at the break.

Possession: Wolves 52%-48% BlackburnShots: 10-4Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 3-2Touches in opposition box: 9-7

An intriguing first half as the whistle sounds and both teams head down the tunnel.

Both teams scored when the other seemed on top slightly.

Wolves have probably shaded it with those efforts from Lopez and Mane which went narrowly over.

Plenty to think about for the two managers.

The first half is brought to a close at Molineux and an engaging opening 45 minutes of the new Championship season results in this game being level at 1-1 at the break. Munetsi put Wolves in front before McLoughlin equalised for Blackburn.

Forshaw is the third Blackburn player into the book tonight as the referee goes back to penalise the midfielder for an earlier foul on Andre. That was not Forshaw’s first foul either.

With no VAR or hydration breaks, there will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Mane wins it back for his side on the edge of his own penalty area and drives forward. He takes it across the halfway line before feeding a lovely pass to his right to find Armstrong, whose shot is blocked.

Mane comes close to a stunner. Trippier rolls the ball across the face of the penalty area to 18-year-old Mane, who takes on the shot first time but his effort goes just over the bar.

Wolves come close to restoring their lead. Mane drives inside from the left and plays the ball forward to F Lopez, who takes one touch before getting his shot away from just outside the box. He tries to pick out the top corner but it just misses the target.

Like London buses, two yellow cards come at once and another Blackburn player is into the book. It is their captain Cantwell who receives a yellow card for delaying the restart. Cantwell was not too impressed with that decision.

Both teams off the mark for the season now, a brilliant near-post run and header from McLoughlin who scores his first-ever goal in English football to level the game up.

Molineux briefly stunned into silence. A slight delay from the fans celebrating the header as well.

The first booking of the Championship season goes the way of Blackburn left-back Pickering. It is a pretty simple decision for the referee as Pickering cynically pulls back R Gomes, who had spun him, and rightly receives a yellow card.

R Gomes delivers a cross from the right side of the Blackburn box across the penalty area but Armstrong does not pre-empt that and is not on hand to meet it. However, Alebiosu, with Mane not far behind him, puts it behind for a corner. Trippier delivers and the Blackburn keeper makes a meal of it, missing his punch out but then scrambles back towards his own goal to gather the loose ball.

The visitors went behind against the run of play but probably deservedly they are back on level terms. Morishita clips in the cross from the right to the near post, where McLoughlin meets it first and guides a powerful header into the far corner. Two goals in the opening half an hour of the new Championship season.

"They STUN Molineux!" 😳Sean Mcloughlin delightfully heads past Dan Bentley to equalise for Blackburn 👏 pic.twitter.com/v5qLhJ0wBt

Blackburn are getting great joy down their right through Alebiosu and Morishita, with the latter winning them a corner as Toti is forced to head behind from a cross. Pickering sends it into a good area and the touch comes off the head of Munetsi, whose header loops into the air and goes just over his own bar for another corner on the other side.

Cantwell’s delivery to the far post is headed away.

We have the first goal of the season and it’s the returning Marshall Munetsi who gets it.

A cool finish from the midfielder after a bit of a drab start from the home side.

That will please the new Wolves boss. Such a simple move but the home side ripped Blackburn wide open with two passes.

Work to do for the visitors now who had probably started the better of the two teams before the opener.

Wolves fans make their feelings about VAR known following the goal. No VAR in the Championship of course but no VAR was needed for that anyway. A perfectly good goal.

Mane cuts inside from the left onto his preferred right foot and curls a dangerous ball into the box that is punched away by Toth in the Blackburn goal. 18-year-old Mane was one of very few bright spots for Wolves last season and in many ways it is a surprise that no Premier League teams have lured him back to the top flight quite yet. That could though still happen before the deadline.

The first goal of the Championship season comes against the run of play. It is a clinical, ruthless goal that comes from an incisive pass and clinical finish. The pass is fed through by F Lopez to pick out the run of Munetsi, who is cool, calm and collected as he finishes past Toth. Blackburn had been the better side up until that point but Wolves take the lead at Molineux.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq

A shot on target for Blackburn but an easy save in the end. Alebiosu, who has looked good in these early stages, drives down Blackburn’s right before cutting it back to Morishita on the edge of the box. Morishita takes one touch before shooting but his effort is tame and straight at Bentley.

Blackburn have definitely been the better side in these early exchanges, dominating possession and looking a threat going forward.

Blackburn may be heavy underdogs tonight but they have settled down well away at one of the favourites to get promoted. Tony Mowbray may well be seeing this as a good time to play Wolves away.

Alebiosu shows quick feet down Blackburn’s right and clips a cross to the back post, where Afolayan meets it but his header is just off target.

Safe to say the doom and gloom of last season appears to have lifted at Molineux. The home fans in fine voice early on here.

By contrast, Kieran Trippier’s first touch of the season is greeted by loud boos by the travelling Blackburn supporters.

In fact, every Trippier touch is greeted by a chorus of boos. Will they keep that up all game?

They’ve certainly not forgotten his Burnley connection.

New managers and new signings galore. This should be a fascinating spectacle.

He may not be in the starting XI tonight but Jimenez is being serenaded by the home fans on his return to Wolves after a few years away at Fulham. Jimenez and his wife have paid for 5,000 scarves for the Wolves fans tonight.

Blackburn boss Tony Mowbray did say ahead of the game that Wolves have not been used to winning games over the last 12 months so can the visitors take advantage of that tonight? Blackburn are underdogs tonight and not too much is expected of them this season so surely they have nothing to lose this evening?

Due to his Burnley ties, new Wolves defender Trippier is booed by the travelling Blackburn fans. On the other side of defence for Wolves is Moller Wolfe, who started for Norway against England in the World Cup quarter-finals in Miami.

After Jeff Beck’s Hi Ho Silver Lining rings around the stadium and tributes paid to former Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes, we are under way at Molineux. The 2026/27 Championship season is officially under way.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off on opening night in the Championship.

Wolves: Bentley; Trippier, Mosquera, T.Gomes; R.Gomes, André, Munetsi, Möller Wolfe; Lopez, Mané; Armstrong.Substitutes: Sá, Bueno, Jiménez, Lima, Doyle, Chirewa, Djiga, Tchatchoua, Edozie.

Blackburn: Toth; Alebiosu, Atcheson, McLoughlin, Pickering; Forshaw, Montgomery; Afolayan, Cantwell, Morishita; Gudjohnsen.Substitutes: Pears, Ribeiro, Tavares, Morsy, Fevrier, Carter, Henriksson, Ohashi, Garrett.

These do not look good if you are a Blackburn fan; these are their attacking statistics and rankings in the Championship last season:

Goals: 42, 23rdxG performance: -13.9, 24thShots on target: 146, 23rdShot conversion: 7.9%, 22ndChances created: 368, 21st

Near the bottom of the league in every single one of those pretty much.

A debut for our brand new away kit 🤩#WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/Qxyvw1jAgi

Former Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes has died aged 79 in the last week and the club he played 382 times for is paying tribute to him tonight:

Paying tribute to a Wolves legend on tonight's matchday programme 🧡 pic.twitter.com/VEHciTuOZq

"We know what we are doing" 🤝Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto is confident in his side ahead of his the first Championship game of the season 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/2m12gsJ2y8

"We're ready for a strong performance" 💪Wolves defender Kieran Trippier and Blackburn's Sam Morsy preview their opening game of the season clash 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/I5t1J9Gapp

When Wolverhampton Wanderers last attacked the Championship under a Portuguese manager new to English football, it proved a vintage season.

Molineux was under the spell of Nuno Espírito Santo in that 2017-18 campaign, and the big question is whether César Peixoto can lead a repeat nearly a decade later.

Peixoto was a surprise appointment in June, replacing Rob Edwards, and he has been entrusted with the mission of returning Wolves to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

“I have changed some things with set-pieces and some things in other moments of the game because I want the team to be organised and understand all the different moments within a match. During pre-season we have scored some goals from high pressing, but we will not be able to press high in every moment of every game. The players have to understand the game and recognise what each moment requires. It is important that we work as a team. When we can press high, we’ll press high. When we need to defend in a mid-block, we will stay organised. When the opposition pushes us deeper, which will sometimes happen, we have to be organised there as well.

“There are a lot of crosses in the Championship, for example, so the team needs to understand what to do in those situations. We want to play our football, be offensive and react strongly when we lose the ball, but we also need to understand the different moments of the game. I think we are at a good level to attack the Championship.”

Our experts have been having their say ahead of the new Championship season. A number of them believe Wolves will be promoted, including John Percy:

It is difficult to look beyond West Ham. Nuno Espírito Santo romped to the Championship title with Wolves in 2018 and remains a shrewd operator (along with his No 2 Rui Pedro Silva), while convincing Jarrod Bowen to stay is significant. I am going to go for Wolves and Middlesbrough as the other two promoted clubs.

The boys are in the Black Country 👋 #WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/WjuGwrxYtQ

Saturday:Bolton vs PrestonBristol City vs MillwallCharlton vs DerbyMiddlesbrough vs LincolnNorwich vs West BromPortsmouth vs QPRStoke vs SwanseaSheffield United vs Birmingham

Sunday:Watford vs SouthamptonBurnley vs West Ham

🔢 Team news...2⃣ changes✅ Kristi Montgomery & Andri Gudjohnsen come in🆕 Sam Morsy on the bench🤕 Augustus Kargbo, Dion De Neve, Scott Wharton, Moussa Baradji, Mathias Jorgensen & Lewis Miller on the injured list#WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/esyE5Fibqc

☝️ One change from Port Vale🇳🇴 Wolfe in at LB🇪🇸 Hugo misses out with minor groin issueOur line-up for tonight's @EFL Championship opener 📋 pic.twitter.com/oRpIymUw1k

The 2026/27 Championship season kicks off at Molineux as Wolves host Blackburn, with the home side hoping to put the bad memories of last season firmly behind them. There are new playoff rules in place for this season, with six places now up for grabs in the play-offs.

Wolves are aiming to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, having endured a miserable season in the top flight last year as they finished bottom with just three wins to their name. It has been a summer of change at the club as they chose to change managers. Rob Edwards lost his job in what was a shock move and was replaced by 46-year-old Cesar Peixoto, with this being his first head coaching position outside of his home country Portugal. Back in 2017/18, Wolves won the Championship title led by Peixoto’s compatriot Nuno Espirito Santo.

“I am ready,” Peixoto told Wolves’ club website. “We have worked very hard during pre-season, and I think we have had a great pre-season. All the players have worked very, very hard and they understand what I want from them. I am ready and confident going into the first game. Football is football, whether it is in Portugal or England, but there are different characteristics to the game here. We have watched, observed and analysed the Championship. We did that work before I came to the club, so we know what to expect.

“It is going to be a tough season with good teams, but we are prepared to fight for the three points game after game and week after week. We know what we want from the team and we know what our big goal is. We’re going to work very hard and fight to achieve that goal.”

They have brought in vast experience on the player side in the shape of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez, who is back at Molineux three years after leaving for Fulham. Although they have lost Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes to Aston Villa, most of their squad has stayed intact as they pursue promotion back to the top flight. It is a special year for the club as they celebrate their 150th anniversary.

Blackburn, led by experienced manager Tony Mowbray, did not enjoy a great season in the Championship last year, finishing down in 20th place and just five points above the relegation zone. 14 years have now passed since Blackburn last played in the top flight.

“I think it is a tough start,” Mowbray said. “On paper, I would suggest the first couple of games, particularly, jumped out as a tough start. One of the Premier League sides from last season, away from home. They have got a very talented squad, a pretty expensive squad. They have got some very good individual talent. Yet, there is an argument to say they have not won many football matches in the last calendar year. So, what we get, we will have to wait and see.”

These sides last met in the FA Cup during the 2024/25 season, with Wolves winning that fourth-round tie 2-0 thanks to goals from Matheus Cunha and Gomes, both of whom are now plying their trade elsewhere. The omens would appear to be on Wolves’ side as they are unbeaten in their last eight league meetings with Blackburn. Both sides progressed to the second round of the League Cup last weekend, with Wolves beating Port Vale 3-0 and Blackburn overcoming Burton Albion 2-1.

Before I talk about how I spent my Saturday afternoon, let me share with you the good news that, thanks to the generosity of 32 donors, we now have enough funds to be able to pay for the ramp and very soon it will be installed by Nathan White alongside other work in the museum and around the ground that he also has to perform.

Thanks Nathan, for your support and hard work and for removing one reason for me "falling down" on the job.

We need to keep on fundraising for a while until the first exhibition is installed and the outside of the museum has been given a clean and been branded so people don't think we are the ticket office, but I would like to thank everyone for their support for this project. Long, may it continue.

We are striving to put on the first exhibition in December, hopefully to coincide with the 130th evening scheduled for Wednesday 9th December and the home match with Newport County on the following Saturday 12th December. Plans for the evening on the 9th are progressing with players from Crawley Town teams as far back as the 1950s promising to attend, six of whom will form a players panel to take questions from you, the supporters of the real Red Devils. Now, what happened Saturday? We picked up our second win of the season away to Oldham Athletic, albeit against ten men for seventy-six minutes and nine for an hour, with Danilo Orsi answering his critics in the best way possible by being in the right place to score after Charlie Barker had hit the woodwork with a thunderous drive from the edge of the box. For once it may have seemed that we got the rub of the green, and all I can say about that is, “about time”.

There was a lot of noise in my flat on Saturday afternoon and to the other residents I can only apologise and assure them that next Sunday it should be quiet as I will be in Wimborne, hopefully watching the Red Devils go three games unbeaten and progress to the 2nd round of the FA Cup.

A long way to go yet as we try and rescue our season, but with the return of Josh Flint and now being 17th in the form table, I really think we won’t have long to wait until we are out of the drop zone. Remember, "it ain't over till the overweight lady sings, so if you see her approaching, please point her in another direction"

#1922. Pulisic insists he ‘always wanted to renew’ with Milan after confirmation: “Wanted to stay”

Christian Pulisic has finally signed a renewal to stay with AC Milan, and he spoke after it was confirmed this afternoon.

It’s a big day for Milan. After years of negotiations, Pulisic has put pen to paper on a new deal to signify his importance to the club. Indeed, the American has been in talks across three seasons over a new deal. Yet, nothing was ever officially done.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Instead, talks broke down on two occasions and this felt like the final opportunity to agree on terms, even if a clause was available to extend his stay for another year past next summer.  Thankfully, that option was not needed, though, and the American has signed a new deal to keep him at San Siro until 2031.

Speaking to Sky Sport, via MilanNews, after the official confirmation of his renewal dropped, he admitted that he’d always hoped to renew his deal at San Siro, as well as looking ahead to the derby.

Your contract renewal until 2031 is now official. How happy are you?

“I’m very happy; renewing has always been my dream. I’ve always wanted to stay here, where I feel great confidence. I’m very happy here.”

Tomorrow is the derby, which is always a special match. What kind of match will it be?

“We know the derby is very intense; it’s a battle, and it will be the same tomorrow. I always want to score, not just in the derby. I want to help the team. We want to win.”

“We know that Inter have won a lot in recent years and that they play very well. Since I’ve been here, I’ve always seen them like this: a team that always plays well, always at the same level, and that deserves respect.

“But for us, the important thing is to focus on ourselves and put in a good performance tomorrow. If we do things right, we have a chance to win.”

What do you think of AC Milan and Amorim’s project?

“Yes, we always want to win: it can’t be any different with this jersey. It’s clear that it takes time, because there’s a new coach with new ideas, but we also want to win right away.

“We have a good relationship with the staff and the coach, we’re very happy and we’re learning something every day. Now we have to keep improving and win the championship.”

“A dream? Right now, it’s still the same dream, the same one as when I arrived.”

#1921. Scotland squad: Two key players set to return, one major injury worry and Ryan Gauld wildcard

Sebastien Pocognoli names his next Scotland squad on Tuesday for two Nations League matches against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

Scotland sit third in Group B1 on four points and are unable to catch leaders Switzerland, who have an 100 per cent record on 12 points. The Scots will be keen to catch Slovenia in second place, who are three point ahead. However, at least four points are required to give Pocognoli and Co a chance of doing so.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

North Macedonia visit Hampden on Friday, November 13 before Scotland head to St Gallen on Monday, November 16 to conclude their campaign against the Swiss. We take a look at the players would could make the squad:

Pocognoli named four goalkeepers in his squad for the first international window and given the dearth of options in this area of the team, there are unlikely to be any changes.

Angus Gunn has the gloves, but there is some debate as to whether he should remain as Scotland’s No 1 despite featuring regularly at club level for San Jose Earthquakes. Scott Bain’s excellent performance at the weekend for Falkirk against Celtic strengthened his case, while Jon McCracken has kept 12 clean sheets for Bradford City this season.

Liam Kelly was the other keeper picked last time out and given his inactivity at Rangers, he looks the most vulnerable of the quartet.

Pocognoli handed debuts to centre-halves Stephen Welsh, Luis Binks and Luke Graham last time out. Given all three are playing regularly for the clubs, they are expected to keep their place in the squad. Jack Hendry is another who is set for a call-up, but Scott McKenna is likely to miss out after picking up a back strain while playing for Dinamo Zagreb. That could open the door to Ryan Porteous at LAFC, or Wrexham’s Dom Hyam.

At right-back, Aaron Hickey, Nathan Patterson and Colby Donovan are in line for call-ups, while on the other flank, captain Andy Robertson, Kieran Tierney and Josh Doig are in pole position to be included.

If Robertson plays the next two Scotland matches, he will move on to 103 appearances and become the country’s most capped player, surpassing Sir Kenny Dalglish.

The big news is that Scott McTominay is primed for a recall after missing the last camp due to minor heart surgery. The 29-year-old has started the past seven matches for Napoli, scoring four goals, and is set to work with Pocognoli for the first time.

McTominay’s club-mate Billy Gilmour was an integral part of Pocognoli’s midfield and is fit, while fellow Serie A midfielder Lewis Ferguson started every game in the last international break and has regained first-choice status at Bologna.

John McGinn missed a penalty for Aston Villa at the weekend but has performed well at club level over the past few weeks and he is likely to be joined by Ryan Christie in the squad. If there is one more midfield berth, Kenny McLean is more likely to get it than Lennon Miller - who didn’t feature at all in the last international break - and uncapped Blackburn man Kristi Montgomery.

A wildcard could be Ryan Gauld, who is fully fit at Vancouver Whitecaps and has scored three goals in his past four matches.

Ben Gannon-Doak’s game-time for in-form Bournemouth has been limited to League Cup and European matches, but the 20-year-old has impressed when called upon by manager Marco Rose. He remains Scotland’s biggest threat out wide.

Josh McPake has had a rough schedule with Hearts but after winning his first cap last time out against Slovenia, he has done enough to keep his spot. Team-mate Calvin Miller may also have been in the running for inclusion, but he faces a spell on the sidelines due to a knee issue.

Findlay Curtis has struggled for starts at Rangers, but should Pocognoli want a third winger, he is the most likely to get the nod.

Che Adams was absent last time out due to a muscle strain, but four goals for Torino so far in Serie A suggests he is No 9 in form and it would be a surprise should he not be included.

Much was made of Oli McBurnie’s composure in front of goal - he is zero from 20 caps in terms of goals - but he continues to lead the line well for Hull City in the Premier League and scored a free-kick at the weekend.

Robbie Ure has scored one goal and provided two assists recently for Sevilla and should stay involved, while Kieron Bowie did enough in the last international camp with his excellent goal in North Macedonia. He flits in and out of the Sassuolo starting XI right now.

Ross Stewart fired a reminder to Pocognoli by scoring for Swansea at the weekend and could be a wildcard selection, while Hearts’ James Wilson will hope to stay in the plans too, although he has dropped out of the Tynecastle starting XI.

Middlesbrough are flying at the top of the Championship and Tommy Conway, who can play through the middle or out wide, has started their past three matches.

#1919. Goring CC FC 10 v Wittering United Reserves FC 2

Goring started well and on 15 minutes skipper Todor Bankov won a header on the half way line from which Connor Pomeroy's clever flick set Luke Tate on his way to open the scoring. This was quickly followed by a goal from Pomeroy who latched onto a fine pass from Tate and smashed home from the edge of the box.  Pomeroy added a third on 24 minutes before Wittering responded with a goal from Hashur Hussain. Pomeroy completed his hat trick from the penalty spot after 36 minutes for a 4-1 lead but Wittering again fought back and a second goal took the score to 4-2 at half time.

Goring were now rampant and when Rubano was brought down In the box on 58 minutes up stepped Bankov to fire home for a 6-2 lead. A clever pass from Willcox set up Pomeroy for his fourth goal and Goring's seventh in the 74th minute.

#1918. Bradford City 0 Huddersfield Town 3: 'Make it so' as table-topping Terriers show the enterprise on derby day

Town emphatically did that on derby day and for those Terriers followers present who suffered in silence at Valley Parade on an autumn lunch-time 13 months earlier, events will have felt cathartic.

This time it was their Bradford City counterparts who went through the mill. Saturday constituted their heaviest-ever home defeat to their West Yorkshire neighbours as the hosts conceded three league goals in a Valley Parade fixture for the first time in over two-and-a-half years.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It was what went before which made Huddersfield’s triumph all the more remarkable. City goalkeeper Jon McCracken hadn’t picked the ball out of his net for almost 11-and-a-half-hours before Joe Low beat him with a magnificent early overhead kick not in keeping with a 6ft 5in centre-half.

After six successive clean sheets in all competitions, City shipped three goals in the space of 48 minutes; their first concessions under Michael Duff. A funny old game, which ended with Bradford - the team with the best defensive numbers in the EFL before kick-off - adopting damage limitation tactics following the dismissal of their captain midway through a tortuous second half.

Martin Drury wanted more on his return to BD8, yet was entitled to be happy enough. ‘We want five’ was the pre-game driver for his players, mindful of the fact that City had conceded just five goals in 12 previous league matches this term. Confidence, not arrogance, Drury insisted.

No nap hand, but any visiting side who scores three times at Valley Parade in one game should be safe in the knowledge they are the real deal.

That was reinforced by the narrative of this game. Despite trailing, City were the better side in the opening half. But good sides don’t panic and find a way, which league leaders Town certainly did.

On the restart they married defensive solidity - in marked contrast to their feebleness in this fixture in September 2025 - with attacking verve.

That Town clearly possess more gears - they were without Bojan Radulovic, don’t forget - should serve as a warning to serious third-tier rivals.

They were dynamite when it mattered. Two goals in the space of three minutes early in the second half and the game was over.

Duff spoke beforehand of Town being devastating on the counter and the visitors’ second goal was the stuff of nightmares on Hallowe’en. Most un-Bradford like.

City were caught with their pants down following a corner and danger duo Derensili Sanches Fernandes and Joe Taylor were in for a treat.

Corey O’Keeffe got himself in a horrible pickle and Fernandes rammed a low shot through the legs of McCracken for his fifth goal in six outings.

Soon after, Taylor sneaked around George Pratt before dispatching a downward header at the far post from a succulent Sean Roughan left-wing cross which simply oozed confidence.

Quiet in the first half, Taylor and Fernandes remain stellar attacking players with enterprise. One or the other will do something sooner or later. Or both. Their combined league aggregate of goals/assists in 2026-27 now stands at 23. Keep them fit and firing and the sky is the limit this term.

For Drury, it was also a good day tactically. His selections worked, unlike his opposite number.

The big pre-match call seemed to be Low or Radinio Balker. In the event, Drury picked them both, mindful of their aerial progress against a Bradford side who throw it in the mixer. The decision was vindicated.

Duff's move to start with Jake Beesley proved right also. He did his job and put himself about. The decision to bring in Henry Cartwright as Callum Connolly's replacement did not work, by contrast. At times, he looked like someone who hadn't started a league fixture this season.

Duff's half-time substitutions didn't reap reward either in a half where everything that could have gone wrong did. The sight of interval replacement Adam Phillips hobbling off late on applied the salt.

Bradford City: McCracken; Pennington, Baldwin, Pratt; O’Keeffe, Cartwright (Pointon 58), Sarcevic, Touray; Jackson (Powell HT), Swan (Phillips HT); Beesley (Lapslie 72). Substitutes unused: Dawson, Gillesphey, Morgan.

Huddersfield Town: Young; Bronkhorst, Balker (Gooch 92), Low, Roughan (Bowat 83); Fernandes (Tovide 92), Humphreys, Collins, Mumba (Sway 92); Taylor, Fletcher (Harness 78). Substitutes unused: Alnwick, Brierley.

#1916. “I’m confident” – Cardinale offers insight on ‘intense’ Milan atmosphere ahead of the derby

AC Milan chairman, Gerry Cardinale, spoke outside the training ground this afternoon, as his team prepares for their biggest game in October.

Tomorrow’s derby has a lot at stake. For Milan, a win could re-enter them into the title discussion, if not just cement their hopes of a top four finish. A loss, though, would put them 10 points behind the Nerazzurri.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s going to be a big ask with a squad ravaged by injuries, but the Rossoneri have been in similar positions before. In other words, they’ve not forfeited the game before a ball has even been kicked at San Siro.

With the new stadium being shown on Thursday, too, it’s also the beginning of the end for these games at their current home.

Speaking outside Milanello to MilanNews, Cardinale touched on the atmosphere ahead of tomorrow’s Derby della Madonnina and his confidence for the game.

“Serious. Very serious. I think everyone’s focused.”

“Every derby is important, every match is important, so, you know, to do things well you have to be serious. It’s a match. These guys are focused, and Ruben is doing his job, the guys are doing theirs. Today was a great training session.”

“Yes, I’m always confident because we’re prepared and doing our job. Injuries always come unexpectedly and you have to deal with them, but that’s football. But tomorrow we’ll go onto the pitch very determined and very focused. And we’ll see what happens.

“We’ll go onto the pitch to win, there’s no doubt about that.”

“Of course. Several times a day. But you’ve spoken to him too, right? I was there at the press conference. What do you think? It was a good press conference. Ruben is very clear in his words, very authentic, very transparent. This is the new Milan.”

It’s fair to say the American has worn his heart on his sleeve with his words; hopefully, his confidence is repaid by the team.

#1915. 'Take your medicine': Bradford City boss Michael Duff's message after Huddersfield Town loss - plus one small consolation

It arrives in the fact that the Bantams have a clear week - having had relatively few 'proper' training sessions under Duff due to their match schedule following his appointment on October 6.

City switch to cup business and host non-league Marine in the FA Cup next Saturday before welcoming York City in the EFL Trophy on Tuesday week.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Given the good chance that their league appointment at Leicester City on November 14 will called off due to international call-ups, City's return to league action is likely to be on November 21 when they entertain Doncaster Rovers.

Duff said: "We've got a couple of weeks now before the next league game.

"Obviously, there's a couple of (cup) games in between that. But we'll need a reaction now. And the reaction has been good week to week."

Duff, who was 'serenaded' in unflattering terms by fans of former club Town in the second half, insists the Bantams must take their medicine following the maiden defeat of his tenure, on a day when they also conceded their first goals under his watch.

Equally, the 48-year-old is keen to look at the broader picture at City following a 'bad day at the office'.

He continued: "There have been a lot of good performances. And they were good for the five or six games before that (Huddersfield). So, you put it together, it's been a good, strong 10 or 11, 12 games.

"We've just been beaten. Take your medicine. Dust yourselves down. Stay together. And crack on to the next one.

"It's easy when you're winning or you're not conceding goals. The seasons are long; 10-and-a-half months. And there's loads of ups and downs. And football doesn't work in a straight line.

"There's been bumps in the road before. Hopefully, it's a bump in the road.

"Ultimately, it's just a bad day to have a bad day at the office.

"That's the frustration. We know we've let the supporters down in terms of the result. And things like that.

"But I don't think we've been played off the park, whilst it was 11 v 11. It was key moments.

"That's what they do well. They transition really well. And we knew that. That's what we have to take home."

#1914. Charlton Athletic vs Bolton Wanderers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 01 Nov 2026 15:33, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 15:34

Charlton Athletic and Bolton square off on Tuesday evening looking for the win that would move them clear of the relegation zone.

The Addicks and Trotters sit level on points in 20th and 19th place in the Championship table.

Given how strongly Charlton started the season, Nathan Jones has arguably deserved the time that he has been given to turn around their current run of form.

However, opening the campaign with a three-game winning streak in the Championship has been followed by a 10-match run without success.

Although the London outfit remain five points clear of the drop zone, they have only accumulated five points since the start of September.

Charlton's latest defeat came at the hands of leaders Middlesbrough by a 3-0 scoreline, there having been no expectations of a win at the Riverside Stadium.

Nevertheless, Charlton have only lost one of their six home fixtures at The Valley, putting together a five-game unbeaten run before a 3-1 defeat to Norwich City in their last such contest.

As for Bolton, the recent goalless draw at Southampton suggested that they had fully adapted to life back in the Championship.

Instead, eight goals have since been conceded across defeats to Middlesbrough and Bristol City, the latter coming from a winning position.

Steven Schumacher's side had been leading 2-1 heading into the final six minutes, but they eventually succumbed to a 93rd-minute winner from the visitors.

Although Bolton have the second-worst defensive record in the division, they make the trip to The Valley on a three-match unbeaten streak on their travels.

As well as deciding whether to stick with three central defenders, Jones will likely make changes in personnel for Charlton.

Tyreece Campbell and Karlan Grant could be brought into the final third, with Miles Leaburn likely to drop down to the substitutes' bench.

Ivan Mesik and Conor Coventry are options in defence and midfield, but Collins Sichenje and Matty Godden will again miss out through injury.

With Bolton defender Chris Forino picking up an injury against Bristol City, Lewis Brunt could be recalled to the defence.

Ruben Rodrigues may also take the spot of Atsuki Ito, but Ethan Erhahon, John McAtee and Ryan Hardie are all sidelined.

Charlton Athletic possible starting lineup:

Okonkwo; Ramsay, Mesik, Koumetio, Jones, Bell; Rankin-Costello, Coventry, Skipp; Campbell, Kelman

Bolton Wanderers possible starting lineup:

Bonham; Larrazabal, Brunt, Davies, Conway; Simons, Sheehan; Iling-Junior, Rodrigues, Gale; Darby

Despite the manner of Bolton's last two defeats, we cannot ignore how long it has been since Charlton posted a win. With that in mind, we are backing the visitors to edge their way to three points in a nervy game

#1913. ‘Deeply shocked’ – Club rally round after cup tie is abandoned as incident leaves player hospitalised

Midhurst and Easebourne FC’s second team – who play under the name Midhurst and Easebourne Community – were playing a home Malcolm Simmonds Memorial Cup match at the Rotherfield against Emsworth Town when the flashpoint occurred around 15 minutes into the match.

Police and league officials have been involved as investigations continue – with the club saying they are doing all they can to support ‘one of our own’ at a ‘horrific’ time.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Midhurst and Easebourne said in a statement on Saturday night: “Following the abandonment of our community team fixture this afternoon at the Rotherfield in the Malcolm Simmonds Memorial Cup, we can confirm that two Midhurst players were involved in a serious incident, with one requiring hospital treatment. As a result, the match was abandoned.

“As a club we are deeply shocked that an incident of this nature has occurred during a game that should be enjoyed by everyone involved.

"We would like to extend our sincere thanks to South East Coast Ambulance Service and the club’s first aid-trained staff, who provided outstanding care and support to our player and his family during a very difficult situation.

"We are working closely with Sussex Police and the West Sussex Football Club as enquiries continue. Our priority remains the wellbeing and recovery of the player involved.

"We will provide updates through our official channels when appropriate and when further information is available. ***#OneClub #OneCommunity #OneVision.”

A further statement on Sunday afternoon revealed the extent of a player’s injuries.

The new Midhurst and Easebourne FC statement said: “Unfortunately two of our players were assaulted by yesterday’s opposition in a completely unprovoked attack. This led to one of our team members requiring urgent medical treatment after the serious injuries he received.

"We are now pleased to say he has been discharged from hospital after suffering severe damage to his internal mouth, a broken bone in his jaw, and a high chance of requiring surgery to fix the injury further.

"We would also like to thank again the South East Coast Ambulance Service for their swift response, and all of the medical team at the accident and emergency department.

"As a club we will continue to be working closely with Sussex Police and the West Sussex Football League to make sure the corrrect sanctions are carried out, and make sure we protect any further teams from having to put their players at such risk playing the game we enjoy.

"We will also be carrying out internal welfare checks on the rest of the playing squad, staff and supporters who were affected by yesterday’s incident. Our support goes out to ‘one of our own’ and his family members at this horrific time.”

#1912. Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

Jaissle’s team found their feet as the first 45 minutes progressed, with Yoane Wissa their biggest attacking threat. The striker endured a difficult first season at the club, but his performances at the World Cup with DR Congo appear to have restored confidence.

Newcastle were level just before half-time, when Malick Thiaw rose highest to plant home a back-post header from a corner. Former Brentford goalkeeper Mark Flekken appealed in vain for a foul, but there was no infringement.

After changing all 10 outfield players at half-time against Everton, Jaissle was more circumspect with second-half substitutes; Rory Finneran for Lewis Miley was the only change before the 80th minute.

Newcastle faded though, and the game was won by Victor Boniface scoring just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute. The Nigeria striker wrong-footed Sean Steur with an impudent piece of skill before rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

The North-East club are coming to terms with the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães this summer, as well as manager Eddie Howe. They have one more pre-season friendly to play, against Strasbourg on Sunday, before they begin their Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool.

Newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; M Miley (Pivas 81), Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley (Finneran h-t); Elanga, Woltemade (Neave 86), Barnes; Wissa. Subs Charlton, Harris (g), Sanusi, Johnson.

Bayer Leverkusen (4-2-3-1) Flekken; Vazquez (Tape h-t), Bade, Tapsoba, Gutierrez (Belocian 70); Garcia, Fernandez (Terrier 70); Maza (Boniface 80), Tillman (Doganay 70), Moreira (Tella 80); Kofane (Schick h-t). Subs Hofmann, Arthur, Oermann, Poku, Blaswich (g), Alfa-Ruprecht, Hawighorst, Lomb (g).

Referee Michael Oliver (Durham). Attendance 39,059

A second pre-season defeat in a week for Newcastle. Just like against Everton, they faded in the second 45 minutes but Jaissle decided to leave some tired legs out there for fitness purposes. The performances of Barnes and Wissa were promising, but Newcaslte are giving up chances.

Newcastle had a free-kick with the last kick of the game, but Harvey Barnes loops the delivery straight into Flekken’s gloves.

Schik with a chance to wrap up the victory, but Hornicek saves before Thiaw clears to deny Terrier a tap in on the rebounds.

There will be just three minutes of added time to play.

Elanga fouled near the touchline, but time is running out. The free-kick won by Neave came to nothing.

Chance for Barnes! Good combination play involving Elanga and Wissa down the right, and the ball flashed across the six-yard box. Barnes almost steered it in, but did not make firm enough contact.

Newcastle attacking with more urgency since conceding, but there are moans and groans in the ground at a misplaced Elanga pass. Sean Neave has just replaced Woltemade, and the 19-year-old wins a free-kick in a crossing position with his first action of the game.

The striker has only been on the pitch a few minutes, but Boniface has restored Leverkusen’s lead. Lovely chop inside the box, which sent Steur for a hot dog, before passing the ball into the far corner. No celebration of note from a player who could be on the move this summer.

Newcastle making just their second change of the game: Pivas replaces Mason Miley at right-back.

Leverkusen have made two more changes: Moreira and Maza off, Tella and Boniface on.

The corner is straight down the throat of Flekken, and that prompsts some groans from the home fans.

Newcastle having to defend deep for long periods, but Elanga did well to win a free-kick with little support. Moreira dragged the winger down. Then Wissa’s cross is turned behind for a corner.

Woltemade’s control lets him down as he tries to bring the ball down on halfway. The game is being played at a snail’s pace at the moment, but Leverkusen are dominating the ball.

Play has now resumed. Garcia does well to defend after Lewis Hall won the ball back in a dangerous position.

Time for another hydration break and Leverkusen are making three more substitutions. We await further changes from Jaissle. Should the game finish level, there will be a penalty shoot-out to decide the winner of the Visit Malta Cup.

Rather like the mid-week friendly against Everton, Newcastle have faded after half-time. Struggling to get into the game in any meaningful way. Slick football from Leverkusen but Fernandez fails to bring the ball under his spell in the box when there was time and space to shoot.

Leverkusen just inches away from regaining the lead. It was an incisive run off the left from Afonso Moreira, who tried to place the ball into the far corner but his attempt rolled just wide of the post.

Good defensive header by Lewis Hall before Wissa wins a foul on halfway. Newcastle feeding off scraps at the moment. Elanga goes too early and is flagged offside.

Bayer Leverkusen have had the better of it in this half, but some of the shooting has been wayward. This time is it Schik’s turn to slash a shot over the bar. Fouls committed by Finneran and Botman.

Newcastle with a three-on-three on the break after Wissa does well to win the ball back on halfway, but Woltemade was too slow to get his shot away at the end of the move. More good play from Wissa.

Half a chance for Fernandez to shoot from the edge of the D, but he was leaning back and ballooned the shot miles over the bar.

Finneran, the youngster in Newcastle’s midfield, is caught on the ball but then does well to recover it. I reckon there will be a raft of changes on the hour mark.

Corner for Leverkusen after Moreira gets forward and attacks Mason Miley. The German side have additional aerial threat with Schik on the pitch. Woltemade does well to head clear.

Bayer Leverkuen kick off in the second half.

Jaissle made 10 against Everton, so wants his starters to build minutes today. Rory Finneran is coming on for Newcastle, an 18-year-old academy player. He replaces Lewis Miley in midfield. Czech striker Patrik Schik is on for Bayer Leverkusen.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of an even first half, with Wissa Newcastle’s best player. The story though, is that kit clash that prompted Newcastle to change into their lilac third kit halfway through the half.

Just the two minutes of stoppage time to play.

Newcastle equalise from a set-piece. Flekken is claiming a foul, but it is a legitimate goal. The goalkeeper was nowhere to be seen on a corner that looped all the way to be back post, and he seemed to lose his bearings allowing Thiaw to find the far corner.

Newcastle have a corner after another move in which Wissa was lively. His performances have been a ray of light in pre-season, he really struggled in his first season at the club.

Lewis Hall takes the free-kick, but he scoops it well over the bar. Elanga delivers a low cross from the right, but Garcia is well positioned to clear.

Newcastle enjoying a lot more possession now, but you cannot say they look like equalising.

That was better though, more zip in the attack with Elanga laying the ball off for Wissa and Fernandez is booked from dragging the Newcastle forward to the ground. Free-kick in a shooting position.

Good play from Lewis Hall, skipping beyond two challenges to escape from a tight spot but then his crossfield pass is intercepted. Moreira passes the ball straight out of play for a Newcastle goal kick, when there was a chance for Leverkusen to punish the hosts on the break.

Elanga tries to take on Gutierrez but his low cross is too close to Flekken. Gutierrez then buys a foul when under pressure from Lewis Miley. Game has become quite bitty following those stoppages. Maza then chops down Harvery Barnes.

The game is back under way. Changing kits has improved things visually but it is still not ideal. You wonder how on earth two clubs of this stature failed to liaise on this before the game.

Bayer Leverkusen are still on top, but play has been stopped for a hydration break. Some boos from the stands, it is not an especially hot day.

On the subject of the kit clash, Newcastle are now changing into their lilac away kit. Shades of Manchester United at the Dell all those years ago.

A short stoppage in play after Tapsoba receives a knock in the small of the back from Newcastle’s goalkeeper Hornicek. Both managers get their players over for a tactical conflab.

Leverkusen look very accomplished in possession, they are moving the ball well through the lines. Kofane was a big threat when they played Arsenal in last season’s Champions League and they are looking to find him with crosses. Mason Miley defends well at right-back, but at the expense of a corner.

Flekken called into action again, Newcastle starting to warm to their task. It was direct play from first Elanga and then Barnes, but his cross deflects towards the goalkeeper and he parries away. Then Barnes is fouled, and Newcastle have a free-kick in a crossing position near the left corner of the penalty area. Poor delivery from Barnes, Flekken claims.

Newcastle fans sing “walking in a Keegan wonderland” in unison. Bade is then penalised for catching Woltemade late as they contested an aerial challenge.

Newcastle’s best moment so far: Wissa peels off the shoulder of Bade and tested Flekken with a volley from a tight angle. The goalkeeper saved and Leverkusen scramble clear, but it was good movement from the Newcastle striker.

Leverkusen continue to make the running, enjoying more possession and most of it is coming inside Newcastle’s half. Goalkeeper Flekken takes a beat inside his own six-yard box, and his pass out is almost cut out by Woltemade.

Newcastle’s players are wearing black armbands in memory of Kevin Keegan.

#1911. Burgess Hill 4s show grit and determination to defeat strong Hailsham 3s

Burgess Hill 4s produced a determined and disciplined team performance to secure a hard-earned 1-0 victory over a strong Hailsham 3s side in an entertaining and closely contested match.

The game was evenly balanced throughout much of the first half, with both teams creating attacking opportunities and moving the ball well. Burgess Hill looked dangerous going forward through the combination of Cath Donovan, Becs Marriner and Sabine Rowan, while Hailsham continually tested the home side with their pace and movement. As the game developed, Burgess Hill enjoyed several promising attacking spells of their own, forcing Hailsham onto the back foot and demonstrating plenty of attacking intent.

Behind them, the midfield unit of Gillian Branagan, Jo Richardson, Debs Scott and Toni Frier worked tirelessly to ensure Burgess Hill remained competitive in the middle of the pitch. Branagan had an outstanding game in the centre, repeatedly breaking up Hailsham attacks and distributing the ball intelligently into attacking areas. Scott worked relentlessly across the pitch, competing strongly for every loose ball and providing support in both attack and defence. Richardson provided calmness and composure whenever Burgess Hill were in possession, helping her side maintain shape and move the ball effectively, while Frier's energy and determination helped drive the team forward and disrupt Hailsham's rhythm.

At the other end of the pitch, Burgess Hill's defence produced an outstanding display. Sarah Bailey was tireless on the right-hand side, combining strong defensive work with energetic forward runs to support attacks before tracking back quickly to close down danger. On the left, Lucy Fox was rock solid throughout, producing a series of crucial clearances from inside the D and denying Hailsham attackers the opportunity to test the goalkeeper. Sweeping behind the defensive line, Wendy Caddye was calm and composed, reading the game superbly and consistently clearing danger before it developed into genuine opportunities. In the centre, Ali Gillham delivered an exceptional performance, producing a number of powerful and accurate clearances that bypassed the Hailsham midfield and found Burgess Hill's attackers, turning defence into attack with a single hit.

Also playing a vital role was goalkeeper Grace Mortimer, who communicated well with her defence throughout and showed great bravery coming off her line on several occasions to clear danger before Hailsham could capitalise.

The breakthrough came towards the end of the first half following an excellent team move. Branagan won possession in midfield and played a perfectly weighted pass to Marriner at the top of the D. Marriner showed great awareness to move the ball on to Donovan on the right side of the circle. Driving forward and facing the goalkeeper one-on-one, Donovan kept her composure before producing a perfectly timed slip pass across the face of goal. The move caught the goalkeeper off guard and found Rowan waiting unmarked at the left post, where she calmly guided the ball into the corner to give Burgess Hill a deserved 1-0 lead.

The second half proved even more challenging. Hailsham emerged determined to find an equaliser and increasingly applied pressure as the game wore on. Matters became even more difficult for Burgess Hill when Branagan was forced to leave the game midway through the half, leaving the side without a substitute. With Frier having sustained an earlier injury that limited her movement, the team had to dig deep physically and mentally to protect their advantage.

As Hailsham pushed forward, Burgess Hill showed tremendous resilience. Every player contributed, tracking back, making tackles and working for one another as Hailsham searched relentlessly for a way back into the contest.

The final stages of the game were particularly tense. Hailsham were awarded two consecutive short corners in the final two minutes, creating the best opportunities of the match to snatch a late equaliser. However, Burgess Hill defended superbly, with players charging out quickly, sticks down and bodies behind the ball to deny the initial strikes on goal.

The biggest moment of all came in the closing seconds. A lifted effort from Hailsham looked destined to find the net, but Mortimer reacted brilliantly, getting her pads to the ball and producing a vital save. Fox was quickest to react to the loose ball, clearing the danger and helping preserve Burgess Hill's slender lead.

After several nervous moments, the final whistle brought relief and celebration for the Burgess Hill side. Against a strong and determined Hailsham team, Burgess Hill had matched their opponents going forward, taken their chance when it came, and then shown outstanding character to defend their lead under immense late pressure.

While Rowan's goal ultimately secured the victory, this was very much a team performance. From the attacking pressure of Donovan, Marriner and Rowan, to the tireless efforts of the midfield and the heroic defensive display led by Bailey, Gilham, Fox, Caddye and Mortimer, every player played their part in a memorable and well-deserved 1-0 win.

Burgess Hill Team: Mortimer (GK), Marriner (C), Donovan, Branagan, Richardson, Frier, Caddye, Bailey, Gillham, Rowen, Scott, Fox. Player of the Match: Sarah Bailey

The Baggies and Saints occupy fourth and fifth place in the Championship table respectively.

#1904. Hull City's pussy cat passivity against Ipswich Town a warning on how not to play it their way

But they were lessons they ought to have taken on board a fortnight earlier, so we will wait and see if it goes in this time.

Coach Sergej Jakirovic has been in situ for nearly a year-and-a-half now, and for a long time, the Tigers seemed to have got his approach off pat.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

But Saturday was a perfect “before and after” of how not to and then how to play their way.

The Tigers lost the first half 1-0 with timid football deserving of harsher punishment. But in the second they were aggressive, and came out 2-1 winners. The net result was a fifth draw already this Premier League season.

If you did not know better in the first half, you would have thought the team in black and amber was respectfully playing away to a far superior side, not at home to one below them in the table on goal difference.

Most teams in the top flight are more talented – not necessarily better – than Jakirovic's, so they tailor their tactics accordingly, Hull wrapping themselves in a double blanket of a 5-4-1 formation and inviting to the opposition to play. They even did in when alongside Ipswich in last season’s Championship.

It suited the Tractor Boys, who are much more eager to get the ball down but have not found anyone so eager to accommodate that since returning to the big league.

But there is a bit more to it than just that.

For it to work, Hull must be good defensively and effective on the counter-attack. They were neither for 45 minutes, playing with a passivity that was their downfall at Fulham too as if they had wiped it from their memories.

It took 20 minutes for Ipswich to play behind rather than in front of the Tigers but the hosts were not resolute enough in keeping them out, and far too sloppy on the ball.

The first-half passing accuracies of the teams – 74.1 per cent to 90.1 – said it all. Over the whole season, no other club has had worse or better.

It frustrated the home fans, who booed their players off at half-time. The only solace was that somehow it was only 1-0. That would be crucial.

Ipswich had taken the lead in the 22nd minute when Abdoul Ouattara glided rather too easily past Elliot Stroud and fed Florentino Luis to smash the ball past Konstantinos Tzolakis at the near post.

It summed up the passivity of the pussy cats.

"I can say I was surprised," said Jakirovic.

When Semi Ajayi over-ran the ball he was fortunate Tim Iroegbunam – the exception to the dismal Hull rule in the first half – got back to tackle, and that referee Thomas Kirk spotted what must have been quite a soft foul on Oli McBurnie before the ball ended up in the net from Julio Enciso at the corner.

Hull had got slightly better by pushing John Egan into midfield, but it took until 39 minutes for Iroegbunam to take their first shot, and it was woefully wide.

And it needed the half-time introduction of Matt Crooks for Hull to finally live up to their nickname.

Crooks has struggled at times with the step up in class this season, but was instrumental in this game.

Rattling very late into former Leeds United and Middlesbrough winger Jack Clarke after an hour earnt him a fifth yellow card this season, the first player to that mark in the Premier League. But Arsenal away is not the worst game for a team in survival mode to miss a big player, and the tackle was another sign of Tigers baring their teeth.

Hull's goals mixed McBurnie brilliance with Ipswich culpability.

The Scotland striker is a big unit who gets kicked black and blue most games, but he can also drop into midfield and show class, as he did just before the hour, turning a ball around the corner for Iroegbunam to sprint over the halfway line to.

"It was a weird one because I wasn't looking to shoot," he admitted. "It was almost like he was forcing me to shoot, the centre-back. No one came and engaged me. It was like, I have to shoot now."

And if daring a player who had never scored a Premier League goal to score may have seemed low risk, egging McBurnie to find the bottom corner when he stood over a free-kick in the D was nonsensical.

McBurnie could go straight past the wall, no need for bend, and goalkeeper Christian Walton even touched the ball on its way in. After 930 days between Premier League goals, it was his second in a week. Not even London buses are like that.

With the tables turned, that should have been the cue for a home win, but if Ipswich were too stand-offish with Iroegbunam, Hull were too weak in the tackle when Enciso was on the ball, even if his 74th-minute finish was wonderful.

With about 20 minutes to find a winner, both teams tried, but neither could do it.

A draw was okay for Hull, who remain above the point-per-game mark even as winning is becoming an increasingly distant memory. If heeded, the lessons of the day could be much more valuable.

Hull City: Tzolakis; Coyle (Norton-Cuffy 77), Ajayi, Egan (Crooks HT), Mendy, Giles; Iroegbunam (Morita 77), Slater (Gelhardt 90); Belloumi, Stroud (Cho 58); McBurnie.

Unused substitutes: Phillips, McNair, Herrington, Mouzakitis.

Whether those names have been an upgrade so far is difficult to tell, but it’s certainly been an introduction of a new wave of talent.

After dominating in Serie A last season, Inter have started the season in similar fashion, only dropping points to Roma so far. However, they’ve been something of comeback kings, regularly finding an escape when behind.

In fact, in their last three Serie A games, they’ve conceded the first goal – including the midweek disallowed goal against Venezia – yet they’ve always ended up with three points. The inevitability from recent seasons hasn’t disappeared.

What makes this potentially more frustrating is that they’re also struggling with injuries, but still getting results. Without Lautaro Martinez, Stones, Jones and Benjamin Pavard, a drop-off would’ve been understandable, but it hasn’t happened.

After their win in midweek, considering their schedule has also been rough, Chivu rotated slightly. So, there will be a few changes made this weekend to rotate back to their full-strength XI.

In the backline, Manuel Akanji will return to the centre of the back three, replacing Carlos Augusto. Whilst Alessandro Bastoni and Yann Bisseck will start either side of the Swiss defender. Of course, Ivan Provedel remains between the sticks.

Across the midfield, changes will be slightly more common. Federico Dimarco and Andy Diouf will remain on the flanks, whilst Piotr Zielinski retains his starting spot. Though Nicolo Barella and Hakan Calhanoglu both return to the starting XI.

Marcus Thuram will be given a starting role, hoping to continue his fine form this season, but Ange-Yoan Bonny will return to the bench. Pio Esposito will take his place instead.

Predicted bench: Martinez, Di Gennaro, Augusto, Jakirovic, Bovio, Mkhitaryan, Lavelli, Mosconi, Spence, Bonny, Stankovic, Sucic.

#1902. Barnsley FC improvement evidenced by Daniel Stendel nostalgia as Oxford United draw raises spirits - analysis

On the day Barnsley paid tribute to their record-appearance maker, they produced the type of spirit he embodied.

The life of Reds legend Barry Murphy, who recently died at the age of 86, was celebrated prior to kick-off and again in the second minute with a moving round of applause.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

A full-blooded right-back who played with the club deeply embedded in his heart, Murphy would have enjoyed the fight on show in Barnsley’s 1-1 draw with Oxford United.

“Today I have the feeling this is the Barnsley Football Club I know in my first time (spell in charge),” said Reds head coach Daniel Stendel.

“[We had] a, big unity, a big fight, not only on the pitch, in the past, in the environment here, and it was a really good feeling. I hope he feels it too.”

Jack Shepherd saw red for a reckless foul on Louie Sibley just nine minutes in and the weary home faithful could have been forgiven for fearing the worst.

Barnsley have been in freefall but their response to yet another setback was impressive. They abandoned their signature high press and adopted a more pragmatic approach, dropping deeper and getting bodies behind the ball.

Off went frontman Tobi Adeyemo as Barnsley introduced defender Jubril Okedina, switching to a strikerless system in the aftermath of the red card. The latter slotted in at right-back while Arley Kay tucked inside at centre-back alongside Sam Gale.

Stendel’s men still attacked at pace, yet there was noticeably less of the reckless abandon that has unravelled the Reds with such alarming frequency of late.

Vimal Yoganathan fired the hosts ahead against the run of play, connecting with a cross supplied by the impressive Okedina.

“The two wingers from Oxford are maybe the best in the league,” said Stendel. “We defended it really well, especially in the second half, when there's a lot of times a one-against-one situation.

“He's a really good defender, he wins the most duels, he blocks the balls, he wins balls.

“It's a good sign for him and also for us that we have a player like him.”

Barnsley defended with drive but not desperation, retaining their discipline as they kept Oxford at bay.

The U’s did eventually level proceedings via Mark Harris, yet an equaliser was all they could muster against a gritty Barnsley. Aaron Ramsey’s men even went down to 10 men themselves late on, when goalkeeper Jamie Cumming was judged to have fouled Rylan Brownlie.

The Oakwell faithful have had little love for their players of late - and understandably so. It was therefore even more significant and indicative of improvement when they responded to Oxford’s leveller with a rallying cheer of encouragement. All the negativity and pessimism of recent weeks, dissipated by an hour of hearty fight.

“It was really important,” said Stendel. “Especially with the experience in the last couple of weeks.

“It was more the feeling, ‘oh come on, we conceded again a goal’.

“I think we can talk with the players, change the mindset in a situation like this when we conceded a goal. It's really difficult to change it only when you talk and we try some things in training.

“But I think the most change for the heads today was the applause after the 1-1. It was a good feeling, not only for the players, also for us outside. Come on, keep pushing and try again.”

There was similar support when Barnsley last went a man down early on, in their 1-1 draw with Leicester City last month.

The reality is that the bulk of Barnsley fan anger is aimed at the club hierarchy. If there is deemed to be fight and at least an adequate level of tactical cohesion, those on the pitch can be shielded from the anger that is bubbling up.

During Stendel’s first reign as Reds boss, there was a team spirit with which the supporters could resonate. The challenge before him in his second tenure is considerably greater – but there was undoubtedly some nostalgia in the air on Saturday.

Barnsley: Slicker, Kay, Gale, Shepherd, Larkeche; McGeehan, Connell; Yoganathan (Johnson 78), Kelly (Kirk 78), Cleary (Brownlie 65); Adeyemo (Okedina 12).

#1901. Liverpool vs. Arsenal: Andoni Iraola explains Trey Nyoni start against Premier League champions

By Ben Knapton | 01 Nov 2026 15:56, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 16:06

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has explained his reasoning for handing Trey Nyoni his first Premier League start in Sunday's clash with champions Arsenal at Anfield.

The 19-year-old was surprisingly named in the Liverpool starting lineup for the visit of the holders, getting the nod over the more experienced Ryan Gravenberch alongside Alexis Mac Allister.

Speaking to Sky Sports ahead of kickoff, Iraola hailed Nyoni's on and off-ball work as key factors in his decision to start the 2007-born midfielder in such a crucial game.

"The thinking is that he's playing very well and we trust him. I think he gives us good control on the ball. I think he also understands the game well," Iraola said.

"Without the ball, I think he's smart to deal with all the complications that Arsenal put there in the middle – they start rotating players. I think he's pretty good on those things. We definitely trust Trey to do well."

Nyoni had made 12 substitute appearances in the Premier League before making his full debut against Arsenal, although he was given the nod against Chelsea in the fourth round of the EFL Cup in midweek.

The teenager also featured from the off against LASK Linz and Villarreal in the Champions League, and he has emulated former Liverpool starlet Raheem Sterling with his start against Arsenal.

Indeed, Nyoni is only the second Liverpool teenager to make their first Premier League start for the club against the reigning champions, after Sterling against Manchester City in 2012.

Nyoni previously came off the bench against Nottingham Forest, Ipswich Town, Bournemouth, Manchester City, Brentford and Brighton & Hove Albion earlier in the Premier League season, playing 58 minutes against the Bees after replacing the injured Dominik Szoboszlai.

The latter is only fit enough for the bench following his latest hamstring setback, though, as Florian Wirtz continues as Liverpool's creative focal point.

However, Iraola has also suggested that both Szoboszlai and Victor Munoz - who is also among the substitutes following a knee problem - will be in line for minutes in the second half.

"We have to consider we have very good options for the second half. We are recovering Victor [Munoz], recovering Dom [Szoboszlai] – I think it gives us good options for the second half," Iraola added.

Liverpool will move to within three points of Arsenal and Manchester City in the Premier League table with a win against the Gunners, who have not triumphed in the top flight at Anfield since 2012.

#1899. Sheffield Wednesday 1 Blackpool 1: Owls showcase flair and fight for Dave Challinor to work with

But League One is about more than just that. No team can play pretty football 50-plus times in a season, and there are days when you just have to dig in.

Sil Swinkels' debatable first-half red card turned Sunday at home to Blackpool into one of them and, cheered on by a crowd of 30,674, they dug in for victory, only to have to settle for a 1-1 draw.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Spirit was not to blame in a squad ravaged by injuries, but 41 minutes with a man light and the ex-factor of Jerry Yates, the South Yorkshire-born striker who spent the second half of last season on loan at Hillsborough, did for them.

Even after his frustratingly simple 81st-minute goal, the 10 men refused to settle for just a paint, but in the end it was all they could take.

Normally new managers inherit teams low on morale, quality or both, but Challinor, appointed hours before kick-off, cannot grumble on either front.

Having taken a while to find their feet, when they did the Owls played some good flowing football as he watched on from the director's box.

Matt Hamshaw often used a 3-4-1-2 at Rotherham United, and for the forwards Challinor will inherit, putting three central makes some sense. Davis Keillor-Dunn, Callum Slattery and Mason Burstow combined well.

"I was looking to see how I could get two up front and work backwards from there,” explained the caretaker manager.

played a lovely ball in behind in the 14th minute, but the man who got on the end was wearing tangerine orange.

A minute later, a good flowing mov got the ball out to Max Low, but he made a mess of his stabbed shot.

Burstow shot from distance without troubling Bailey Peacock-Farrell on his return to Hillsborough.

The Northern Irishman gave the ball away to left wing-back Lowe in the 21st minute but Keillor-Dunn, twice, and Slattery had shots blocked.

When the corner came in, the Kop started celebrating a goal for Burstow, who had earlier dinked a ball from Swinkels wide under pressure, but he missed the target again, this time under far less duress.

For all the good football the Owls were playing, the game came from a gift to Keillor-Dunn the day before his 29th birthday.

Leighton Clarkson was trying to find right-back Andy Lyon but instead picked the forward out. Keillor-Dunn drove forward and found the bottom corner.

Lyon had missed a free header at a corner and Ernie Waver made an excellent tackle after Dion Taylor turned Swinkels too easily, but at 1-0 up it was hard to see past a home win.

That was until Swinkels was sent off 40 minutes into his first start since August.

The centre-back was penalised as the last man when he fouled Tom Bloxham, who appeared to be going away from goal.

Suddenly, Keillor-Dunn and Slattery had to play wide in a 4-4-1.

Blackpool struggled to make inroads in the first half of the second half, although Hayden Coulson missed the target with a gilt-edged opportunity, and Burstow needed to throw himself in the line of fire for a mighty block.

The hosts, inevitably, had to rely on sporadic moments but Keillor-Dunn almost caught Peacock-Farrell AWOL, shooting wide from inside his own half, and forced the former Leeds United goalkeeper into an excellent stretching tip-over.

So Ian Evatt played all his remaining cards in the 67th minute, throwing on his last four substitutes at once and going to a 3-1-2-4 shape with former Owl Yates and ex-Huddersfield Town striker Dion Charles at the head.

Josh Bowler forced a good save from Ashley Maynard-Brewer in the 76th and although Yan Valery responded by bringing Peacock-Farrell into the game as Burstow lay injured, it made sense for Hamshaw to try to lock the door more securely.

But within seconds of bringing Keillor-Dunn off so Ricardo Santos could restore the back three, Blackpool equalised.

Inevitably it was Hamshaw's good friend Yates, shrugging off Weaver to the very obvious disappointment of the youngster, to apply a first-time finish to a long ball.

The Owls refused to accept their fate, Burstow showing Keillor-Dunn how to do it with an effort from the halfway line that Peacock-Farrell only just scrambled around his post, then bringing on Harry Gray and Kieran Morrison, with defender Lowe one of those making way.

But Blackpool wanted three points too, defender Olly Casey striking the crossbar with a long-range effort, but Hamshaw's stint as caretaker manager ended with consecutive draws – something for the new man to build on.

Sheffield Wednesday: Maynard-Brewer; Palmer, Weaver, Swinkels; Valery, Heskey, Bannan, M Lowe (Gray 89); Slattery; Burstow (Morrison 89), Keillor-Dunn (Santos 81).
