#1878. Serie A preview: AC Milan vs. Inter – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

On Saturday night, AC Milan face Inter in a game that needs little to no introduction. It’s time for the Derby della Madonnina.

After their defeat in midweek, Milan must end October on a high note. It’s a game that could define their season – a daunting sentence to say only a few months into the campaign – such are the sides of the scale.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ruben Amorim was happy to admit that his side needed to improve after the recent inconsistencies in his press conference on Friday night, and with two defeats in three games, he’s unfortunately right.

Game date: Saturday, October 31 Kick-off time: 20:45 (CET) Venue: San Siro Referee: Marco Guida (VAR: Mazzoleni)

As mentioned, this is a huge game for Milan, simply because of how they arrive at this game. Defeats to Bournemouth and Bologna in their last two midweek fixtures have had an impact on hopes for this season.

So, if they are to prove that they are ready to compete, they must show it against one of Europe’s best sides. Saying that, the Nerazzurri are not invincible and Amorim’s side can get the better of them at San Siro, but they will have to fight for 90 minutes.

Unfortunately, the Portuguese’s job is not made much easier, with several injuries still to contend with. Fikayo Tomori headed to the medical room this week, after suffering a torn muscle in his right thigh.

He joins Matteo Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze, amongst others there. However, Amorim has been given the boost of three potential returns. Indeed, Adrien Rabiot, Mario Gila and Diego Moreira are all expected to be available in some capacity. To what extent, though, remained largely unknown for most of Friday.

Looking at the loss to Bologna, the injury issues had clearly had an impact on the team, as Ruben Amorim named a heavily rotated side, with only five starters on the pitch from the first minute. Though that may have been to combat Saturday’s game.

In the defence, there will be no changes to the core, as Mike Maignan starts in goal, with Koni De Winter and Strahinja Pavlovic ahead of him. However, both full-backs will be changed, with Gila returning to the starting XI, alongside Davide Bartesaghi.

Luka Modric also returns in a starting role alongside Rabiot, who will be entrusted with a starting role after recovering. Then, it will be a full-strength attack, or close to it.

Omari Hutchinson keeps his spot, with the Englishman showing signs of consistency, whilst Moreira also returns from injury. After signing his renewal – which could be worth €10 million per season – Christian Pulisic will start behind Goncalo Ramos.

Updated with the latest Gazzetta dello Sport prediction below

Predicted Milan XI (4-3-3): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Pavlovic, Diawara; Musah, Modric, Rabiot; Moreira, Ramos, Pulisic.

Predicted bench: Torriani, Bouyer, Estupinan, Vladimirov, M. Cissé, Vos, Perera, Bartesaghi, F. Terracciano, Musah, Jashari, Comotto, Ossola, Menon, Camarda, Cisse.

Injuries & suspensions: Chukwueze, Gabbia, Tomori, Saelemaekers, P. Terracciano.

In the summer, Inter oversaw a period of change, with several of the old guard departing. Davide Frattesi headed to Lazio on loan, Denzel Dumfries left to Real Madrid for €20 million, whilst Stefan de Vrij, Yann Sommer, Francesco Acerbi and Matteo Darmian all departed as free agents.

Changes would also come with the incoming mercato, though, as the Nerazzurri spent more than €100m. Djed Spence, Manuel Akanji, John Stones and Curtis Jones arrived from the Premier League, for a combined fee of €75m. Then, Aleksandar Stankovic returned from Club Brugge, with Ivan Provedel also making the switch from Lazio.

Whether those names have been an upgrade so far is difficult to tell, but it’s certainly been an introduction of a new wave of talent.

After dominating in Serie A last season, Inter have started the season in similar fashion, only dropping points to Roma so far. However, they’ve been something of comeback kings, regularly finding an escape when behind.

In fact, in their last three Serie A games, they’ve conceded the first goal – including the midweek disallowed goal against Venezia – yet they’ve always ended up with three points. The inevitability from recent seasons hasn’t disappeared.

What makes this potentially more frustrating is that they’re also struggling with injuries, but still getting results. Without Lautaro Martinez, Stones, Jones and Benjamin Pavard, a drop-off would’ve been understandable, but it hasn’t happened.

After their win in midweek, considering their schedule has also been rough, Chivu rotated slightly. So, there will be a few changes made this weekend to rotate back to their full-strength XI.

In the backline, Manuel Akanji will return to the centre of the back three, replacing Carlos Augusto. Whilst Alessandro Bastoni and Yann Bisseck will start either side of the Swiss defender. Of course, Ivan Provedel remains between the sticks.

Across the midfield, changes will be slightly more common. Federico Dimarco and Andy Diouf will remain on the flanks, whilst Piotr Zielinski retains his starting spot. Though Nicolo Barella and Hakan Calhanoglu both return to the starting XI.

Marcus Thuram will be given a starting role, hoping to continue his fine form this season, but Ange-Yoan Bonny will return to the bench. Pio Esposito will take his place instead.

Predicted Inter XI (3-5-2): Provedel; Bisseck, Akanji, Bastoni; Diouf, Barella, Calhanoglu, Zielinski, Dimarco; Thuram, Esposito

Predicted bench: Martinez, Di Gennaro, Augusto, Jakirovic, Bovio, Mkhitaryan, Lavelli, Mosconi, Spence, Bonny, Stankovic, Sucic.

Injuries & suspensions: Pavard, Jones, Stones, Martinez, Henrique.

Saturday’s contest will be the 243rd meeting between the two sides and, after the horrific period of defeats between 2023 and 2024, Inter sit the happier of the two, with 88 wins to the Rossoneri’s 83.

Saying that, it’s the Diavolo who are currently enjoying a better time of things, having avoided defeat in their last seven meetings. Last season, this record was made even better, with a double taking place, thanks to two 1-0 victories, with goals from Christian Pulisic and Pervis Estupinan.

➤ AC Milan have won three of their last four Serie A matches against Inter (D1), as many as they had in their previous 16 meetings (D4 L9). The Rossoneri have won their last two matches and have not won three consecutive matches against the Nerazzurri since a run of four under Carlo Ancelotti between 2002 and 2004.

➤ Inter have won more matches (70) and scored more goals (260) against Milan than any other team in Serie A history. However, the Nerazzurri have also conceded 236 goals against the Rossoneri, fewer than those conceded against Roma (237) and Juventus (270); with 496 goals in total, the Milan derby could become the third match in the competition’s history to reach the 500-goal mark, after Inter-Roma (544) and Inter-Fiorentina (502).

➤ Milan have collected 18 points from their first nine games of this Serie A season, the same amount they achieved at the same point last season; in five of their previous six seasons in the top flight, the Rossoneri have collected at least 21 points after the first 10 games, with the sole exception of 2024/25 (17).

➤ AC Milan have lost four of their last eight home games in Serie A (W3 D1), as many as they had suffered in their previous 29 (W15 D10); furthermore, the Rossoneri have conceded six goals in their last two home games, one more than they had conceded in their previous five.

➤ Inter have scored in each of their last 19 Serie A matches, the longest unbroken streak among teams currently in the top flight; their last game without a goal came against AC Milan on March 8, 2026.

➤ Since the start of last season, Inter have scored at least two goals in 16 away league matches; only Bayern Munich (18) have done better in the top five European leagues, with Barcelona sharing the same figure as the Nerazzurri.

➤ Inter and Milan are the only two teams in Serie A this season to already have two players with at least four goals scored: Marcus Thuram and Lautaro Martínez for the Nerazzurri, and Adrien Rabiot and Alphadjo Cisse for the Rossoneri.

➤ Hakan Çalhanoglu played 135 Serie A matches for AC Milan between 2017 and 2021, scoring 22 goals and providing 31 assists. The Nerazzurri midfielder hasn’t been involved in a single goal in his last four matches for the Rossoneri in the tournament, after having been involved in four goals in his first five (two goals, both penalties, and two assists).

➤ After his brace on the last matchday, Alphadjo Cisse reached four goals in Serie A at 20 years and 6 days; if he were to score his fifth goal at 20 years and 9 days, he would become the seventh-youngest player in AC Milan’s history to do so, and the third in the three-point-for-a-win era, after Alexandre Pato and Stephan El Shaarawy.

➤ Francesco Pio Esposito, at 21 years and 125 days, could become Inter’s youngest Italian goalscorer in a Serie A derby since the three-point-for-a-win era; among Nerazzurri players of any nationality, only Obafemi Martins and Ronaldo have scored in a league derby at an earlier age during this period.

For the visitors, Marcus Thuram will always be a player to keep an eye on. The Frenchman is the leader of the attack, especially with Lautaro Martinez out, and he has hurt the Diavolo previously. If given the chance, he’ll do so again.

The flanks could be decisive on Saturday, and Federico Dimarco is another who can and will haunt San Siro if given the chance on Halloween. Facing Mario Gila will be no easy task, but if any wide player is to take advantage of the makeshift right back, it’ll be him.

Arundel were welcoming Westfield to Mill Road for the first time, with both sides sitting in mid-table.

#1876. Shakhtar Donetsk vs Sporting Lisbon - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 01 Nov 2026 16:30

Shakhtar Donetsk and Sporting Lisbon will both be looking to bounce back from their first defeats of the 2026-27 Champions League campaign when they meet at Stamford Bridge - the Ukrainian side's temporary home ground - on Tuesday evening.

Separated by just two points in the league-phase table, the Portuguese outfit sit 12th with six points, five places above the nominal hosts, who are playing their European home matches at the West London stadium due to the ongoing conflict in Ukraine.

Shakhtar have made a positive start to their domestic campaign, sitting top of the Ukrainian Premier League with 28 points from 11 matches, although their progress in Europe has been less convincing.

Arda Turan's side have collected four points from their opening three league-phase fixtures, beginning with a 1-1 draw at PSV Eindhoven before recording a 3-1 victory over AEK Athens, though they suffered a 1-0 defeat to 10-man Inter Milan in their most recent continental outing.

The Ukrainian champions have responded well on the domestic front, though, following that setback with an emphatic Ukrainian Cup victory over Dynamo Kyiv, a draw against Zorya Luhansk and Friday's 2-0 success over Obolon, inspired by Alisson Santana.

Both goals in their latest league outing came after the 70th minute, but Turan will want his side to make a faster start on Tuesday, knowing that Shakhtar have won 18 of their last 24 matches as hosts in the Champions League proper when leading at half time (D4, L1).

However, the Miners have a poor head-to-head record to overcome, having lost both previous meetings against this very opponent, with each encounter ending in a 1-0 defeat during the 2008-09 Champions League group stage.

Sporting, meanwhile, made a stronger start to their Champions League campaign, winning their opening two matches against Galatasaray and Lens before a 3-2 home defeat to debutants LASK Linz on matchday three brought their four-game winning run in the league phase to an end.

That setback was part of a two-match losing streak that sparked protests from supporters, with Rui Borges's side also suffering a league defeat at home to newly promoted Academico de Viseu, though the Lions have since returned to winning ways.

After overcoming Maritimo in the Taca da LIga last Tuesday, the Lions secured a 2-0 victory away to Casa Pia, leaving them third in the Primeira Liga table, albeit nine points adrift of the summit.

Tuesday's encounter gives under-fire Borges another opportunity to win back the trust of the club's supporters and board, while Sporting will also be keen to strengthen their hopes of securing another automatic place in the Champions League knockout rounds after finishing seventh in the league phase last season.

The Portuguese visitors can also take confidence from their impressive record against Ukrainian opposition, having won seven of the last eight such meetings, including each of their most recent four.

Shakhtar Donetsk form (all competitions):

Shakhtar will be without Pedrinho, who faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines following thigh surgery, while Eguinaldo (shoulder) and Marlon Santos (muscle) are also expected to miss out through injury.

Pedro Henrique is likely to return at left-back after making way for Irakli Azarov, who made his first start for the club following his return from injury, while Alisson is also expected to be recalled after making an impact off the bench last time out.

Sporting are likely to remain without Zeno Debast and Rodrigo Zalazar, who are both dealing with muscular injuries, while Nuno Santos is still working his way back from a lengthy knee tendon layoff.

Nestory Irankunda is also a doubt after suffering a knee knock against Casa Pia, although he completed recovery work with the starters, meaning Flavio Goncalves could be an alternative if the Australian is not fit to feature.

Luis Suarez failed to score against Casa Pia, ending a 10-match scoring run across all competitions, though the Colombian has found the net in three consecutive Champions League appearances, equalling the Sporting record held by Sa Pinto and Nani.

Shakhtar Donetsk possible starting lineup:

Riznyk; Tobias, Bondar, Matviyenko, P Henrique; Nazaryna, Ocheretko, Isaque; Alisson, Elias, Mendoza

Sporting Lisbon possible starting lineup:

Kaique; Fresneda, Quaresma, Inacio, M Araujo; Doumbia, Altimira; Catamo, P Lima, Irankunda; L Suarez

Shakhtar have shown enough in recent weeks to suggest they can make life difficult for Sporting, who have not been entirely convincing in their recent outings, although the Portuguese side's greater quality could prove decisive.

#1870. GdS: Ten-point risk and high ambitions – three keys for Amorim in Milan-Inter

AC Milan are taking on their city rivals Inter this morning, and for Ruben Amorim, there is one key player in each department.

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Milan are entering the derby at a pretty clear disadvantage, currently seven points behind Inter in the standings. Ruben Amorim made it clear yesterday that the Scudetto remains the goal, but if the gap is increased to ten, it will be tough.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s true that Stefano Pioli, in February 2022, also risked going ten points behind until Olivier Giroud turned the game around. The problem is that his successor Goncalo Ramos hasn’t even scored a goal in the league since the end of August.

Furthermore, Cristian Chivu and his Inter have been in very good form lately and will be looking to end their seven-game run without a win in the fixture. It’s going to be a night with a lot of emotions, so let’s see how it will pan out on the pitch.

Mario Gila’s return is absolutely essential for Milan, but it will take more from them to regain solidity at the back. The Rossoneri have conceded four more goals than they did at this point last season, and six in their last two home games.

Switching from Max Allegri’s low block to Amorim’s more proactive style of play has clearly come with a cost. Yet, it’s not like the Rossoneri have been pressing like crazy so far, which is obvious when you compare them with Inter.

The Nerazzurri have a much higher centre of gravity (54.7-48.5 m), they steal more balls in the final third of the pitch (41-28), and they shoot more from offensive recoveries (13-7). Meanwhile, Milan are continuing to concentrate, play vertically and run quickly.

There is also another truth that needs to be highlighted: too many goals have been conceded due to individual errors. Amorim is well aware of this and it might have something to do with the decision to start Sankhoun Diawara on the left, with effectively four centre-backs in the back four.

In midfield, just like with Gila in defence, Amorim can count on another crucial return: Adrien Rabiot, the team’s top scorer along with Alphadjo Cisse (4 goals). For Milan, the midfielders are crucial with their goals.

The midfield is indeed the centre of Milan’s power, where the Ballon d’Or winner Luka Modric reigns supreme and where counterattacks that end up in goal are born. Amorim’s choices in this department weren’t easy.

The most tested on the eve of the match: a 4-3-3 with Musah and Rabiot on either side of Modric, and an attacking trident of Moreira-Ramos-Pulisic.

There were fewer doubts for Chivu who has a tested midfield and, in general, the most coherent team in the league. But that doesn’t mean they don’t have problems. Against Venezia, Inter suffered six dangerous transitions, against Roma there were seven.

In the middle of the pitch, due to the pressure of pressing or laziness in the return, there have often been gaps to exploit. It’s extremely dangerous to leave that space against galloping players like Diego Moreira, Christian Pulisic, and Rabiot.

The Frenchman, who already crippled Inter on the counterattack as a Juventus player (goal and assist for Kostic), could become a key factor in the derby.

Despite conceding one fewer goal than a year ago (10-11), as the pink newspaper continues, Inter appear to be more vulnerable at the back. The centre-backs have dipped in form and the conceded xG is much higher, which Milan will try to exploit.

Ramos is pushing hard to score his third league goal, which he desperately needs despite adding a lot to Milan’s game: 14 balls recovered (Thuram 4, Lautaro 5, Pio 8), 21 lay-offs (Thuram 7, Lautaro 8, Pio 13). All he has to do is find the net.

However, if the player that Milan fear the most is Thuram, then that player is Pulisic for Inter. He decided the penultimate derby, scored in the one that stopped the haemorrhage of six defeats, and also impressed in the Supercoppa Italiana.

He knows the art of hiding between the lines and striking from the attacking midfield, which Inter’s 3-5-2 often struggles to achieve. Perhaps he can celebrate his contract renewal by deciding yet another derby.

The incident in question occurred in the 21st minute at Anfield with Liverpool searching for an equaliser after falling behind to Kai Havertz’s third Premier League goal of the season.

From a free-kick, Alexander Isak appeared to have his shirt pulled in the box by Jurrien Timber and replays proved it did enough to stop the in-form Liverpool striker from making contact with the teasing cross.

However, to the surprise of Reds head coach Andoni Iraola, no penalty was awarded and Sky Sports presenter Dave Jones then revealed at half-time that the incident was checked and cleared by VAR.

Daniel Sturridge, speaking on Sky Sports’ Super Sunday show said the VAR officials had made a mistake as the shirt pull was “clear and blatant”.

"If he [Isak] makes more of it, it's a penalty. I don't think he makes enough of it,” Sturridge said. “It's clear and blatant."

Ian Wright, a former Arsenal striker, admitted his former club got away with the decision.

He said: “He shouldn't have to make more of it. We can see it. As an Arsenal man, I'm glad we got away with it.

"Unless I'm pulled back, I'm going to head it as much as I can. When he pulled him, it was just about enough as he would need to go down."

Jamie Carragher, meanwhile, did not mince his words when delivering a verdict on the VAR decision.

He said: "One of the best goalscorers in the league is pulled back seven yards out and it stops him heading the ball - why does he need to make a meal of it?

#1867. Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal: Kai Havertz goal sends champions top and ends long Anfield hoodoo

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal recorded a first Premier League win at Anfield in 14 years but needed some help from Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker, whose first-half error led to Kai Havertz’s solitary goal in the 1-0 win.

Not since manager Mikel Arteta was running the Gunners’ midfield in 2012 had they tasted victory in the red half of Merseyside and they were tested to the limit in ending end that run.

However, if it is one thing Arteta’s side are well-drilled at it is seeing out games having maximised their opportunities and the celebrations in front of the visiting fans having moved top of the table showed how significant they felt this result was.

And while most of the football was played by Liverpool after going behind it did not bring any rewards – partly due to poor judgement and execution but also bad luck.

How Jurrien Timber’s tug on the shirt of Alexander Isak as he tried to connect with a header escaped the eagle eye of VAR will remain a question, especially as they were quick to look into a more regular coming together of Cody Gakpo and Christos Tzolis.

By then the hosts were already behind after another miscalculation by Alisson.

A week ago against Brighton the Brazil international had got away with a few loose passes in the win against Brighton. Arsenal were not so forgiving.

His attempted pass to Jeremy Jacquet gave the centre-back no chance of retaining possession and the loose ball was seized upon by Arsenal, who moved it the right where Noni Madueke and Declan Rice combined for Havertz to tap in at the far post.

The margins were always going to be tight in a match between the current champions, who have won all five league games when scoring the game’s first this season, and their predecessors and that one error proved to be the difference as for all their pressure Liverpool failed to test David Raya.

Much of that was down to the hosts’ lack of composure in the final third – Raya did not have to make a save – and Arsenal’s experience at doing the necessary dirty work to deny those opportunities.

#1865. Arsenal: Why Noni Madueke avoided a red card against Liverpool as Premier League issue statement

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

The Premier League have issued a statement explaining why Noni Madueke was not sent off in Arsenal’s win over Liverpool.

As the huge Premier League showdown at Anfield entered its closing stages on Sunday afternoon, Madueke clashed with Alexis Mac Allister after the Liverpool midfielder had fouled Martin Odegaard.

While the Gunners were awarded a free-kick on the edge of their own box, Mac Allister was not happy with the decision and had words with Odegaard - who was on the floor - and appeared to tap the Arsenal captain on the head.

Madueke then came rushing over and leaned his head into Mac Allister as the two players came face-to-face, thus risking a potential red card for violent conduct.

Interestingly, the Arsenal winger was already on a yellow card but referee Andy Madley did not punish Madueke, instead showing a yellow card to Mac Allister and Jurrien Timber.

The Premier League’s match centre have now confirmed that Madueke avoided a red card because his action was not considered aggressive or violent.

A statement reads: “The referee’s call of no violent conduct by Madueke on Mac Allister was checked and confirmed by VAR.

“VAR: “All of the situations have been checked and cleared. There is some contact as Madueke and Mac Allister square-up. In my opinion, it's not forceful, not violent, not brutal”.”

Gary Neville, who was on co-commentary duty for Sky Sports, slammed the Liverpool midfielder for going down far too easily and praised the VAR officials for not advising the referee to produce a red card.

"Well done to VAR because they're recognised that Mac Alliser going down is embarrassing,” Neville said.

#1863. Andoni Iraola reacts to 'clear' Liverpool penalty in Arsenal defeat: 'I don’t understand'

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has said he will tell Alexander Isak to go to ground next time after being denied a “clear” penalty in the defeat to Arsenal.

Sunday’s huge Premier League showdown at Anfield was settled by Kai Havertz’s solitary goal, but the general consensus - at least in the Sky Sports studio - was that Liverpool should have awarded a chance to equalise.

The controversial moment took place in the 21st minute when Isak appeared to have his shirt pulled in the box by Jurrien Timber.

While replays showed contact was enough to stop the in-form Liverpool striker from connecting with the cross, referee Andy Madley opted to not point to the spot and VAR agreed with the on-field decision.

This came shortly after Liverpool had another penalty appeal turned down when Cody Gakpo went to ground under a challenge from Christos Tzolis.

Speaking after the game, Iraola said he could understand why the apparent foul on the Dutchman was not given but insisted Timber should have been penalised for stopping Isak from getting a shot on target.

“The Alex one is a clear penalty,” Iraola told Sky Sports. “We can all see that [Timber] holds the t-shirt and the ball just goes one centimetre in front of Alex.

“Alex is going to hit the ball in front of the goal.

“So because he does not go to the floor, you are not going to call the penalty? I don’t understand it.”

Iraola was then asked if Isak should have made more of the pull as the Liverpool striker, instead of appealing for the decision, appeared to have words with Timber as the pair jogged alongside each other.

"The fact that you are even asking me that he should have gone to the floor, that's the thing,” the Spaniard added.

“If he goes to the floor, they call the penalty for me. They call the penalty 100%.”

Iraola finished up by saying he will “definitely” tell Isak to make more of any contact inside the box in the future.

#1862. Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang

Mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

“Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

There will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

As it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

There was also another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

“They know how to do it,” Arteta said of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”

Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

“Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they showed it,” Lampard said. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”

"They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard said Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt

Before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he said, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

If that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

The energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment new signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

The opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

Coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their new club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

Saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the new £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Odegaard showed in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

"It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx

From there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

"How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I

"I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE

It’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the new season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J

There will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

Awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

Torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

Coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

Odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

Lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

Lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

Here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

Tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

The visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his new side.

Odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

The ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a big deflection and flies out for a corner.

From a Coventry corner, Arsenal counter attack with such intensity and speed. The move ends as Odegaard attempts to find Tzolis with a through ball, but the Norwegian overhits the pass and delayed it too long. The offside flag is then raised against Tzolis.

Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

It’s a nightmare start to the second half for Coventry. Whatever Arteta said to his players at the break has worked wonders.

Lewis-Skelly then shoots from long range and his shot is tipped over the bar by Rushworth.

White overlaps Saka and latches onto the winger’s pass. Saka then tees up Odegaard, who scuffs his close-range effort. Rushworth is wrong-footed and despite getting a glove to it, the ball trickles into the net and Arsenal are cruising.

It's Martin Odegaard... Arsenal have three! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/LrqSSGJWE6

Odegaard has scored some beautiful goals in an Arsenal shirt. That wasn’t one of them. He won’t care, though. Two goals in two games for the Arsenal captain.

Read more about his return to form here: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/08/21/odegaard-a-man-possessed-in-bid-to-unlock-arsenal-attack/

We are back under way for the second half. Will Arsenal add more goals to their tally or can Coventry produce a memorable comeback?

It’s been a steep learning curve for the newly-promoted side, who have been overpowered and outclassed by Arsenal’s quality.

Arsenal are in complete control thanks to a commanding first half display against Coventry. Havertz and Saka have the goals, with the reigning Premier League champions on course to claim a routine three points to kickstart their title defence.

Once again, Saka plays a short corner. Odegaard then passes to Rice, who is in acres of space on the edge of the penalty area. The midfielder shoots, but his curling effort drifts narrowly wide of the far post.

There will be two minutes of added time at the end of this half.

The ball bobbles into Tchaouna’s path and the winger tries a very ambitious acrobatic effort from the edge of the box. It had Raya worried for a second, but the effort lands on the roof of the net. That would have been a spectacular goal if it had sneaked in.

Tzolis teases Thomas and works some space before clipping a cross in towards Havertz. The forward doesn’t connect with the header and Coventry scramble it clear.

Odegaard is pulling the strings and slips a delightful pass through to the onrushing White, who finds himself very far forward, but the right back is swiftly closed down by Coventry’s defence as he shoots.

At the other end, Simms does brilliantly to turn Gabriel and win a free kick just outside the box. The Brazilian centre back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

Coventry are feeling the full effects of the stark difference in levels between Championship and Premier League. Arsenal look streets ahead at the moment.

Christos Tzolis has only played a few games for Arsenal but it’s already easy to see why he registered 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He has shown on numerous occasions this summer that he is willing to cross the ball as soon as he receives it. No delay, no faff. It worked against Manchester City last weekend and it created Saka’s goal here.

Welcome back to the Premier League, Coventry... It’s been a chastening opening 27 minutes for Lampard’s side.

Yirenkyi then receives a yellow card on his debut for pulling Lewis-Skelly’s shirt.

Rice strides through midfield and plays a one-two with Odegaard. The English midfielder tees up Tzolis, whose fires a cross into the corridor of uncertainty. Rushworth parries it into the danger zone, gifting an unmarked Saka a simple finish from close range. What a start for the champions!

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Arsenal are purring and oozing confidence. Coventry need to be careful and must stay in this game. They cannot allow Arsenal to get a second and run away with this.

Coventry had started well but their first error in defence was ruthlessly punished. That’s Havertz’s 10th goal in his last 17 matches for club and country (including pre-season friendlies). After such an injury-disrupted campaign last year, he’s had a very good summer.

Van Ewijk fails to clear his lines and he’s closed down by Tzolis. The ball ricochets into Calafiori’s path and the left back picks out Havertz with a low cross.

The German sweeps a composed shot into the bottom corner. It’s such a cultured finish and Arsenal begin their defence of the Premier League with a 1-0 lead after 15 minutes.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

Some steady possession for Coventry, who are looking to take the sting and excitement out of the game while also calming the buoyant Arsenal fans down.

Tzolis pops up on the right wing and latches onto Rice’s pass. The attacker then delivers a first-time cross into the box which finds Saka, whose half-volley is blocked by Amenda.

Arsenal then work a short corner that ends with White teeing up Tzolis, but his low strike is smothered by Coventry’s defence. Tzolis has certainly made a lively start, and unsurprisingly, Arsenal’s set pieces are causing some early problems.

Tzolis looks dangerous as he dribbles at Van Ewijk, before cutting inside and unleashing a powerful shot. However, his effort is high and wide. Nevertheless, it’s positive play from Arsenal’s new signing.

Following that Coventry corner, the Premier League holders have monopolised the possession in the early minutes. Chants of ‘Champions of England, we know what we are’ ring around the stadium thanks to the home support, who are in full voice.

Coventry get us under way and the newly-promoted side have won an early corner, which is comfortably dealt with by Arsenal’s defence.

The atmosphere at the Emirates is electric. Can Arsenal flex their title-winning credentials once again or will Coventry cause an almighty upset?

New Arsenal signing Ezri Konsa has been presented on the pitch, with both sets of players set to follow him any moment now.

The 2026-27 season is just minutes away from kicking off.

Coventry have recruited some powerful, aggressive players this summer. They will be looking to frustrate Arsenal by shutting down the spaces around their penalty area, and they will certainly be competitive at set-pieces.

Meanwhile, the Arsenal fans have just had their first glimpse of Ezri Konsa in the club’s shirt. The new signing walked out onto the pitch to wave to the supporters.

With just over five minutes until the 2026-27 Premier League season starts, here are tonight’s teams in full...

Arsenal: Raya, White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori, Odegaard, Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.

Subs: Arrizabalaga, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Nwaneri, Merino, Zubimendi, Dowman.

Coventry: Rushworth, van Ewijk, Thomas, Amenda, Dasilva, Onyeka, Yirenkyi, Grimes, Thomas-Asante, Simms, Tchaouna.

Subs: Wilson, Rudoni, Sakamoto, Awoniyi, Kitching, Latibeaudiere, Eccles, Overgaard, Hamer.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “He had a slight tension in his groin. He hasn’t done a pre-season, he only had four or five days before that [Man City] game. We have to take a lot of new stuff for him as well. We need to take it bit by bit.”

Another game, another snub for Gabriel Martinelli. As was the case against Manchester City in last weekend’s Community Shield, the Brazilian isn’t even on the bench tonight. It’s quite clear what’s going on here: Arsenal need to make sales and he is an obvious candidate to depart. It’s not particularly pleasant, though, and you can’t help but feel for a player who has been so important to this club over the last seven years.

Martinelli has made it clear he does not want to move to Galatasary, who made an offer recently. Will a more suitable club come forward for him? We’ll find out in the coming days.

In two full seasons at Coventry between 2021 and 2023, Viktor Gyokeres scored 40 goals in 97 games for Coventry, and was part of the side that lost on penalties to Luton Town in the Championship play-off final to Luton Town.

If Coventry had won that game, would Gyokeres still be wearing a sky blue shirt instead of joining Sporting CP and then Arsenal, who knows...

The striker will have to wait to get onto the pitch against his former team, with Mikel Arteta choosing Kai Havertz to lead the line.

Odegaard comes into the new Premier League season, which begins when Arsenal host Coventry City on Friday night, with a point to prove. That may sound unusual, given his new-found status as a title-winning captain, but last year was a strange one for the 27-year-old. The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

Last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

Arteta looks raring to go and ready to mount another title charge.

"Everything has to start with me" 💪Mikel Arteta says Arsenal are ready for the new Premier League season 💥 pic.twitter.com/rsUcs7ot7T

After last season’s Championship by a whopping 95 points under Frank Lampard’s management, Coventry head into their first Premier League campaign since suffering relegation from the competition in 2001.

Coventry were playing in the fourth tier as recently as 2017, so lining up against the Premier League holders is a full-circle moment for the club and supporters that is richly deserved.

"I loved it, I loved driving here, feeling the atmosphere, the fans" Frank Lampard on what tonight means for him and Coventry 😍Watch live here: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/077Bga2Z4W

On Friday night, at the home of champions Arsenal, Coventry officially begin a new chapter back in the Premier League and expectations will be high. The man responsible for that tidal wave of optimism is Lampard, their promotion hero.

He has proved a transformative appointment since arriving in November 2024, and the former England and Chelsea captain is relishing the chance to rattle some cages.

His return is a feel-good story and Lampard has a point to prove. He admits that the desire to upset his detractors drives him on. “I’ve got experience of the Premier League and hopefully I can get that across to the players,” he said.

“The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”

Arsenal ruined Enzo Maresca’s first competitive outing as Man City’s new manager in the club’s first match without Pep Guardiola. It was one-way traffic as Arsenal cruised to a resounding 3-0 win to lift the Community Shield in Cardiff.

Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring just 23 seconds after he was brilliantly played in by Myles Lewis-Skelly’s defence-splitting pass. Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

The Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

"I'm really pleased, that's a really good team" Ian Wright is happy with the Arsenal starting XI to face Coventry, do you agree? 💬 Watch live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/IUBlMS963w

New signings Aurele Amenda, Loum Tchaouna and Caleb Yirenkyi all start and make their Coventry debuts this evening.

Carl Rushworth and Frank Onyeka also begin from the outset after making their moves permanent following successful loans last season.

Your City tonight. 📋 pic.twitter.com/V0nzaemLYF

As Sam Dean confirmed earlier on, Bruno Guimaraes is absent from the squad. The Brazilian was subbed off at half-time in the dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City with a thigh issue.

Both Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka start after being used off the bench in the Community Shield last weekend, with Guimaraes and Noni Madueke dropping to the bench.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your Premier League opening day XI ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/yRf2BEs3BA

To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

The centre back has penned a four-year deal with the option of a further year.

Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, Sporting Director Andrea Berta said: “Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers.

“Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.”

Konsa will play no role in tonight’s encounter, having only completed the move earlier in the day.

Reinforcing the backline ✍️ pic.twitter.com/deYQhZcmOy

Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

#1861. Liverpool vs Arsenal LIVE: Premier League result, latest updates and fan reaction

Arsenal are celebrating their first Premier League win over Liverpool at Anfield for 14 years. Not since September 2012 - when Mikel Arteta lined up in their midfield - had the Gunners emerged victorious at this famous old ground, until Kai Havertz’s 16th-minute finish expertly teed up by Declan Rice ultimately settled a pulsating heavyweight clash on Sunday. It was an excellent start to the game from Arsenal, who were more than up for the fight as they sought to bounce back from their midweek Carabao Cup last-16 humiliation at the hands of fourth-tier Fleetwood.

They were largely dominated thereafter by an in-form Liverpool team seeking a sixth successive win across all competitions under Andoni Iraola to underline their own title credentials, but a stunning rearguard effort proved so effective that the hosts failed to muster a single shot on target despite peppering the box with crosses and creating several golden opportunities - the best of which was wasted by Alexis Mac Allister. Florian Wirtz hit the crossbar, while Arsenal were very fortunate not to concede a penalty for Jurrien Timber’s shirt pull on Alexander Isak.

Mac Allister failed to get Noni Madueke sent off as tempers flared late on and Arsenal saw out a statement win that took them above Manchester City to the top-flight summit, three points clear and now nine ahead of Liverpool in fifth.

The first Arsenal win at Anfield since September 2012 takes them top of the Premier League table.

“An absolute defensive masterclass,” says Gary Neville.

So gritty and hard-fought and they leapfrog Manchester City, who are now three points behind after back-to-back defeats.

The perfect way to respond to that Fleetwood humiliation in midweek.

More than 30 crosses from dominant Liverpool and 17 total shots, but none on target after Opta took away a debatable one from Barcola.

Liverpool stay fifth and now nine points off the summit as their run of five successive victories across all competitions is halted.

95 mins: One more chance for Alisson to boom a free-kick up towards Van Dijk.

Mac Allister‘s shot is blocked by Konsa, but there’s a foul by Isak on Gabriel.

Raya was booked for delaying a free-kick a few minutes ago.

93 mins: Liverpool are throwing everything at this but they just cannot break down an incredible rearguard effort from Arsenal.

Barcola looks the most likely to grab an equaliser, with Szoboszlai also looking dangerous.

But there’s still been nothing to particularly trouble Raya all day.

89 mins: Tsimikas plays it to the back post for fellow Liverpool substitute Munoz, who gets in past Hincapie and Calafiori but doesn’t connect properly with the cross.

SIX minutes of added time are signalled as Barcola’s effort is deflected wide.

Arsenal clear the corner but are quickly under the cosh again...

87 mins: Liverpool are furious as Szoboszlai is denied a free-kick outside the Arsenal box following a challenge by Gyokeres, who can break.

86 mins: Time is quickly running out for Liverpool here as they again probe patiently in search of that elusive equaliser.

They are leaving Van Dijk up top it seems as Calafiori turns away Ngumoha’s cross.

84 mins: We now have two further Arsenal changes with just over five minutes plus stoppage time left to play at Anfield.

Hincapie and Gyokeres replace Tzolis and goalscorer Havertz.

Interesting that there's only 10 minutes left and Arteta has made just one change.

Arsenal have such a deep squad but he's keeping faith with those who are already up to the speed of the game.

Time will tell if that is the right decision or not.

80 mins: Madueke was already on a yellow card there, but he isn’t punished any further.

Instead it’s yellows for Mac Allister and Timber.

A raft of Liverpool changes are now coming.

Tsimikas, Munoz and Koumas replace Kerkez, Araujo and Wirtz.

Hincapie is preparing to come on for Arsenal, meanwhile.

77 mins: It’s all kicking off now at Anfield as Madueke sticks his head in needlessly on Mac Allister, who goes down very theatrically indeed.

Timber initially took exception to Mac Allister slapping Odegaard on the back of the head after a foul on the Arsenal captain, who was on the floor.

Referee Andy Madley has some sorting out to do here.

#1859. Kai Havertz breaks Premier League scoring record, surpasses Man City legend in Liverpool vs. Arsenal

By Ben Knapton | 01 Nov 2026 17:11, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 17:24

Arsenal striker Kai Havertz is now the Premier League's all-time leading German goalscorer following his opener against Liverpool.

The former Chelsea man was given the nod up front over Viktor Gyokeres at Anfield, despite a shoddy display in Tuesday's shock EFL Cup fourth-round loss to Fleetwood Town.

However, Havertz quickly repaid Mikel Arteta's faith in him, latching onto the end of Declan Rice's low cross to the back post and tapping home in the 16th minute.

In doing so, the 27-year-old broke the record for the most Premier League goals ever by a German player, registering his 46th in the English top flight.

Havertz was previously level on 45 with Ilkay Gundogan, but the former Manchester City man has now been surpassed, and the Arsenal centre-forward is in a league of his own.

"Absolutely brilliant from Arsenal." Kai Havertz gives Arsenal an early lead at Anfield! ⚡️ https://t.co/eeyhRcLlel

Havertz's opening goal at Anfield was his third of the 2026-27 Premier League season, and his first on the road, following home strikes against Coventry City and Chelsea.

The former Blues striker scored 19 English top-flight goals for Chelsea, and his tap-in at Anfield marked his 27th in an Arsenal kit, including a personal best 13 in the 2023-24 season.

Havertz is one of three active players in the top 10 for Premier League goals for German footballers, as Brighton & Hove Albion's Pascal Gross is third in the charts with 34 to his name.

Kevin Schade of Brentford is eighth on the list with 24, while Gundogan, Mesut Ozil (33), Jurgen Klinsmann (29), Uwe Rosler (29), Leroy Sane (25), Robert Huth (21) and Lukas Podolski (19) make up the rest of the top 10.

Two penalty shouts for Liverpool! ? Jurrien Timber had hold of Alexander Isak’s shirt before Christos Tzolis had his hands round Cody Gakpo. Should either have been given as a penalty? https://t.co/l4rBpqxLwl

Havertz's goal proved enough to send Arsenal into the half-time break with a 1-0 lead, although both Gunners and Liverpool fans were left bemused as to how.

Andoni Iraola's men dominated their North London counterparts following Havertz's historic goal, and had no fewer than four penalty appeals waved away by the officials.

One such incident saw Jurrien Timber grab Alexander Isak by the shirt as a cross came in, but the Swede did not protest vociferously, and the pull went unpunished.

Timber also escaped a potential handball when sliding to block a cross, while Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo also went down under pressure, but their appeals fell on deaf ears too.

However, Liverpool ultimately failed to score in the first half despite having 28 touches in the Arsenal box, the most the Gunners have ever faced in the opening 45 minutes of a Premier League game.

#1857. Arsenal: Declan Rice 'is a world class midfield player - the Moises Caicedo debate is not close'

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Jamie Carragher has claimed Declan Rice is the best midfielder in the Premier League, while also insisting the Arsenal star has settled the debate with Moises Caicedo.

Last season, pundits as well as Arsenal and Chelsea supporters were split with regard to who was the best midfielder in the league.

Both Rice and Caicedo have established themselves among the leading players in their position since their £100million-plus transfers from West Ham and Brighton respectively in the summer of 2023.

However, after Rice put in an impressive performance in Arsenal’s win over Liverpool on Sunday - providing the assist for Kai Havertz - Carragher is now of the opinion that the England international has cemented his standing as the very best in the division.

"He’s the best midfield player in the Premier League by a long way. It’s not even a debate,” Carragher said on Sky Sports’ Super Sunday post-show.

“It was a debate last season about him and Caicedo, it’s not even close. Declan Rice is the best midfield player in this country.

"I’m not an Arsenal fan, but sometimes I hear people speak about him.

Declan Rice is the best midfield player in this country

"And I’m sort of flabbergasted that they don’t understand football and they’re not watching the same game as me.

“He is a world class midfield player, there is absolutely no doubt about it and one of the best midfield players Arsenal have ever had and they’ve had some great ones when you think of [Patrick] Vieira and Liam Brady going back further.

“He is right up there with the best of them”

Carragher may have been taking a swipe at Graeme Souness as the former Liverpool player and manager has been extremely critical of Rice as a midfielder this season.

“He’s not a midfield player then is he? I think he may be a centre-half. The ball travels faster than you do. I see him run with the ball 30 yards and pass it square," Souness told Piers Morgan on Football Uncensored.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Andoni Iraola would not be drawn on Jamie Carragher’s claim that his Liverpool side should be considered Arsenal’s nearest challengers in this season’s Premier League.

Liverpool have bounced back impressively from their 3-0 defeat to Manchester City earlier this month, winning five straight games in all competitions.

But Iraola suggested it was too early to engage with that kind of title talk and said his team still needed to ‘improve’.

‘I think it is too early to start looking at the standings,’ Iraola said in his pre-match press conference. ‘It is about preparing ourselves for a very difficult game.

‘We know Arsenal and how good they are. They have very good players, working a lot in synchronicity and we have to be ready for that challenge.

‘It’s going to be a demanding game but we also trust our players, trust ourselves and in the good atmosphere we will for sure have on Sunday, I hope we will be at level to win this game.

‘It is still October,’ he continued. ‘We have to take one game at a time and I always say the reference is more or less when we’ve play against each other once so halfway through the season. That’s when you can start to look at the standings.

‘Right now, we are in a position where wneed to improve and keep getting better.

‘For fans, it is good if they have expectations or they think we can win. Normally that’s a good thing but if you ask me if I think it is still very early in the season.’

Liverpool will hope to be boosted by the return of Dominik Szoboszlai and Víctor Munoz for Sunday’s game as they continue their recoveries from hamstring and knee injuries, respectively.

‘I think they have a chance,’ Iraola added. ‘But I don’t know for sure if they will be involved or not. We still have two days, so I think they have a chance, yes.’

#1853. How Arsenal lured Liverpool into perfect trap as Anfield curse broken

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

A familiar feeling and yet at the same time a very new one for almost everyone in the Arsenal camp.

Of those in the travelling party making their way up to Liverpool from north London, only Mikel Arteta had previously tasted an Arsenal win in the Premier League at Anfield.

He was booked that day, not for leaving his technical area but for a foul in midfield, where he started alongside Abou Diaby and Santi Cazorla.

There have been some miserable treks to this part of the world since then for Arsenal. Two 5-1 hammerings and as many 4-0 defeats.

Even in recent seasons, when it has been far more competitive and Arsenal far more comfortable in this environment, still the hoodoo was not broken.

Until now. There was no great surprise about the manner in which this 1-0 Arsenal victory came. These were three points earned off the back of the defenders, steering the ship to safety in the choppiest of waters.

This was not a dominant display or even a convincing one on the whole. Far from it. For large periods, there were passages of play that would have slotted in fairly well to those heavy defeats in previous years.

After falling behind to a lovely Arsenal move finished by Kai Havertz, Liverpool put the Gunners in a blender up until half-time. They played at 100 miles per hour and sent Arsenal for a spin.

Ezri Konsa twice stumbled on the ball. Aimless hacks were launched up the pitch. Bruno Guimaraes flew into one desperate challenge on the byline, cleaning out not only Bradley Barcola but Declan Rice as well in the process.

Arteta first appealed for calm and then screamed furiously at his players as the pressure continued. Arsenal lost duels and conceded ground. Alexis Mac Allister somehow headed over and Alexander Isak sliced wide.

And yet still Arsenal held firm. For no other side would this have felt sustainable and yet for Arsenal it strangely did. This is what they do. The occasion, the atmosphere, would have swallowed up many a team but not this one.

A victory at Anfield is a landmark for this Arsenal side, delivering in one of the few stadiums that had been left to conquer.

Arsenal player ratings vs Liverpool: 9/10 rock steps up in masterclass

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

It is another key indicator of progress. As was the case at Villa Park, the City Ground and the Stadium of Light earlier this season, Arsenal picked up three points at a ground where they failed to do so last season.

Victory at Anfield is a landmark for this Arsenal side and an ominous sign for their rivals

Arteta's side are now seven points up on the equivalent fixtures. That is an ominous sign for those hoping to close the gap.

Of the 17 shots the Gunners faced, not a single one forced David Raya into action. Arsenal never had real control of the match and their decision-making on the ball was too often too frantic and rushed.

None of that was costly, though, because they are a remarkable defensive unit. In the second half, with Liverpool attacking The Kop, Arsenal gave up very little.

Konsa was shaky early on but ended up producing an exceptional defensive display. He threw himself in front of shots, as did Jurrien Timber and Gabriel.

It did not need to be a thing of beauty. Arsenal won 18 fouls in the match and plenty of them were soft. They were streetwise in using every bit of contact to draw free-kicks and ease the pressure.

As has often been the case at Anfield, Arsenal had to suffer. This time it was all worth it.

#1849. Jamie Carragher calls out Liverpool star for 'ridiculous' Arsenal incident: 'It's got to stop'

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Alexis Mac Allister has been strongly criticised for his “embarrassing” actions during Liverpool’s Premier League defeat by Arsenal.

The Argentine midfielder was a central figure during Sunday’s high-profile showdown between potential title rivals at Anfield, where the defending champions won for the first time since September 2012 thanks to Kai Havertz’s first-half goal.

Mac Allister spurned arguably dominant Liverpool’s best chance to equalise before the interval, heading over the crossbar from close range after being picked out by a pinpoint left-wing cross from Milos Kerkez.

He was later at the centre of the game’s biggest flashpoint as tempers flared in the closing stages, falling to the ground theatrically while clutching his face following an altercation with Noni Madueke.

Mac Allister had initially sparked the incident by slapping Martin Odegaard on the back of the head and barking something at the Arsenal captain while he was down on the ground following a foul, behaviour which Jurrien Timber also took exception to.

Madueke was already on a yellow card for earlier sweeping the legs of Bradley Barcola, but avoided any further punishment from referee Andy Madley following a review by VAR Stuart Attwell, who deemed that it was not a headbutt as Timber and Mac Allister were both booked instead.

Mac Allister’s behaviour was branded as “embarrassing” by Gary Neville on commentary, while he was also criticised heavily by Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher after the match.

“I wanted Liverpool to win the game, but I’m delighted he [Madueke] never got sent off there,” Carragher said on Sky Sports. “We have really got to be strong calling people out and just saying, ‘this is embarrassing’.

“It’s got to stop. It’s ridiculous. I said it a couple of weeks ago with a similar sort of thing, I can’t stand it. I think everybody in the country watching football, this head-to-head stuff... if someone puts their head back and butts, of course, red card.

“But this stuff about head to head and if someone touches the other one goes down and the player gets sent off, as a game, as football, people in the Premier League, supporters, call your own people out for it.

#1848. Kaka discusses Hall of Fame induction, tonight’s derby and the Milan project

AC Milan legend Ricky Kaka will be inducted into the Rossoneri’s Hall of Fame ahead of tonight’s derby, which he believes is anyone’s game.

As confirmed in the last few days, after inducting the likes of Marco van Basten, Filippo Inzaghi, Andriy Shevchenko and more, it’s now time for Kaka. The Brazilian is one of the greatest players to have even worn the red and black shirt, scoring 104 goals and assisting another 81 in  307 games.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The ceremony will take place before tonight’s derby clash between AC Milan and Inter, which is a very important game for the Rossoneri. A loss would leave them 10 points behind the top, so hopefully Kaka’s presence and celebration can act as fuel for the team.

Speaking to Gazzetta dello Sport, Kaka shared his thoughts on the Hall of Fame, his memories of the derby and what will be needed from Milan tonight. He also commented on the Rossoneri’s project as a whole, stating that time is needed.

“I’m getting ready. My family will be there. My wife, daughters, my brother, and many friends. I also wanted to thank the fans who voted. I can imagine the atmosphere. It’ll be exciting.”

What do you remember about your first derby?

“A header from a cross by Rino Gattuso. It was also my first goal for AC Milan. Fantastic. The city experiences this match in a special way; among my memories, I’d logically put the Champions League derby in the quarterfinals. The comeback from 3-2 was also fantastic.”

You mentioned Gattuso, who as a coach, after changing many clubs, is doing well with Lazio…

“Being a coach is a tough job. Rino is doing really well now. He has a very special character, he’s someone who always wants to win, and I’m happy he’s able to express himself to the fullest. He’s a great friend, I always cheer for my friends and I’m very happy.”

“Let’s say no, for now. The pressure of the coaching job isn’t for me. But we can talk about it again in a couple of years.”

Speaking of friends, what do you think of the Paolo Maldini and Leonardo affair with the national team?

“I’m amazed at how little time passed before their resignations. It’s difficult to judge from afar, but I think it would have been a good thing for Italian football to have such competent people at the helm. I hope Italy regains its place soon.

“There are so many things to manage, from youth development onwards. I often meet with former players who live in Italy and ask questions. Italy at the World Cup is a good thing for football as a whole.

“Plus, my connection to Italy is incredibly strong; I try to return at least once a year, and more if I can. In recent years, we’ve visited the art cities, Florence, Venice, but also the lakes, Capri, and the sea. And Sardinia is wonderful.”

Let’s get back to football. Were you surprised by Milan’s collapse last season?

“I think all the fans expected us to qualify for the Champions League. Was it a physical or mental decline? Maybe a bit of everything. When confidence starts to wane, everything changes. Now, however, we must aim to return to the best of Europe. The Champions League is special.”

“It’s under construction. For seven years, it was Leao’s Milan, a great player on whom a lot of trust was placed. Now it’s different. The team is a collective with new faces and two masters: Modric remains the brains, then there’s Rabiot. And Ramos is a goalscorer.

“It will take some time to put it together. The important thing is to always aim high, even in the Europa League.”

What kind of relationship did you have with the Inter fans?

“A relationship of great respect. Inter helped me grow a lot because I’ve always looked at competition as something that helps me grow, so I saw the matches against Inter or Juventus as important matches, and I had to prepare well because the team was very strong, the opponents were very strong.

“But with the Brazilians of my time, Maicon, Julio, and the others, there was friendship. And also with the Argentines: many others were and remain friends, like Materazzi.”

How do you see Inter on this evening, which will be special for you?

“They are still doing well after last season. They’re a team to beat, but we Milan fans can do it already in this derby. Chivu as a coach was a nice surprise; Inter didn’t play well at the start, but then they corrected their position. But I wouldn’t say the Scudetto is a one-man showdown like you might think in Italy.

“I see the game as open and the road to the title even more so. The season is long, but Milan must aim to be consistent. So far they’ve done better in the league than in Europe, there will be moments of decline in the other teams and we’ll have to take advantage of them.”

“Not great at the World Cup, but it takes a bit of time. The national team is different from a club where you’re there every day evaluating players. Carlo was only able to work with the group for a year.

“For the next World Cup, it will be five years of preparation, five years with these guys, learning the culture of the country, knowing a little about what it’s like to play in the World Cup with Brazil. So I have a lot of confidence.”

You won the Ballon d’Or in 2007 and no one had any reason to argue. This time they gave it to Harry Kane, and Lamine Yamal doesn’t seem to have taken it too well. Your opinion?

“The right choice. Harry Kane has done very well, he was a key player with Bayern Munich and won a lot. Mbappé didn’t win much with Real Madrid, Lamine had success with Barça but wasn’t as decisive as expected. Their time will come, but I think the choice based on their performance this season is acceptable.”

Let’s get back to the derby. Who are the key players?

“Modric and Rabiot are masters, they manage and set the pace. Pulisic enchants me with his intelligence in the game, Goncalo is a goalscorer. As for Inter, what can I say? They are a consistent, solid team and have many dangerous players.”

Do you have any favourite places in Milan?

“I like walking downtown, I like Brera, I love the hidden corners. Drinking coffee, talking to people.”

Paul Merson believes Arsenal can have the Premier League wrapped up by mid-December if they navigate a tricky run of fixtures that begins with a trip to Anfield on Sunday.

#1846. Mikel Arteta explains shock Arsenal decision against Liverpool as new injury scare revealed

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta hailed his “incredible” Arsenal medical team for getting Christos Tzolis ready to start against Liverpool.

The Gunners came away from Anfield with a 1-0 victory, the first time they have won at the ground in the Premier League since 2012.

Kai Havertz scored the only goal of the match early in the first half and that proved enough as Arsenal delivered another massive defensive effort.

Tzolis was a surprise inclusion in the starting lineup, having not played a minute since he suffered a hamstring injury while on international duty with Greece a month ago.

Eberechi Eze was only named on the bench, though Arteta revealed after the match that the Englishman had been dealing with an injury concern of his own.

Arteta threw Tzolis straight back into the side and he was impressive at Anfield, working tirelessly and producing moments of real quality in attack.

He forced Alisson into a superb low save and almost created a second Arsenal goal with a lovely cross to the back post.

Asked what convinced him Tzolis was ready to start, Arteta replied: “It’s the energy that he had in training.

“When I asked him the question, how convinced he was. We had an issue with Ebs [Eze] as well, it was incredible that he was in the squad today.

“I want to give credit to all the medical and performance team. What they are doing with those boys is incredible. Every three days, to keep everybody at this level.

“These are the margins sometimes when you win a football match, whether you have somebody available or not. They deserve that credit.

“With Christos, incredible. He didn’t want to come off, he wanted to complete the game. We took some risks, but at a point we decided enough was enough.”
