#1845. Peter Schmeichel blasts ‘disgraceful’ Manchester United star after Chelsea defeat: ‘He is not suitable for us’

Peter Schmeichel branded Lisandro Martinez as ‘disgraceful’ following Manchester United’s 2-0 defeat to Chelsea on Saturday.

After a goalless first half, Morgan Rogers capitalised on a woeful display of defending from Martinez to put Chelsea in front in the 50th minute.

Xabi Alonso’s side then doubled their lead in the 64th minute through Cole Palmer’s spot-kick after Martinez was sent off for hitting Wesley Fofana with his forearm in United’s penalty area.

The defeat piled more pressure on Michael Carrick, who are now without a win in nine games, but Schmeichel believes the defeat to Chelsea is solely down to Martinez’s performance in the second half.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

‘I put this solely on Lisandro Martinez’s shoulders,’ Schmeichel said after United’s defeat.

‘This is an absolute disgrace how he played this game. Two weeks ago he came out and made some very, very strong statements against his teammates, against the football club, and it felt like he was trying to orchestrate a move. He’s in the last year of his contract.

‘What he did today, honestly, I have no words. The first goal, he’s played a World Cup final, you can’t defend the way he defended for the first goal and the penalty, I literally have no words how crazy that was.

‘Then he walks off the pitch shaking his head as if he’s done nothing wrong. So bad.

‘It really is baffling how he can defend like this. Morgan Rogers just walks through. He just let him go, it’s just not good enough.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘If you play in the Premier League you’ve got to defend better than that, if you play for Manchester United you’ve got to defend even better than that.

‘I might be accused of being on his back but I can point to so many goals they conceded this season where he’s the main guy, where he is not doing the job he’s supposed to do.

‘I think his behaviour two weeks ago, and what he did today with the penalty, it just shows you he’s not a suitable player for Manchester United.’

When asked about the defending for Rogers’ goal, Carrick said after United’s defeat: ‘I think the manner of the goal we conceded, it’s never a good goal to concede.

‘Morgan [Rogers] went right through the middle of us and, at that point, the game is in the balance. It was a big moment, for sure.’

#1844. Cole Palmer names Chelsea’s ‘best player on the pitch’ in Man Utd win

Cole Palmer has named Romeo Lavia as ‘the best player on the pitch’ in Chelsea’s 2-0 win over Manchester United on Saturday.

After a goalless first half at Stamford Bridge, Morgan Rogers opened the scoring before Cole Palmer doubled Chelsea’s lead from the penalty spot.

United were also reduced to 10 men as VAR intervened to punish Lisandro Martinez for hitting Wesley Fofana with his forearm.

Lavia, meanwhile, delivered an impressive performance at the heart of Chelsea’s midfield alongside Moises Caicedo.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

The 22-year-old was signed in a £53 million deal from Southampton in 2023 but has made just 53 appearances in three years due to multiple injuries, but Palmer believes his Chelsea teammate is one of the Premier League’s most underrated players.

‘Today was one of the best games I’ve seen him [Lavia] play,’ Palmer told BBC Sport after Chelsea’s win over United.

‘I’ve said all along he’s one of my favourite midfielders, people still don’t realise how good he is.

‘Obviously, he’s had his injury problems but he’s trying to put that behind him now and put in performances like today.

‘Today I thought he was the best player on the pitch.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

When asked for his verdict on Lavia’s performance, Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso said: ‘From a midfielder point of view, for me it has been a top, top performance.

‘He’s done so many things right, he’s been always connecting the defence with the attacking players, he’s been able to switch the game, he’s taken many right decisions, he’s been very dynamic, competitive.

‘So I think that not just this game, for the last two, three weeks he’s been playing at a very good level and I’m very happy for him and today he deserves a huge recognition for his performance.’

Palmer, meanwhile, also praised Estevao for his performance on what was his first Premier League start for Chelsea this season.

‘Every time I got the ball I tried to give it to him to show what he can do because I know he’s been wanting to play, he’s been patient and he played well,’ Palmer said.

Alonso was also impressed with Estevao’s response after the 19-year-old was left on the bench for Chelsea’s penalty shootout defeat to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday night.

‘We spoke after Tottenham and he knew that he was going to be playing tonight, today,’ Alonso said.

‘He has had the best response to show that he deserves more, that he was prepared and that’s what you want from a football player, so I’m very happy for him.

‘He deserved to enjoy his game, he had a good connection with the crowd. He was really close to scoring that goal. At the end he fought really hard, he was tired and it has been a good day for him.’

#1843. Arsenal player ratings vs Liverpool: 9/10 rock steps up in Anfield masterclass

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal moved three points clear at the top of the Premier League table with a battling 1-0 win over Liverpool.

Kai Havertz’s finish at the back post after a sweeping Arsenal move in the 16th minute proved to be the winner, as Arsenal came away from Anfield with a win for the first time since September 2012.

There were some nervy moments, with Liverpool on top and piling on the pressure for large periods, but Arsenal just about held firm.

Standard Sport’s Matt Verri was at Anfield to rate the Arsenal players...

One sensational pass through to Martin Odegaard broke the Liverpool press. Did just about enough to put Alexander Isak off and stop him finishing from a corner. For all the pressure Liverpool put on Arsenal, he did not have a save to make.

Incredibly lucky to not concede a penalty for a very obvious tug of Isak’s shirt. So adventurous in attack, often the most advanced player. Tireless shift and rescued his side with a last-ditch block on Ronald Araujo from close range.

Looked rattled at times early on but he stepped up massively in an incredible second-half display. A pivotal block to deny Florian Wirtz but plenty in the highlights reel beyond that. Won all seven ground duels. Massive performance when Arsenal needed it most.

Angered Liverpool fans with how often he went down. Fairly quiet afternoon by his standards, with Konsa more in the thick of it, but more than played his part in dragging Arsenal to an ugly, hard-fought win.

Sometimes a bit too frantic on the ball when Arsenal needed calm but he showed he can be a complete left-back with this outstanding defensive display. Gave Cody Gakpo and then Rio Ngumoha nothing. Shifted to wing-back for closing minutes.

Yet another monster effort in midfield. Great overlapping run and perfect cross created Havertz’s goal. Intercepted brilliantly in his own box when Bradley Barcola looked to be in. Mopped up and shielded the defence. A machine.

His kind of occasion. Roared at the away fans after one huge challenge to halt Barcola. Snapped into the challenges and relished the red-hot atmosphere, but began to tire and looked vulnerable when Liverpool ran in midfield. Replaced after an hour.

Arteta explains shock Arsenal decision as new injury scare revealed

Carragher calls out Liverpool star for 'ridiculous' Arsenal incident

Involved in Arsenal’s opener and kept causing Milos Kerkez problems. Nearly produced a cut back to make it 2-0 as well. Struggled defensively, with Liverpool getting far too much space on their left, and booked for a trip, but he was an outlet.

Led the Arsenal press exceptionally in a really bright start and it created the opener as he won it back. But Arsenal needed more on the ball and there was not enough control to ease the pressure, with flicks not coming off.

Surprise inclusion in the starting lineup but delivered for Mikel Arteta. Impressive how sharp and bright he was, and clipped one superb cross to the back post that should have been converted. Too unselfish at points but also denied by a sensational Alisson save.

Perfect response to his wasteful run when he tapped in to open the scoring. So often shows on the biggest stage and did so again. Overall performance was not his best and he was far too keen to go to ground, but a winner at Anfield is a huge moment.

Slow to get up to the pace of the game and booked for hauling down Isak. Grew into it and had one lovely dart forward from midfield, but then played the wrong pass.

Aggressive as ever and did not have too much stress slotting in on the left in defence.

Did a decent job holding it up and trying to release come of the pressure. Added a bit more energy.

Not used: Kepa, Eze, Mosquera, White, Zubimendi.

#1842. Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

Sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

“He is a top player, no doubt about it,” said head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

“He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”

A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a big cheer from the home fans.

Tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

He lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

Richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

De Zerbi spent much of the first half telling his back four to get higher up the pitch and it was perhaps understandable that captain for the day Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson looked like a group of strangers.

This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

Bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

Once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Igor Thiago missed a penalty after substitute Rodrigo Bentancur fouled Kevin Schade, as Spurs threatened to completely collapse with the result already pretty much decided.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

De Zerbi can console himself with the fact his Spurs team will quickly look a lot different. There are more new faces to come in, with winger Savinho on the brink of joining and Tottenham hoping Omar Marmoush will follow him from Manchester City.

Mikey Moore, who forced Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher into two second-half saves, is expected to join Cologne on loan and Mohammed Kudus is close to returning from injury, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro will come back in.

But if ever there was proof that spending a fortune offers no guarantee of happiness, then this was it.

Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that big-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his new-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on new players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow new signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

His team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian said: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

“You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

“We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. But no excuses, it’s a normal situation when you are building a new project. I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems.

“I am surprised by the result and performance. They [Brentford] deserved to win and we played very bad. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can’t find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance.

“Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things, like organisation and pressing.

“We can improve quickly but first, we have to understand this game better. I know their physical condition and [they are] new players but we have to put something more.

“We had to fight more. Players know I have a lot of confidence in them and we hope to improve quickly. Until we reach these conditions we have to suffer and today is an important defeat. Maybe we can wake up stronger.”

We had some problems with the timing of the pressure, we arrived too often late. We lost too many duels to compete with Brentford. I am sorry for that and sorry for the defeat. We have to improve in the physical condition and the organisation.

It was the first game and part of our journey, we knew we had a lot of new players. To become a team I said before the game we need two things, soul and style of play. We didn’t fight in the right way. Brentford is maybe one of the most important teams in the Premier League in terms of duels.

It was a game, especially in the first half, in one direction. We were not in the right position to make the high pressure, with Mikey Moore on the left centre.

We didn’t play well, we didn’t play in the right way. I think not because we don’t remember last season, because these players are good people but we lost too many duels. One of the best qualities of Brentford is the one-to-one, the man-to-man and the set-pieces.

Really pleased. Felt like there was a performance coming, you never really know after pre-season. The reality is the first game of the season comes and it can quickly come unstuck. I felt good for a number of weeks about how we were coming together. I was pretty pleased.

Our fans were amazing today. There is a genuine connection here that helps. I thought we started the game brilliantly and they were fully engaged. We want to be relentless. We looked like a real team.

That’s what we wanted, we wanted to start sharp, we want to show people what we’re made of and we did that today. We know last season we were one point off, this year, we’ve added quality people to the squad.

He’s been unbelievable, I can’t praise him high enough. He’s one of them players that we might lose the ball you just know he is going to win it back and he gets us on the counter-attack so quickly.

Is that Pedro Porro, Micky Van de Ven and Mohammed Kudus could be back for the next game against Newcastle, and Savinho ought to be through the door.

According to Opta, Brentford won the xG battle 3.96 to 0.47, taking 26 shots to Spurs’s nine. De Zerbi’s team finished the game with 59 per cent possession, but that is inflated by Brentford sitting off when three up. It’s the most xG Spurs have conceded in a single game since a 6-3 defeat by Liverpool in December 2024.

Less Christ the Redeemer more Christ, that was terrible.

"I think that sums it up"Fair to say this Spurs fan wasn't pleased with their performance 😅 pic.twitter.com/ZAdVaVbjlS

Possibly Brentford’s best performance under Keith Andrews, though that may be overstating the strength of the opposition. This was a complete display: they pressed Spurs, they played through Spurs, they played over Spurs, they dominated Spurs from set-pieces and their defenders bullied Spurs’s forwards. It will be interesting to hear from De Zerbi and whether he is philosophical or irate. This is far from Spurs’s ideal projected team, but still unacceptable.

Kinsky palms away a Damsgaard corner, and Yarmoliuk slices his shot over the bar. We are deep into stoppage time, and Brentford’s players are still pressing Bentnacur and Senesi and making them play with their heads down.

Just four minutes of added time to play but Spurs have more defending to do in the shape over another Brentford corner. They survive, but Brentford quickly establish possession again.

It would appear Lord Sugar is still watching:

To all Spurs fans don't worry this is all tactical to lure other teams into believing we are a easy touch. #coys

Another Brentford debut: Callum Wilson replaces Igor Thiago. Destiny Udogie has replaced Archie Gray for Spurs. “You should have signed for a big club!” sing the Brentford fans, in reference to the club almost signing Gray two summers ago. Football fans never forget.

Another Brentford goal would put them top of the table, for what that is worth. Spurs enjoying some possession in the Brentford half now, but it is entirely sterile.

Igor Thiago’s shot is blocked, Brentford still look the more likely team to score the next goal. Jadon Anthony shows he has a long throw, which might be a small reason why Brentford decided to sign him. Janelt then drags back Maddison.

Jadon Anthony involved in some Brenford pressure that results in a long throw and a corner, but the new man then slices a volley over the bar. Standing ovation at the Gtech for Sangare as he makes way for Damsgaard, while Hickey replaces Kayode. Be tough to beat his performance as debut of the weekend.

Michael Oliver letting some meaty challenges go, the game is quite feisty despite the scoreline. Schade launched himself into a tackle on Solanke but he did not really catch him with his studs.

A few Spurs fans may have thought better of staying to watch the final 20 minutes. I wonder “if” this Spurs fan has switched the television off?

First match if season . Smiling before the game. Hope to be smiling after. pic.twitter.com/hsTc79PBti

Richarlison beats the turf and Ajer punches the air after the Brentford defender wins the foul. Andrews is making another couple of changes: Jensen and Ouattara off, Yarmoliuk and new signing Jadon Anthony on.

Two more Spurs changes too: Maddison and Solanke on, Moore and Richarlison off.

Really sharp save from Kelleher to keep out Moore’s powerful shot from close range. Moore has at least carried a threat for Spurs in the second half, but they are struggling to sustain much pressure.

Tonali with a hit from 25 yards but it deflects comfortably into the arms of Kelleher. Surely a (Kew?) bridge too far for Spurs to dig out any kind of result from here.

De Zerbi looks a little resigned on the touchline, he will know that this is far from his ideal Spurs team on the pitch but that cannot excuse such poor standards.

He fails to open his account for the season. Sent Kinsky the wrong way, but he dragged the penalty just a touch and it cannoned off the post. The lead remains three.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

Spurs are being overpowered here, they cannot cope whenever Brentford come forward. There were appeals for handball against Van Hecke after Janelt swivelled and shot, but the foul is given against Bentancur for bundling over Schade. A complete mess for Spurs.

Any hope that the half-time double change would bring a revival now appear forlorn.

But here is a chance for Mikey Moore! Robertson forward to good effect, and his low cross arrives to Moore at the back post but his shot was too close to Kelleher. Almost crept through his legs.

Well that is surely game over. Cracking strike from Sangare from the edge of the box after a Brentford corner is cleared, they have always been so good at winning those second balls. Driven strike, good save from Kinsky and Kayode is first to the rebound to score from a couple of yards.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Important defensive header from Van Hecke to repel Sangare’s dangerous cross, and we enjoy our first look at a Kayode long throw. Some Strictly Come Dancing moves from Senesi and Collins in the penalty area, and the referee has a word with them. It continues when the throw is taken, and Sensi has a chunk of his shirt, but VAR says the Spurs man was fouled beforehand.

Will we see a different Tottenham in the second half.

Gallagher and Bergvall hooked, replaced by Bentancur and Fernandes who makes his Spurs debut.

15 - There was 15 passes in the build-up to Keane Lewis-Potter's opening goal for Brentford, only Michael Kayode's goal v Wolves in March (19) and Rico Henry's goal v Bournemouth in December (18) have seen more in a Premier League goal for the Bees under Keith Andrews.Busy. pic.twitter.com/8j5RZWFxvH

This has been a dreadful start to the season by Tottenham. Sandro Tonali has barely looked like a £10m player, let alone a £100m midfielder and, maybe unsurprisingly, De Zerbi’s players look like strangers. He will demand a major improvement in the second half. Keith Andrews will be delighted - maybe other than the fact the game isn’t already dead. His team have been dominant.

Brentford utterly dominant, there has been an alarming gulf in industry, precision and class between the two teams. Spurs will surely improve, both in the second half and as the season goes on, but this has fallen well below the standards you expect of a team with European aspirations. If a few of these players never played for De Zerbi again they could have no complaints.

No sign of a Spurs revival at half time, Brentford playing through their press with ease and then have space to run into. Kayode wins his header at the back post but no player was there for the knockdown.

Important block from Ajer after Spurs’s best piece of combination play around the box, before Tonali slashes a volley well over the bar from distance. Cue “what a waste of money” from the home fans.

Richarlison has been non-existent up front for Spurs, bullied by Collins and Ajer.

Tonali with a stray midfield pass to Outtara which rather sums up the Spurs performance so far. Surely there will be sweeping changes from De Zerbi at half time. Solanke, Maddison and Fernandes are the three players you’d have in mind.

“You’re going down with the Fulham,” is the chant from the Brentford fans.

Lewis-Potter swings in a dangerous cross, headed down by Kayode, and Van Hecke stoops to block Outtara’s shot. The whistle goes for a high boot.

This is far from Spurs’s strongest hypothetical team but they are being taken to the cleaners here. Spurs caught in that Brentford man-to-man press again and the ball bounces off Richarlison. Jensen shoots with power from the edge of the box, and Kinsky bats the shot back into danger, and there was Janelt to poke the rebound home. Brentford in total control.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

Spurs’s defence breached again, and Outtara really should have made it two but his first touch was far too heavy and Kinsky was able to clear. Spurs will not be the only team to struggle against this Brentford front three. Schade won the flick on, Thiago swept the ball across the box, but the finish was lacking from Outtara.

Outtara fouls his former Bournemouth team-mate in the Spurs box. A lovely chipped pass forward from Schade releases Thiago in the left channel and another spell of home pressure begins. Lewis-Potter roaming everywhere. Then Brentford win a free-kick which will go in the mixer. Senesi fouled Outtara.

Bergvall floats in a decent cross from the left but it splits Richarlison and Moore. Sweden manager Graham Potter is in the stands watching Bergvall. Van Hecke is known for his progressive passes, but he overhits one through for a Brentford goal kick.

Spurs players not happy with Michael Oliver. Conor Gallagher feels he was pulled back in midfield, before Oliver blows for a 50:50 in Brentford’s favour.

All so simple for Brentford to get at Spurs again, and it takes some excellent defending on the cover from Robertson to deny Outarra who could have been through for a second goal.

Igor Thiago’s header hits the bar but the flag goes up for offside. Brentford’s man-to-man press is smothering Spurs at the moment, they cannot break through it to establish any territory higher up the pitch.

Igor Thiago makes enough of a nuisance of himself to force Senesi to put the ball out for a throw, Brazil vs Argentina in the match up. Brentford just look sharper and more match-ready all over the pitch.

Half a chance for Spurs to reply with a quickfire equaliser, but Tel’s free-kick was tame and deflected through to Kelleher. De Zerbi can have no complaints, it was one-way traffic before the goal.

Well that’s a good early impression from Sangare. He played a lovely one-two before picking out Lewis-Potter for Brentford’s goal.

To say this opening Brentford goal was on the cards would be a mammoth understatement. The home team are finding it so easy to progress the ball to dangerous positions around the Spurs box.

The new man Sangare is involved, playing a one-two at the edge of the area, before picking out Lewis-Potter who was unmarked on the penalty spot. Brentford’s left back popping up in the box, and it is a simple finish.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Pretty much Spurs’s first meaningful foray over the halfway line, but Gallagher’s shot from distance is wild. In other news, Jon Bon Jovi is in the stands. He popped up at a few games at the World Cup.

Brentford continue to make inroads down their left, Lewis-Potter driving at Gray and whipping in a dangerous cross that glanced off Van Hecke at the near post and only just wide of the far post. The corner is swung to the unmarked Sangare at the back post, and his header loops well over.

Brentford continue to look the better team, moving the ball at pace in the final third, but Schade stumbles up against Bergvall in the box. Spurs yet to settle of establish any possession in the game so far.

Collins then catches Gallagher on the foot, as the Spurs man rushed into a challenge to close the defender down. Not much in it.

From that free-kick, Jenson’s delivery was a wicked one: inswinging and flat to the near post, and the ball glanced off Robertson’s head and behind for a corner.

Jensen then tees up Lewis-Potter for an ambitious volley from the edge of the box, and there are hopeful appeals for a handball penalty against Gallagher, and then Collins fails to divert to follow up cross on target.

Not the most distinctive contrast between the two kits, but not as bad as Newcastle vs Bayer Leverkusen in pre-season.

Brentford on the front foot in the early exchanges, Sangare involve in their first attack, but Tel runs back to defend well against Kayode.

Schade then wins a free-kick from Van Hecke in a crossing position wide left, the forward’s feet were too quick for the Dutch defender.

The usual rendition of Hey Jude before the game in south west London.

[On three of the back four being new signings] I have a big confidence because all three are very important players with experience and qualities. They have been working for one month and we have no problem with them.

[On Gray wearing the armband] He’s very young but he is a big personality. great behaviour and he deserves to be a captain today. He cannot suffer too much pressure because he is an important player for us for a long time.

[On if there is more business to be done] We have not the right or complete squad today but no excuse we have the qualities to compete against an important team with a clear style, they are very strong in set-pieces and long balls especially.

This will be a first look at new signing Mamadou Sangare for Brentford fans. Lots of people have tipped him to be one of the signings of the summer. I haven’t seen enough of him to give an opinion but it will be interesting to see how he gets on against Tottenham’s first-ever £100m man Sandro Tonali.

There’s a decent chance this Tottenham starting line-up will not play again together for the rest of this season. Mikey Moore is expected to move to Cologne on loan, while Savinho’s arrival will relegate Mathys Tel to the bench. Spurs also have Mohamed Kudus and Xavi Simons to return from injury. De Zerbi will want a good start to the season, but this is not the Tottenham side he will be relying upon moving forwards.

There will be no easing into life at Spurs for Robertson, who faces Dango Outtara in one of the game’s key duels. The Scot has plenty of experience of course, but there were signs towards the end of time at Liverpool that he had started to struggle in one-on-ones against wingers.

Archie Gray will become Tottenham’s youngest-ever captain tonight. Aged 20 years and 163 days, he will beat Steve Perryman’s record of 20 years and 260 days. On Friday, De Zerbi listed all of his captains with Gray down in fifth place. New permanent captain Micky van de Ven misses the trip to Brentford through injury.

If we include the league goals Mikey Moore scored while on loan at Rangers last season, Spurs’s front three scored 22 league goals combined last season. By contrast, Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Dango Outtara scored 37 between them in the Premier League. Brentford are firm favourites with the bookies for this one, and that difference in firepower is probably why. Omar Marmoush could help matters.

Seventeen-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett is one of the outstanding players in the country at his age group, and there is a lot of excitement about him at Spurs. Post-Kane, the club’s academy has not delivered much bona fide first-team quality, but Williams-Barnett appears on that trajectory.

Brentford XI: Kelleher, Schade, Jensen, Thiago, Ouattara, Sangare, Ajer, Collins, Lewis-Potter, Janelt, Kayode

Subs: Valdimarsson, Hickey, Henry, Pinnock, Yarmoliuk, Wilson, Anthony, Damsgaard, Schuster

Your Bees to kick-off the 26/27 season 🐝 pic.twitter.com/nJO5emjgQM

Spurs XI: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Senesi, Robertson; Gallagher, Tonali, Bergvall; Moore, Richarlison, Tel

Subs: Dubravka, Danso, Maddison, Udogie, Fernandes, Solanke, Bentancur, Davies, Williams-Barnett

Our Spurs side on the opening day 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/Uh5z221aTc

Starting the season in west London 📌 pic.twitter.com/uglTu9zDvA

Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the big spenders.

That is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s new leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

De Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

Spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

Brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the big boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

Asked about the Mali international, Andrews said: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

“He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”

Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

#1841. Danny Murphy says Man Utd star is ‘unlikely’ to play for Michael Carrick again

Danny Murphy believes Lisandro Martinez is fast becoming a ‘liability’ and is ‘unlikely’ to play under Michael Carrick again following his red card in Manchester United’s 2-0 defeat to Chelsea.

Morgan Rogers fired Chelsea in front shortly after the restart at Stamford Bridge and United’s woes were compounded as Martinez was sent off for a second bookable offence in the 63rd minute.

The hosts made no mistake with the resulting penalty as Cole Palmer squeezed the ball past Senne Lammens from 12 yards and Xabi Alonso’s men held firm with their man advantage to emerge with maximum points.

The result propelled the Blues up into fourth place in the table, with the west London giants winning at home without conceding for the first time in their last 13 matches.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Meanwhile, United’s miserable winless run extended to nine games in all competitions, heaping yet more pressure on a dejected-looking Carrick amid widespread speculation over his future at Old Trafford.

Martinez’s sending off was just the latest chapter in what is becoming a nightmare season for the World Cup-winning Argentina defender, who went public with his criticism of the Red Devils’ hierarchy last month.

Asked if the term ‘liability’ was perhaps too strong a word to describe Martinez on Saturday night’s Match of the Day programme, ex-Liverpool and Tottenham midfielder Murphy replied: ‘It’s getting that way. A player of that experience and quality, he knows better.

‘There’s something obviously not right at the moment in his head, he’s in a different space, because you don’t see the poor performances for a player of that quality.

‘There was the Dominic Solanke issue last week [against Tottenham] and then there was the interview, rant, whatever you want to call it and then today, his performance in the second half was just nowhere near it.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘To go and do that after you’ve just had a yellow… I don’t know whether he’s thinking of getting away, whether he’s disgruntled at everything going on around the club, but he’s given Carrick a really big dilemma now.

‘When he’s served the suspension, I think it’s unlikely that Michael, if he’s still the manager, is going to put him back in.’

According to Murphy, Carrick will have to accept some ‘responsibility’ for the club’s wretched start to the new season.

However, the former England international feels a combination of ‘physical’ and ‘mental’ issues within the squad is United’s ‘biggest problem’ this term.

‘I’m not sure they care too much about the fans, the way they’ve dealt with things,’ Murphy explained.

‘Look, it’s not all Michael Carrick’s fault. He’ll have to take some responsibility.

‘The biggest problem I see at Manchester United at the moment, it’s not even a lack of quality. Yes, there’s a few spaces in the squad, but physically, over the last couple of months, they’ve looked well off it compared to the team we saw at the end of last season.

‘That’s for one of two reasons. One is they physically aren’t good enough and they didn’t have a good enough pre-season or they’re switched off mentally from the manager’s messaging.

‘I think it’s a mixture of the two depending on which player we’re talking about.

‘To get that cohesion back, that tenacity and that athleticism and that togetherness, I’m not sure whether he’s going to be able to do it with the squad he’s got.’

Estevao made his first start of the Premier League season for Chelsea and impressed in a new-look attack alongside Palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto.

Prior to Saturday’s contest, there had been rumours that the young Brazilian had grown frustrated with his peripheral role at Stamford Bridge and could push to leave the club next summer.

But Murphy is confident Chelsea fans will see a lot more of Estevao if Alonso decided to stick with his 4-2-3-1 formation which worked so well against the Red Devils.

‘He’s a phenomenal talent and the fans have been a little bit bemused that he’s not been used, especially in that last couple of games because he’s gone back to a 4-2-3-1,’ Murphy said of Estevao.

‘In the early part of the season he was playing the three lads up top in a different system so there was no wingers but today, if you wanted a sample of what they’ve been missing… the bravery, the speed, the skill, the threat to the goal.

‘He started on the right, he drifted across sometimes and ended up as a No.10 and on the left, they have that flexibility.

‘The dilemma moving forward is whether he plays this system or the other because where does he play him? He’s got Joao Pedro to come back, he’s got Cole Palmer and he’s got Morgan Rogers.

‘Ultimately, he’s got to be used more. At the moment, Xabi Alonso seems stuck on 4-2-3-1 and if that’s the case then we’re going to see a lot more of Estevao.’

Chelsea will hope to pick up where they left off when they return to Premier League action away to Sunderland in a week’s time.

United, meanwhile, will look to stop the rot in the Champions League at home to Roma on Tuesday night, before they play host to Aston Villa next Sunday afternoon.

#1840. Cardinale reiterates Amorim backing before derby but warns: “I will be crushed if we don’t win”

Gerry Cardinale has reiterated his complete backing for Ruben Amorim ahead of AC Milan’s derby against Inter, but also made it clear that he will be very disappointed if they don’t win.

An important game is on the cards for Milan this evening, hoping to bounce back from their Bologna defeat with what would be a massive derby win. Success would bring them within four points of Inter, while a defeat would increase the gap to ten points.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Cardinale, the Milan owner, will be present at the stands in San Siro after also attending the games against Udinese and Bologna. Last night, he hosted a dinner for many Milan legends and explained his project for the club to them.

After the dinner, Cardinale stopped to talk to the journalist Carlo Pellegatti outside the restaurant (see the video at the bottom). Among other things, he reiterated his backing for Amorim and also made it clear that he really wants to win.

“Look, it was a fantastic night. We had people from Milan getting together in support of AC Milan. And that’s all I could have hoped for. It’s a big day tomorrow, a big game, as you know…”

Are emotions ramping up ahead of the game?

“My job is not to increase the emotion. My job is to keep everything steady and focused, providing the leadership so that we know what we need to do. We need to win tomorrow [today, editor’s note], not just for the first 45 minutes but also the next 45 minutes.

“It’s football, it’s sport, and the great thing about sport is that you never know. But my job is to make sure that we have a steady hand to do the best that we can do and maximise our chance of winning.

“Tonight was a really amazing event. We had legends of AC Milan who know how to win, and that means so much to me, that they came back and bought into what we do. We are bringing this passion and love of winning back.

“Let’s see how we do tomorrow. It’s a long season, but it’s the derby and it’s our home derby, so I want the win more than anything. I will be crushed if we don’t win tomorrow.”

“Listen, we have to come together. If we want to win, it has to be everybody. The fans, us, the press, anybody who supports AC Milan. Let’s come together and all make this possible. Ruben is doing a great job, I made the right decision on Ruben.

“I watched him today at Milanello and he really cares about his training, his managing, his coaching, and his mentoring. I met with every single one of our players and they want to win. It’s only a matter of time.

“You either want to win or you don’t want to win. You can’t fake that. I want to win, the players want to win and Amorim wants to win. I’m telling you, that I got right. Now, football is up and down, but I promise you that they want to win.”

#1839. Jamie Redknapp claims there are only two suitable candidates for Man Utd job

Jamie Redknapp believes Unai Emery and Eddie Howe are the only managers that Manchester United should consider if Michael Carrick is relieved of his duties.

Carrick’s future was plunged into further doubt on Saturday afternoon as his United side were beaten 2-0 away to Chelsea to extend the club’s miserable winless streak to nine matches in all competitions.

Morgan Rogers scythed through United’s defence to open the scoring shortly after half-time and the visitors’ woes were compounded as Lisandro Martinez was sent off for a second bookable offence just past the hour-mark.

Cole Palmer scored with the resulting penalty to double Chelsea’s lead and Xabi Alonso’s men held firm with their man advantage to emerge victorious and move up to fourth in the Premier League table.

The result ensured United remain stranded down in 17th place, meanwhile, with Carrick’s side hovering above the relegation zone only on goal difference after nine matches.

Ahead of United’s latest setback, it was widely reported that Carrick would be given the opportunity to fight for his future and ‘turn things around’ at Old Trafford.

However, with performances failing to improve, speculation over potential replacements continues to intensify, with Antonio Conte, Fabian Hurzeler, Julian Nagelsmann, Howe and Emery among the high-profile names linked.

‘There are only, I think, two runners,’ former Liverpool and Tottenham midfielder Redknapp said on Sky Sports when addressing possible candidates for the hot seat at the Theatre of Dreams.

‘Listen, Michael Carrick is still in the job so it’s unfair to be saying it.

‘But if that’s the case, if this doesn’t improve, it’s inevitable that he’s going to lose his job.

According to Redknapp, Aston Villa head coach Emery is the outstanding candidate to take over the reins from Carrick.

However, the ex-England international is unsure if the Spaniard would want to move considering he is currently able to ‘do what he likes’ at Villa Park.

‘Julian Nagelsmann has done pretty well in Germany. I think he started off his career so good… last few years, not quite so good, obviously with Germany at the World Cup,’ Redknapp continued.

‘I can only really see him [Emery]. It depends, does he want to leave Aston Villa? He’s got a project, he can do what he likes there, he’s running the club, whatever he says goes.

‘I don’t believe anyone else is just going to go in there with a manager and an assistant and change it. There are so many things behind the scenes that need to change.’

The Red Devils will look to stop the rot when they return to action at home to Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

#1838. Declan Rice offers Liverpool hope after Arsenal loss and Premier League title prediction

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Declan Rice has offered Liverpool some hope in the Premier League title race, in contrast to Jamie Carragher’s prediction following their defeat to Arsenal.

In Sunday’s big game from the Premier League, Arsenal came out on top by a goal-to-nil as Kai Havertz’s first half goal was the difference between the two sides.

The German, in the 16th minute, got on the end of Rice’s cross to the back post for a simple tap-in and from there, the Gunners - at times - rode their luck en route to sealing a first league win at Anfield for 14 years.

The result not only means Arsenal are now three points clear of Manchester City at the Premier League summit, the gap between them and Liverpool now stands at nine points with one match to play before the international break.

Such is the distance that Carragher has conceded that this season will not be the year for his former club.

"It means Liverpool aren't going to win the league!” Carragher said while analysing the game for Sky Sports on Super Sunday.

However, Rice - who hailed Arsenal’s team spirit - insisted it is too early to be making definitive statements about the title race.

He said: “Like you said, we’ve not won here in 14 years, so we got off to a very good start.

“We could have probably done a little bit more as well in front of goal but in the end, that defensive line, the way we stick together, that togetherness we have, it’s like nothing I’ve ever seen before.

“I’ve learned that the table, you can only take it seriously in February, March. If you’re there or thereabouts, then you know you’re in with a shout.

“Anything now between now and then, you’ve got to win as many as you can.”

I’ve learned that the table, you can only take it seriously in February or March

Both Arsenal and Liverpool are in Champions League action on Wednesday, facing Slavia Prague and Fenerbahce respectively as this season’s league phase reaches the halfway stage.

The Gunners then sign off for the international break with a home game against Hull, while Liverpool travel to the capital to face a struggling Crystal Palace side at Selhurst Park.

#1837. Villarreal vs Paris Saint-Germain - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 01 Nov 2026 17:24, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 20:47

Hoping to maintain their 100% record in this Champions League campaign, Paris Saint-Germain will face Villarreal for the first time in their history on Tuesday at Estadio de la Ceramica in eastern Spain.

The reigning two-time champions are one of five teams with a perfect record in the competition so far, beating Barcelona 4-2 on matchday three, while Villarreal sit 19th on three points, losing 4-3 to Liverpool in their last Champions League outing.

Competing in their sixth Champions League this season, Villarreal have had some exciting finishes this time around, though not always to their benefit.

Four or more goals have been scored in each of their first three League Phase affairs, with their lone triumph coming at home when they came back to defeat Napoli 3-1.

The two-time Champions League semi-finalists have been anything but stellar defensively in this competition, conceding in 14 straight Champions League encounters, while allowing an average of 3.8 goals per match in those last 10 games.

Inigo Perez has seen his side drop points in two consecutive competitive home matches, but on Tuesday they can win successive Champions League group games at El Madrigal for the first time since 2008.

Villarreal have failed to win their last two League Phase encounters in this competition when leading in the second half, while losing their only match in Europe this season in that scenario at Anfield on matchday three.

El Submarino Amarillo are unbeaten in their two previous Champions League meetings versus French opposition, beating Lille at home in 2005-06 (1-0) and drawing them 0-0 in France that same season.

Three matches into the League Phase, Paris Saint-Germain look intent on becoming just the second team this century to capture three successive Champions League titles, after Real Madrid.

Luis Enrique’s men, who began Ligue 1 without a win in their first three matches, have been dominant in the opening stages of this tournament, following up an impressive 6-1 win over Slovan Bratislava with consecutive 4-2 triumphs over title contenders Manchester City and Barcelona.

Their 14 goals so far match Arsenal’s total from 2010-11 for the joint-most-scored in this competition after three matchdays, and this week they can win their first four Champions League group outings for the first time since 2019.

On Monday, Enrique won his 127th competitive match in charge, the most all-time among managers for Les Parisiens, and this week he can help them set a club record for their longest Champions League unbeaten run, a streak which currently sits at 13 games.

They have won just one of their last three League Phase outings away from home, though they have not lost a Champions League group match on Spanish soil since November 2015 (1-0 at Real Madrid).

Les Parisiens can claim a 10th consecutive triumph across all competitions on Tuesday, conceding a goal or fewer in four of their last five competitive games as the visitors.

Paris Saint-Germain Champions League form:

Paris Saint-Germain form (all competitions):

Several Villarreal players are questionable due to muscular problems, including Nathan Saliba, Alassane Diatta, Juan Foyth and Ilias Akhomach.

Santiago Mourino and Tani Oluwaseyi lead them with two goals each in this phase of the competition, as the latter scored late against the Reds on matchday three.

Their other strikes on that occasion came courtesy of Sergi Cardona and French-born striker Georges Mikautadze, who plays his international football for Georgia.

At PSG, Marquinhos and Ousmane Dembele are dealing with hamstring strains, Nuno Mendes and Alessandro Longoni have leg injuries and Georgian international Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is out because of a cruciate ligament tear.

Ferran Torres, who previous played for one of Villarreal’s main regional rivals Valencia, is tied for the team lead with Dembele on three goals in the League Phase.

Meanwhile, Desire Doue has scored in back-to-back Champions League games, as he, Spaniard Fabian Ruiz, plus Lucas Hernandez and Vitinha netted versus Barca.

Gulacsi; Mourino, Navarro, Veiga, Cardona; Comesana, Gueye; Oluwaseyi; Buchanan, Mikautadze, Moleiro

Villarreal have been consistently poor defensively in this competition, and although PSG do not have their most potent attacking players available, they should have more than enough to punish a side as vulnerable at the back as the Spaniards have been all season.

#1836. Bradley Lowery’s mother issues heartbreaking statement over Coventry fan’s ‘cruel’ act

Gemma Lowery has demanded her late son Bradley is ‘remembered with love, not hate’ after a video emerged allegedly showing a Coventry fan using a picture of her ‘beautiful boy’ to taunt Sunderland supporters.

The incident occurred during Coventry’s Premier League clash with the Black Cats on Saturday, in which goals from Tatsuhiro Sakamoto, Taiwo Awoniyi and Jack Rudoni steered Frank Lampard’s men to a 3-1 victory.

The five-second clip in question appears to show a young spectator in the home end at the Coventry Building Society Arena smirking while pointing to a photograph of Bradley on his mobile phone.

Bradley was a lifelong supporter of Sunderland and his battle with neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer, touched the hearts of supporters across the footballing world – and beyond – before his tragic death at the age of six in July 2017.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

His legacy lives on through the Bradley Lowery Foundation which was established in August later that year and has helped support countless families in raising funds for treatment and equipment which is not readily available through the NHS.

Shockingly, it is not the first time that Bradley’s death has been used in such a sickening way, with Sheffield Wednesday fan Dale Houghton sacked from his job and handed a 12-month suspended prison sentence following a similar incident back in 2023.

In response to the footage, an official statement from Coventry read: ‘Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland.

‘The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action.’

According to The Guardian, a 14-year-old boy has since handed himself into West Midlands police and a thorough investigation will be carried out in due course.

Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland.The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course… pic.twitter.com/RxXnhtW3DF

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

In the wake of Saturday’s match, Bradley’s mother Gemma took to Instagram to plead with supporters to stop the ‘cruelty’ while calling on Coventry to ‘take appropriate action’.

‘My beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate. Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters,’ she wrote.

‘As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile.

‘I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between. So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face.

‘To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt.

‘We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter?

‘I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were. I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don’t. I just for him to learn from this.

‘Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day.’

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Gemma took the opportunity to thank those who had stepped up to defend Bradley since the video first began to circulate on social media.

‘Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know,’ she added.

‘What some people don’t realise is that Bradley’s story didn’t end when his life did.

‘Because of Bradley, children’s lives are being saved, hundreds of families have received vital support, and children facing unimaginable battles are being given hope.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘Through Super Brad’s Pad, families can escape hospital life, spend precious time together and make memories that last forever.

‘That is Bradley’s legacy. The difference my little boy continues to make in this world. No amount of cruelty will ever take that away.

‘So rather than let this photograph be remembered for hatred, I want it remembered for what it truly represents.

‘My beautiful little boy, enjoying one of the happiest days of his life, with the biggest smile on his face. That is how I want the world to remember him. #CancerHasNoColours Forever 6. Forever loved.’

Gemma finished by sharing a link to the Bradley Lowery Foundation’s website: www.bradleyloweryfoundation.com

#1835. Jamie Carragher issues Arsenal verdict after 'absolutely outstanding' Liverpool win

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Jamie Carragher says Arsenal are arguably “the best team defensively” in Europe following their 1-0 win over Liverpool.

Kai Havertz’s first half goal was enough for the Gunners to win for the first time at Anfield in the Premier League in 14 years, with the result also moving the reigning champions three points clear of Manchester City at the summit.

Having taken the lead as early as the 16th minute, Arsenal had to survive some nervy moments to leave Merseyside with a statement victory.

Alexander Isak was unfortunate to not win Liverpool a penalty when his shirt was pulled by Jurrien Timber in the box, while Alexis Mac Allister spurned a glorious chance shortly before the break when he headed over from close range.

Although Liverpool were the side on top for large periods, they ultimately failed to seriously test Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya as they failed to register a single shot on target despite having 17 attempts.

Reflecting on the game, Carragher heaped praise on the Arsenal rearguard as he pointed out how impressed he has been with Mikel Arteta’s side defensively this season even in the absence of William Saliba.

"No, it was a brilliant game and both teams can take a lot from it,” Carragher said on Sky Sports. “Liverpool played really well.

“They didn't do enough but you are playing against, defensively, the best team in this country, arguably in Europe and that is without the best centre-back in the world in Saliba.

"When you think about Arsenal winning titles, especially in '89 and '91 with Tony Adams and that famous back four, I think we're getting close to putting this back four up against that and in that conversation.

"To come to Anfield and be put under that much pressure and not have a shot on target from the opposition, or Liverpool not to have a big chance given the money they've spent on their attack is absolutely outstanding."

#1834. Why is there only one Premier League game on Sunday November 1?

It is a very quiet Sunday in terms of Premier League football, with just one match on the fixture list for November 1.

That game is a big one as Liverpool host Arsenal at 4.30pm, with the Gunners needing just a point to move to the top of the Premier League table.

The Reds can climb one place to fourth with a win at Anfield, but will remain in fifth with anything less.

It could be a cracker, but it is all we are getting as there were eight games on Saturday and there is one more on Monday night as Newcastle host Everton.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

It is very unusual for there to be such a paucity of Premier League action on a Sunday, with Sky Sports really struggling to claim this one as Super.

This is just the second time since May 2024 that a Sunday during the Premier League season has featured just one match.

So why are we restricted to a solo contest as November gets underway?

There were initially two games scheduled for Sunday November 1, with Aston Villa vs Fulham originally set for 2pm, ahead of Liverpool vs Arsenal.

However, the Champions League schedule came out after that decision was made by the Premier League in August.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

That European schedule set Barcelona vs Aston Villa for Tuesday November 3, which means the Villains could not play on Sunday as it would be too close to their glamorous trip to Spain. The general rule is that teams should not play two games in 60 hours.

If the Champions League game had been set for Wednesday then no change would have been needed, but Tuesday meant Villa’s clash with Fulham had to be switched to Saturday.

They played that game at 8pm on Saturday, with Nicolas Jackson opening the scoring for the home team at Villa Park, before Zion Suzuki let in a nightmare own goal.

Liverpool and Arsenal are both in Champions League action next week, but both their fixtures are played on Wednesday.

The Reds go to Turkey to play Fenerbahce in a 5.45pm kick-off, while Arsenal travel to face Sparta Prague.

Manchester United host Roma on Tuesday night, which is plenty of time after they were beaten at Chelsea on Saturday lunchtime.

#1833. 'Red card': Tottenham fans make the same Rodrigo Bentancur point after Noni Madueke 'headbutt'

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham supporters have called out refereeing inconsistencies following Arsenal’s win over Liverpool.

During the closing stages of Sunday’s Premier League showdown at Anfield, Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister and Arsenal winger Noni Madueke clashed after Martin Odegaard had won a free-kick on the edge of his own box.

As the pair went head-to-head, Mac Allister went to ground holding his face, alleging that he had been head-butted by Madueke.

While referee Andy Madley showed the Argentina international - and Jurrien Timber - a yellow card, he did not punish Madueke - who had been booked earlier on in the game - and the Premier League’s match centre issued a statement as to why.

“The referee’s call of no violent conduct by Madueke on Mac Allister was checked and confirmed by VAR," the statement read.

'VAR: “All of the situations have been checked and cleared. There is some contact as Madueke and Mac Allister square-up. In my opinion, it's not forceful, not violent, not brutal”.'

Despite the explanation, some Tottenham fans on social media have pointed out that Rodrigo Bentancur was sent-off in similar fashion during the 1-1 draw with Manchester United last month.

Jamie Carragher, meanwhile, did not share the same view as the Tottenham fans and slammed Mac Allister's actions.

"I want Liverpool to win the game, but I'm delighted he [Madueke] didn't get sent off," Carragher said on Sky Sports. "We have really got to be calling people out and saying 'this is embarrassing'.

"It's ridiculous and it's got to stop. I can't stand it. If someone puts their head back and butts, then red card. But if it's head-to-head and they touch, the other one goes down and the player gets sent off, as a game, call your own people out on it.

#1832. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer defends Michael Carrick and confirms Manchester United return ‘offer’

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer believes Michael Carrick is the ‘right man’ to ‘take Manchester United forward’ despite the growing pressure on his former teammate.

United’s dismal start to the season continued on Saturday as Carrick’s side lost 2-0 to Chelsea.

Manchester United were marginally on top in the first half but fell behind shortly after half-time, Chelsea summer signing Morgan Rogers sauntering through the visitors’ defence and dinking over Senne Lammens.

Carrick still has hopes of a comeback but that became unrealistic when Lisandro Martinez was sent off for two reckless fouls, the second resulting in a penalty which Cole Palmer converted.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

The defeat means Manchester United are without a win in nine games, their longest run of such since 1988, and leaves the club 17th in the Premier League.

There were fresh calls for Old Trafford bosses to sack Carrick after United left Stamford Bridge empty-handed but the ex-England midfielder is expected to take charge of Tuesday’s Champions League clash against Roma.

Reports suggest Carrick will also be in the dugout for next weekend’s Premier League game against Aston Villa before the United hierarchy take stock during the international break.

While Manchester United are sticking with Carrick for the time being, they have already made tentative approaches to three potential replacements – Eddie Howe, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann.

Solskjaer supported Carrick’s appointment back in January and still believes his ex-teammate can turn things around at Old Trafford.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Michael has what it takes to take that club forward,’ he told Norwegian outlet TV2. ‘I think he’s the right man.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘He understands the club, understands the fans, and knows what’s required. You don’t see that “devil” in him. But it’s there, and I have it too. We are so incredibly alike.

‘Perhaps not many people thought I would become a football coach, certainly not the manager of Manchester United. Many probably thought the same about Michael Carrick.

‘When I spoke with United, I also spoke highly of Michael. “If you choose him, you’re getting a good man,” I said. I believe he did the same for me.

‘Neither of us was desperate to get the job. But we’d likely step up if they asked.’

Solskjaer spoke to Manchester United chiefs Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada following Ruben Amorim’s sacking at the start of the year and confirmed he ‘offered’ to return to the club.

The offer came after club legend Solskjaer’s three-year spell in charge of the Red Devils which ended in 2021.

‘I had a good chat with Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada,’ Solskjaer said. ‘We didn’t discuss contract length or anything of the sort.

‘I offered to step in if needed, and I made no demands. I shared my thoughts on what is required for the club to move forward. We had one brief conversation. There were no negotiations.’

Reflecting on his time in charge of Manchester United, Solskjaer added: ‘There were some fantastic moments, but everything has its time.

‘I do miss it, yes. I could have imagined staying there forever, but life goes on. It was a very special period. Of course it was.

‘It was special in many ways. Going back to the past isn’t always a good idea. Yes, I would have stepped in [in January], but I didn’t intend for it to last beyond the summer.

‘It was probably time for someone else to have a go. I also feel like I have some unfinished business. Naturally, it would have been fun to have the opportunity again.’

Manchester United play host to Roma sitting 20th in the Champions League, while the Italians are 15th with one win, one draw and one defeat from their opening three games.

#1831. Guida will officiate Milan’s game against Inter – the record and controversy

Marco Guida has been assigned the Milan-Inter game this evening, set to officiate his 44th game involving the Rossoneri.

Emotions will undoubtedly be running high at San Siro this evening. Before the game, Milan will induct Ricky Kaka into the Hall of Fame, which will be a great moment for him and the fans present. Then, the Rossoneri will have to get a win to avoid dropping too far behind.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In short, it’s a game that means a lot in the red and black parts of the city. Gerry Cardinale stressed his desire to come out on top tonight and most likely, there will be some tough moments for the referee to handle. Let’s just hope there is no controversy on that front.

AIA have assigned Marco Guida to this game, which makes sense considering how experienced the 45-year-old referee is. If we look at his record with Italian teams, Milan are actually the side that he has officiated the most, reaching 43 games so far.

Milan have won 20, drawn 11 and lost 12 with Guida as the referee, receiving ten penalties and nine red cards across the 43 games. A pretty good record, especially when you consider that Guida has often been assigned to high-profile games in the last few years.

It will be Guida’s first Milan game of the season, but in 2025-26, he officiated Juventus-Milan (0-0), Milan-Roma (1-0), Lazio-Milan (1-0), Como-Milan (1-3), Lazio-Milan (1-0), Milan-Cagliari (1-2). The last obviously stands out as a really bad one, but that was the Rossoneri’s own doing.

There was a little bit of controversy last season, more specifically in the win against Roma, as Guida kicked Alexis Saelemaekers after the Giallorossi missed a penalty. The incident was quickly forgotten but at the time, it angered Milan a lot.

Manchester United face a Roma team on Tuesday night that has had a blistering, record-breaking start to the Serie A season in terms of goals.

Gian Piero Gasperini’s side won 5-2 at Udinese on Saturday to continue their fine form which sees them unbeaten in 10 games at the start of the Serie A campaign.

In those 10 fixtures they have scored 28 goals, which is more than they had ever previously managed by this stage of the season.

‘Sometimes the numbers do tell you the story,’ he said after the dominant win at Udinese. ‘Besides scoring lots of goals, we’re also scoring with many different players.

‘That shows how much confidence there is in the team: lots of players believe they can make a decisive contribution, be it with an assist or a goal. We’re scoring more goals with more players and that’s a great sign.’

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal fans believe that Piero Hincapie hit back at a subtle past dig from Virgil van Dijk following Arsenal’s win over Liverpool.

The Gunners are celebrating their first Premier League victory at Anfield since September 2012 thanks to Kai Havertz’s first-half goal brilliantly set up by Declan Rice that secured a hard-fought 1-0 success on Merseyside on Sunday.

Afterwards he took to Instagram to post a series of pictures from the match which finished on a zoomed-in image of the golden Premier League badge worn on the shirt sleeves of the defending champions, captioning the slides: “I don’t forget.”

#1828. Arsenal, Liverpool and Man Utd phone £50m midfielder over stunning transfer

Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United have reportedly made contact with Lennart Karl to gauge whether the attacking midfielder would be interested in a move to England.

Karl, 18, broke into Bayern’s first-team squad in early 2025 and has gone on to establish himself as one of the brightest young talents in German football.

In that time, Karl has made a total of 52 appearances in all competitions for Bayern while helping the club win the Bundesliga, the German Cup and the German Super Cup.

However, in a recent interview, Bayern’s honorary president Uli Hoeness questioned Karl’s social media activity and suggested the teenager still had a long way to go before he could be considered a ‘superstar’- raising some doubts over the youngster’s future at the Allianz Arena.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

‘He’s far from being a superstar,’ Hoeness said of Karl.

‘Young players need humility. Comparisons with Michael Olise obviously don’t do him any good.

‘There’s still a world of difference between them.’

According to Bild, Hoeness’ remarks have caused a level of ‘unrest’ within Karl’s camp, and Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United have been alerted to a potential deal.

It’s claimed the three Premier League giants have all made contact with Karl over the phone to discuss the Germany international’s current situation.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The report adds that while it is not Bayern’s intention to force out Karl, an offer in the region of €60million (£50m) from a potential suitor could be enough to prise the diminutive midfielder away from Munich.

Karl’s contract with the reigning Bundesliga champions runs through to June 2029.

Michael Ballack, who represents Karl with the Lucky 13 agency, was less than impressed by Hoeness’ comments, jumping to the defence of his client’s presence on social media.

‘Lennart is only 18. Where were you at 18? Just as he is trying things out on the pitch, he is doing the same off it,’ the former Bayern and Chelsea midfielder told DAZN.

‘Social media is a major factor today, and not just for the younger generation. Everyone is free to present themselves as they wish.

‘Of course, they will not get everything right. Unfortunately, condemnation is inevitable.’

Ballack added: ‘It is legitimate for Uli Hoeness to criticise how Lennart presents himself publicly.

‘But it is also clear that, in doing so, he is making Lennart a public target.’

Karl has started just three of Bayern’s eight matches in the Bundesliga so far this season.

He was sent on in the 84th minute on Saturday as Vincent Kompany’s men were held to a 2-2 draw at home to fierce rivals Borussia Dortmund.

As such, Arsenal are three points clear at the summit with one more Premier League match to play before the season pauses for a fortnight.

Before Arsenal welcome Hull to the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, they travel to Prague to face Slavia Praha as the league phase of this season’s Champions League reaches the halfway point.

Mikel Arteta will have Declan Rice, Noni Madueke and Riccardo Calafiori available for that trip after the trio shook off knocks to start and play the full 90 minutes at Anfield, while Christos Tzolis’ surprise start was a bonus given a rather worrying update on Eberechi Eze.

With that in mind, here is the latest Arsenal injury news and return dates…

Eze had been expected to start against Liverpool after an impressive performance off the bench in the 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich in the Champions League as well as a decent showing. in the win over Everton last weekend.

However, not only was Eze dropped in favour of the returning Tzolis, he remained on the bench throughout.

Speaking after the game, Arteta revealed the England international had been dealing with an injury concern of his own.

“We had an issue with Ebs as well that it was incredible that he was in the squad today,” the Arsenal manager said. “I want to give credit to all the medical and the performance team because what they're doing with those boys is incredible, every three days to keep everybody at this level.

“That’s why these are the margins sometimes where you win a football match and not when you have somebody available or not.”

The fact that Eze was fit enough for the bench suggests his injury is not too serious and should be in contention to face Slavia Praha, though Arteta should provide a further update after Tuesday’s open training session.

Potential return date: Wednesday November 4, vs Slavia Prague (A)

Bukayo Saka has now missed Arsenal's last three games in all competitions with a quad injury sustained after just 10 minutes against Bayern Munich.

He is not expected to feature against either Slavia Prague or Hull before the international break, but fans are still in the dark as to how long he will be sidelined for.
